At threshold 50, the full-sample PMI-below share is 0.306931 and the two-month regime share is 0.207921 (42 months); at 49.5 the regime share is 0.074257 (15 months).\n\n## 4. Q1 Option A: SVI surface\n\n### 4.1 Model\n\nFor each date-expiry slice, with `k = ln(K/F)` and total variance `w = sigma^2 T`, the raw SVI form is\n\n`w(k) = a + b (rho (k-m) + sqrt((k-m)^2 + eta^2))`,\n\nwith `b >= 0`, `|rho| < 1`, `eta > 0`, and bounds `a in [-2,2]`, `b in [0,5]`, `rho in [-0.999,0.999]`, `m in [-2,2]`, `eta in [0.01,1.0]`. The implied volatility is obtained by inverting the Black-76 price with `brentq` on `[1e-4,5]`. Fitting is bounded nonlinear least squares (`scipy.optimize.least_squares`, TRF, `x_scale=\"jac\"`) with equal weights on liquid OTM quotes and eight documented starting points plus an optional warm start. Each raw fit is audited on `k in [-0.14,0.14]` step 0.01 with the correct Gatheral butterfly function\n\n`g(k) = (1 - k w'/(2w))^2 - (w'^2/4)(1/w + 1/4) + w''/2`,\n\nand with the printed form that omits `w''/2`. Calendar arbitrage is checked by linear interpolation of total variance in `T` at fixed `k`, requiring nondecreasing `w`. Violations are repaired by penalized refits at penalty levels `1e2`, `1e4`, `1e6` (butterfly, positive-w and calendar penalties), followed by a forward calendar repair against the previous expiry. Strict counts use `g<0`; tolerance counts use `g<-1e-8`.\n\n### 4.2 Results\n\nTable 2: Q1A SVI results. Source: `results/approach1/io/metrics.json` (settle) and `results/approach1/io_close/metrics.json` (close).\n\n| statistic | settle | close |\n|---|---:|---:|\n| liquid quotes | 18,771 | 18,810 |\n| OTM quotes used | 11,146 | 11,192 |\n| fits / skipped | 693 / 57 | 693 / 57 |\n| butterfly raw, correct strict | 8 | 23 |\n| butterfly raw, printed strict | 382 | 418 |\n| butterfly repaired, correct at 1e-8 | 0 | 0 |\n| butterfly repaired, correct strict | 1 | 3 |\n| butterfly repaired, printed strict | 390 | 423 |\n| calendar raw / repaired at 1e-8 | 29 / 0 | 29 / 0 |\n| calendar repaired strict | 12 | 11 |\n| OTM median of per-fit max repricing | 0.025827 | 0.043298 |\n| OTM p95 of per-fit max repricing | 0.153681 | 0.159755 |\n| OTM median of per-fit median repricing | 0.007745 | 0.012691 |\n| OTM worst per-fit max repricing | 0.325137 | 0.262438 |\n| eta at lower / upper bound | 31 / 67 | 72 / 46 |\n\nThe settle run is the primary result. On the same 693 fits, the legacy eta bounds `[1e-6,2.0]` put 27 fits at the lower bound and 8 at the upper bound; the current bounds put 31 at the lower and 67 at the upper. The median raw RMSE in total variance is 8.466090e-05 under the legacy bounds and 8.467848e-05 under the current bounds, so the bound change barely affects fit error. On close, the corresponding counts are 51/8 legacy and 72/46 current, with median RMSE 1.561191e-04 in both cases.\n\nTable 3: Q1A forward check on matched IO/IF pairs. Source: `results/approach1/io/metrics.json` and `results/approach1/io_close/metrics.json`.\n\n| statistic | settle | close |\n|---|---:|---:|\n| matched / unmatched forwards | 498 / 252 | 498 / 252 |\n| implied q median on matched pairs | 0.047255 | 0.047704 |\n| IF basis median | 0.055471 | 0.052724 |\n| q minus IF basis, median | -0.006650 | -0.006885 |\n| q minus IF basis, mean | -0.009035 | -0.005865 |\n| IF relative deviation median | 0.001635 | 0.001205 |\n| IF relative deviation p95 | 0.005396 | 0.005427 |\n\nFigures: `results/approach1/io/surface.html` and `results/approach1/io/fit_slices.html`; close versions under `results/approach1/io_close/`.\n\n### 4.3 Discussion and limitations\n\nThe settle fit removes all tolerance-level butterfly and calendar violations on the audit grid, but the strict counts (1 butterfly, 12 calendar) show that \"arbitrage-free\" holds only at the numerical tolerance, not exactly. The printed butterfly formula, which omits `w''/2`, records 382 raw strict violations instead of 8 and 390 repaired strict violations instead of 1; the difference is therefore material and the correct form is the one used for decisions. The close run is worse: 23 raw strict butterfly violations and 3 after repair. The median per-fit median repricing is 0.77% on settle and 1.27% on close, but the median per-fit maximum is 2.58% and 4.33%, so some slices have large relative errors, especially in the wings. The forward check shows implied q about 0.7 percentage points below the IF basis on matched pairs; the mean is more negative than the median, consistent with short-dated annualization amplifying small forward differences, but this was not tested as a separate cause.\n\nSVI fits at the eta bounds are common: 98 of 693 settle fits and 118 of 693 close fits sit on a bound. Whether these are genuine optima or optimizer/ill-conditioning effects was not tested. The audit is only on `|k| <= 0.14`; no global arbitrage proof is claimed. The 252 unmatched forwards are likely due to the main-contract IF series, but that is a hypothesis.\n\n## 5. Q1 Option B: neural surface\n\n### 5.1 Model\n\nQ1B uses the same OTM quotes as Q1A on six sample dates (2024-03-14, 2024-09-13, 2025-03-14, 2025-09-15, 2026-03-16, 2026-09-15), giving 30 date-expiry fits and 470 quotes. The selected sample date for 2024-03 is 2024-03-14, one day before the metadata sample date 2024-03-15, because the selection rule takes the date nearest mid-month with at least 80% of that month's maximum quote count. The surface is one MLP across all expiries: inputs `k/0.2` and `sqrt(T)/sqrt(T_max)`, four layers (three hidden layers of 24 units), `tanh` activation, and a softplus output plus `1e-6` for `sigma`. The loss is the mean squared undiscounted OTM call price error per unit forward plus `lambda1 * mean(max(0,-g)^2)` and `lambda2 * mean(max(0,-dw/dT)^2)` on a collocation grid `k in [-0.14,0.14]` crossed with expiry tenors; `g` includes `w''/2`. The whole objective is multiplied by `c = 1 / initial_price_loss`, which leaves the minimizer unchanged. Optimization is 3,000 Adam steps followed by bounded L-BFGS (1,000 iterations, strong Wolfe, 45 s cap). Seeds are derived from date, design and replication but not lambda, so lambda pairs share an initialization.\n\nSelection is pre-declared: complete fit coverage, then zero butterfly and calendar violations at 1e-8 on the Q1A grid, then the lowest pooled in-sample OTM relative repricing median, with ties broken by the smallest `lambda1 + lambda2`. The chosen pair is `lambda1=0.01`, `lambda2=0.0`. The ablation also compares the unpenalized fit and the strong `lambda1=1` fit. Robustness refits on a random 30% holdout (three seeds) and an outer-15% wing holdout, scoring only held-out quotes.\n\n### 5.2 Results\n\nTable 4: Q1B ablation, chosen model, and comparison with Q1A SVI on the same 470 quotes. Source: `results/approach2/io_scaled/metrics.json`.\n\n| model | median | p95 | max | butterfly violations | calendar violations | dense butterfly | dense calendar |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n| unpenalized (0,0) | 0.009106 | 0.131590 | 0.985702 | 3 | 0 | 37 | 4 |\n| chosen (0.01,0) | 0.008687 | 0.123426 | 0.982950 | 0 | 0 | 30 | 4 |\n| lambda1=1, lambda2=0 | 0.009898 | 0.135121 | 0.976978 | 2 | 0 | 32 | 8 |\n| Q1A SVI re-priced | 0.008214 | 0.054525 | 0.173657 | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a |\n\nThe chosen neural surface has 0 butterfly and 0 calendar violations on the Q1A audit grid (`min g = 0.002068`), but 30 butterfly and 4 calendar violations on the dense grid (`k` from -0.20 to 0.20 step 0.005, listed expiries plus midpoints), with `dense_min_g = -0.560331` and `dense_min_forward_variance = -0.005021`. All dense violations are outside the training collocation range `|k| <= 0.14`; this is consistent with extrapolation failure, but the cause was not separately tested. The Q1B variants (torch versus scipy SVI solvers) reached tolerance on 29/30 and 30/30 fits respectively, with median final objectives 6.560190e-09 and 6.558610e-09. From a cold start the counts are Adam 0/30, L-BFGS 14/30 and scipy 30/30, with median final objectives 1.838110e-08, 8.003028e-09 and 6.560122e-09.\n\nTable 5: Q1B robustness on held-out quotes. Source: `results/approach2/io_scaled/metrics.json`.\n\n| design | model | fits | n | median | p95 |\n|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n| random 30% | SVI | 18/18 | 407 | 0.016297 | 0.126115 |\n| random 30% | neural | 18/18 | 407 | 0.018359 | 0.221206 |\n| wing 15% | SVI | 6/6 | 83 | 0.050337 | 0.559186 |\n| wing 15% | neural | 6/6 | 83 | 0.093261 | 0.780917 |\n\nFigures: `results/approach2/io_scaled/surface.html`, `svi_convergence.html` and `svi_convergence_cold.html`.\n\n### 5.3 Discussion and limitations\n\nThe neural surface is close to SVI in median repricing (0.008687 vs 0.008214) but is clearly worse in the tail (p95 0.123426 vs 0.054525; max 0.982950 vs 0.173657) and in the wing holdout (median 0.093261 vs 0.050337; p95 0.780917 vs 0.559186). The dense-grid audit means the surface must not be called globally arbitrage-free. The cold-start comparison shows that scipy is the reliable solver; torch Adam alone does not reach tolerance within 5,000 steps on any of the 30 fits, and L-BFGS reaches 14/30. `results/approach2/io/metrics.json` is superseded, historical and not rerun: it records the earlier optimization failure (median 0.044285, p95 0.678359, max 0.981883) and is kept only for the record. `results/approach2/io_scaled` is the primary Q1B result.\n\n## 6. Q2 Option A: Monte Carlo pricing\n\n### 6.1 Model and estimators\n\nUnder the brief's GBM, `dS_t = r S_t dt + sigma S_t dW_t`, with `S0` the last close, `K=S0`, `T=1`, `m=252`, barrier `B=1.3 S0`, and `r` the SHIBOR zero at `T`. A futures price has zero drift under Q; the brief specifies drift `r`, so the code follows the brief and flags this as a modelling simplification. `sigma` is the standard deviation of daily log returns times `sqrt(252)` on a five-year window. The payoffs are arithmetic Asian `max(mean(S_{t_i})-K,0)`, discretely monitored up-and-out `max(S_T-K,0) * 1{max S_{t_i}<B}`, cash-or-nothing digital `1{S_T>K}`, and European `max(S_T-K,0)`. All are discounted by `exp(-rT)`.\n\nEstimators are naive Monte Carlo, antithetic `(Z,-Z)` at equal path count, a control variate using the discrete geometric Asian closed form with `ln G ~ N(ln S0 + (r-sigma^2/2)T(m+1)/(2m), sigma^2 T (m+1)(2m+1)/(6m^2))`, and control variate plus antithetic. The control-variate beta is estimated on an independent pilot of 100,000 paths so the estimator is unbiased. European and Asian delta/vega use pathwise estimators; digital and barrier use likelihood-ratio estimators because pathwise is invalid at discontinuities. Finite differences use common random numbers and relative bumps `h in {0.1, 0.01, 0.001}` for spot and sigma. European and digital references are closed form; Asian and barrier references are high-precision control-variate estimates (524,288 paths per dataset, 2,097,152 paths in the IF study). The convergence study uses `N = 2^10` to `2^16`, 30 replications and a `2^22` reference.\n\n### 6.2 Results\n\nTable 6: Q2A calibration. Source: `results/approach3/{IF,CU,RB,SC}/metrics.json`.\n\n| dataset | S0 | sigma | sigma MAD | mu (mean) | mu (log regression) | excess kurtosis | max abs log return | tail-return count |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n| IF | 4071.2 | 0.191098 | 0.142589 | -0.036420 | 0.014016 | 10.015837 | 0.105563 | 106 |\n| CU | 106170.0 | 0.170509 | 0.133017 | 0.087975 | 0.099233 | 5.108945 | 0.068486 | 113 |\n| RB | 3008.0 | 0.198571 | 0.153657 | -0.071838 | -0.090793 | 4.062288 | 0.085650 | 131 |\n| SC | 681.6 | 0.419743 | 0.308155 | 0.061017 | -0.026519 | 4.974414 | 0.149239 | 119 |\n\nTable 7: Q2A prices, validation and variance reduction. Source: `results/approach3/{IF,CU,RB,SC}/metrics.json`.\n\n| dataset | European MC (SE) | Black-Scholes | z | Asian CV+anti (SE) | Asian CV ratio | Asian CV+anti ratio | barrier CV+anti ratio | digital antithetic ratio |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n| IF | 337.316332 (1.180383) | 337.789684 | -0.401015 | 192.847635 (0.016534) | 1542.089430 | 1565.271966 | 1.597735 | 31.731202 |\n| CU | 7949.616615 (27.214444) | 7949.508319 | 0.003979 | 4531.584891 (0.342376) | 1973.512115 | 1955.162451 | 1.624006 | 1316.282827 |\n| RB | 258.645324 (0.908093) | 258.412486 | 0.256403 | 147.608358 (0.013055) | 1466.893598 | 1484.538534 | 1.582477 | 24.610853 |\n| SC | 117.723902 (0.487940) | 117.450120 | 0.561096 | 67.664064 (0.014716) | 308.257474 | 312.026020 | 1.162172 | 4.104964 |\n\nAll four European z-scores are within three standard errors. All four Asian variance-reduction factors pass the 5x benchmark; the barrier control-variate ratios are only 1.05 to 1.62 (except CV+anti 1.16 to 1.62), and the digital antithetic ratio ranges from 4.10 to 1316.28. Greek z-scores are mostly within two: the worst is RB barrier vega at z = -2.152789; European and Asian pathwise Greeks and digital likelihood-ratio Greeks are all smaller in absolute value. The IF study's Asian convergence slopes are -0.474494 (naive), -0.516441 (antithetic), -0.507927 (control variate) and -0.460101 (CV+anti), against the -0.5 target. The vectorized engine is 26.371462 times faster than the Python loop on 2,000 paths and 252 monitoring dates.\n\nTable 8: Q2A finite-difference bias and variance. Source: `results/approach3/IF_study/metrics.json`.\n\n| quantity | bump | bias | RMSE |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n| Asian delta | 0.01 | -0.000519 | 0.005674 |\n| European delta | 0.01 | -0.000102 | 0.006252 |\n| barrier vega | 0.1 | -4.254317 | 59.867589 |\n| barrier vega | 0.01 | -10.900933 | 170.018806 |\n| barrier vega | 0.001 | 61.259527 | 670.022692 |\n| digital delta | 0.1 | -0.000022 | 0.000023 |\n| digital delta | 0.01 | 0.000001 | 0.000036 |\n\nFigures: `results/approach3/IF_study/convergence.html` and `results/approach3/IF_study/fd_bias_variance.html`.\n\n### 6.3 Discussion and limitations\n\nThe Asian control variate is very effective, because the geometric Asian is strongly correlated with the arithmetic payoff. The barrier control variate is weak because the geometric Asian does not capture the barrier event well. Digital antithetic works extremely well in some datasets because the payoff is bounded. Finite differences are noisy for discontinuous payoffs: barrier vega RMSE grows from 59.87 at `h=0.1` to 670.02 at `h=0.001`, so smaller bumps do not help. The roll-jump counts in Table 6 (106, 113, 131, 119) are tail-return counts above the reported threshold, not identified roll dates; the main-contract series carry no roll flags. The calibration uses a five-year window and is sensitive to the large returns retained in the sample. The GBM drift is `r` as specified, not the zero drift of a futures price under Q.\n\n## 7. Q2 Option B: deep hedging\n\n### 7.1 Model\n\nThe hedge is a European ATM call on IF with `S0=100`, `K=100`, `T=0.25`, `m=63`, `sigma=0.191098` (the Q2A five-year IF calibration) and `r=0.014172` (SHIBOR zero at `T`). The policy is a small MLP with two hidden layers of 32 units mapping `(S_t/S0, t/T)` to a delta in `[0,1]` through a sigmoid; it does not see the previous position. The objective is empirical CVaR at 0.95 of `-V_T`, the mean of the worst 5% of losses per batch. Training uses `2^17` paths, batches of `2^12`, 100 epochs, Adam at learning rate 0.005, and one policy per cost `kappa in {0,10,50}` bp. The same network initialization is used for every kappa. Validation uses three independent seeds with `2^17` paths each; training uses one seed (42).\n\nThe brief P&L is\n\n`V_T = sum_t exp(r(T-t)) D_t (S_{t+1}-S_t) - kappa sum_t |D_t-D_{t-1}| S_t - payoff`, `D_{-1}=0`, no terminal unwind.\n\nThe self-financing P&L is\n\n`V_T = sum_t exp(r(T-t-dt)) D_t (S_{t+1}-exp(r dt) S_t) - kappa sum_t exp(r(T-t)) |D_t-D_{t-1}| S_t - payoff`.\n\nThe brief formula omits the financing cost of the stock position. Training uses the brief P&L; evaluation reports both. Net CVaR is CVaR minus the future value of the Black-Scholes premium. Benchmarks are Black-Scholes deltas rebalanced every 1, 5 and 21 days at the same kappas, on the same validation paths.\n\n### 7.2 Results\n\nTable 9: Q2B net CVaR (mean over three validation seeds) and turnover. Source: `results/approach4/IF/metrics.json`.\n\n| kappa (bp) | BS 1d brief | BS 1d selffin | BS 5d brief | BS 5d selffin | BS 21d brief | BS 21d selffin | deep brief | deep selffin | deep turnover |\n|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n| 0 | 0.783819 | 0.963441 | 1.885495 | 2.072134 | 4.103734 | 4.299130 | 0.681660 | 0.891035 | 2.847643 |\n| 10 | 1.200644 | 1.383465 | 2.103973 | 2.291344 | 4.214103 | 4.409974 | 0.989419 | 1.178928 | 2.770302 |\n| 50 | 2.974087 | 3.162954 | 3.001208 | 3.190983 | 4.658068 | 4.855765 | 2.085485 | 2.334088 | 2.523439 |\n\nThe deep policy has the lowest net CVaR in all six brief/self-financing cells. At kappa 0 its CVaR is 0.978632 of daily BS on the brief P&L and 0.985404 on self-financing, so it is close to, and slightly better than, the daily BS benchmark. The brief-minus-self-financing CVaR gap is negative everywhere: -0.179622 for BS 1d at kappa 0, -0.209375 for the deep policy at kappa 0, and -0.248603 for the deep policy at kappa 50; the mean across all cells is -0.195962. The negative sign means the brief P&L reports lower CVaR (looks better) than self-financing P&L. Training CVaR falls from 11.012090 to 4.697527 (kappa 0), from 11.078866 to 4.980354 (kappa 10), and from 11.324191 to 6.127673 (kappa 50).\n\nTable 10: Q2B policy sensitivity to kappa. Source: `results/approach4/IF/metrics.json`.\n\n| kappa (bp) | mean abs difference vs BS delta | max abs difference | mean policy delta | std policy delta |\n|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n| 0 | 0.021793 | 0.080426 | 0.504728 | 0.364797 |\n| 10 | 0.028782 | 0.091034 | 0.507294 | 0.358444 |\n| 50 | 0.053032 | 0.118469 | 0.500717 | 0.337109 |\n\nAs the cost rises, the policy moves further from BS delta and reduces turnover from 2.847643 to 2.523439. Figures: `results/approach4/IF/training.html` and `results/approach4/IF/policy.html`.\n\n### 7.3 Discussion and limitations\n\nThe deep hedge improves CVaR over daily BS by about 2% at zero cost and by about 30% at 50 bp on the brief P&L, with lower turnover. The brief-versus-self-financing gap is systematic and is larger for the deep policy at high cost, because the omitted stock financing scales with the position and the position is held through the path. The training used one seed only; three validation seeds reduce evaluation noise but do not establish training robustness. The study covers only IF, uses no terminal unwind cost, and the policy cannot represent a no-trade region because the previous position is not an input. The kappa=0 closeness to daily BS is a sanity check, not evidence that the network recovers the BS delta globally; the mean absolute difference is 0.021793 and the maximum is 0.080426.\n\n## 8. Q3 Option A: classical probit\n\n### 8.1 Model and protocol\n\nThe information set is implemented by shifting each series forward by its lag `L_i`: row `t` contains only values public at the end of month `t`. The label is `d_t = 1{PMI_t < 50 and PMI_{t-1} < 50}`. The model is `P(d_{t+1}=1) = Phi(beta' z_t)`, where `z_t` contains an intercept, the first `r` principal components of the standardized aligned factor panel (excluding `gdp_yoy`, `cgb10y`, `spread_10y_2y`, `shibor_3m`) and the controls `cgb10y` and `spread_10y_2y`. PCA and standardization use only rows public at the origin; missing values become zero after standardization; series with under 50% training-window coverage are dropped. The probit is fitted by maximum likelihood with a ridge of `1e-4` and a Newton/BFGS fallback. Validation is expanding walk-forward, refit monthly, minimum 60 training months, a 36-month tuning block and a test block of 105 origins from 2018-01-31 to 2026-09-30. The PCA rank is chosen on the tuning block by cross-validated nowcast RMSE at month 3 of the quarter.\n\nThe nowcast is `y_q = b0 + b' fbar_q`, where `fbar_q` averages the aligned factors over the months of the quarter elapsed by `t`; training quarters are those with GDP public by `t`. The benchmark is a random walk with drift estimated from the same information set. Clustering uses rolling 36-month correlations, `d_ij = sqrt(2(1-rho_ij))`, Ward linkage, `k` chosen by silhouette, adjacent-window adjusted Rand indices, and lead-lag correlations with GDP.\n\n### 8.2 Results\n\nTable 11: Q3A test-block classification (105 origins, 34 positives, class share 0.323810). Source: `results/approach5/macro/metrics.json`.\n\n| model | Brier | AUC | accuracy |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n| probit | 0.239616 | 0.692833 | 0.638095 |\n| prior | 0.248216 | 0.603977 | 0.676190 |\n| persistence | 0.228571 | 0.739022 | 0.771429 |\n\nThe probit beats the prior on Brier score but loses to persistence on all three metrics. The chosen PCA rank is 6, with tuning CV RMSE 0.356464 over 12 quarterly observations; rank 5 is 0.383800, rank 4 is 0.431288, rank 3 is 0.617467, rank 2 is 0.800650, rank 1 is 0.677408, rank 7 is 0.456430 and rank 8 is 0.527062. The first principal component explains 0.309793 of variance. No slope coefficient is significant at 5% with Newey-West standard errors; the largest are PC1 (`z=-1.892`) and `spread_10y_2y` (`z=-1.678`). The only strongly significant term is the intercept (`z=-8.180`).\n\nTable 12: Q3A label sensitivity and nowcast. Source: `results/approach5/macro/metrics.json`.\n\n| specification | probit Brier | probit AUC | probit accuracy | persistence Brier | persistence AUC | persistence accuracy |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n| threshold 50, two-month (main) | 0.239616 | 0.692833 | 0.638095 | 0.228571 | 0.739022 | 0.771429 |\n| threshold 49.5, two-month | 0.171497 | 0.715856 | 0.771429 | 0.171429 | 0.629121 | 0.828571 |\n| threshold 50, one-month | 0.246817 | 0.662536 | 0.657143 | 0.276190 | 0.721939 | 0.723810 |\n\n| nowcast | month 1 | month 2 | month 3 |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n| bridge RMSE, all quarters (n=35) | 3.625810 | 3.411277 | 3.314429 |\n| random-walk-with-drift RMSE, all quarters | 4.163149 | 4.163149 | 4.163149 |\n| bridge RMSE, ex-COVID (n=27) | 0.709502 | 0.806523 | 0.878438 |\n| random-walk-with-drift RMSE, ex-COVID | 1.257822 | 1.257822 | 1.257822 |\n\nThe bridge beats the random walk overall, including ex-COVID, but the ex-COVID RMSE worsens from month 1 to month 3 (0.709502 to 0.878438). The paired month-3-minus-month-1 difference is 0.168936 with a 95% interval `[-0.107131, 0.439017]`, so the apparent degradation is not statistically resolved. Clustering has 14 rolling windows; the latest window 2023-01-31 to 2025-12-31 selects `k=9` with silhouette 0.267526. Adjacent-window ARI has minimum 0.034839, median 0.164828 and maximum 0.545584, so cluster membership is unstable across windows.\n\nTable 13: Q3A post-hoc probit robustness (test block already seen; not pre-registered). Source: `results/approach5/macro/metrics.json`.\n\n| model | Brier | AUC | accuracy | share of predictions outside [0.01,0.99] |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n| original probit | 0.239616 | 0.692833 | 0.638095 | 0.276190 |\n| ridge-selected probit | 0.218303 | 0.688070 | 0.638095 | 0.180952 |\n| ridge-selected probit with `d_t` | 0.200141 | 0.739022 | 0.704762 | 0.180952 |\n| prior | 0.248216 | 0.603977 | 0.676190 | 0.000000 |\n| persistence | 0.228571 | 0.739022 | 0.771429 | 1.000000 |\n\nThe post-hoc `d_t` extension improves Brier to 0.200141 and matches persistence's AUC exactly (0.739022), but its paired AUC difference is 0.0 with interval `[-0.131584, 0.071344]`, so there is no evidence that it beats persistence. The original probit's AUC difference versus persistence is -0.046189 with interval `[-0.237456, 0.035180]`. Figures: `results/approach5/macro/regime.html`, `nowcast_revision.html`, `dendrogram.html` and `stability.html`.\n\n### 8.3 Discussion and limitations\n\nThe probit has genuine but modest signal against the prior; persistence is stronger because the two-month label is highly persistent and PMI itself is in the information set. The AUC is 0.692833, below the 0.75 indicative target. The rank is chosen on only 12 quarterly nowcast observations, so the rank choice is noisy. The test block is 105 months but only 35 quarters are available for the nowcast, and the AUC bootstrap intervals are wide. The nowcast improvement over the random walk is concentrated in the COVID period; ex-COVID the month-3 RMSE is higher than month-1 even though month 3 uses more aligned data, and the paired interval includes zero. No cause is asserted for that pattern. Clustering is descriptive and unstable, and it is not used for forecasting.\n\n## 9. Q3 Option B: LSTM and leakage\n\n### 9.1 Model and protocol\n\nQ3B uses 12-month windows of the standardized aligned panel, excluding `gdp_yoy`, as input to an LSTM with at most two layers and a linear logit head. Training pairs are `(window ending s, d_{s+1})` with `s+1 <= origin t`. The loss is `BCEWithLogits` with `pos_weight = n_neg/n_pos`, and probabilities are corrected by `p_cal = sigmoid(logit - log(pos_weight))`. The walk-forward scheme is expanding, with the LSTM refit every six months while the Q3A probit refits monthly. The last 18 training-pair months before each refit are held out for early stopping. Hyperparameters are selected on the 36-month tuning block only by mean Brier over three seeds; the chosen setting is hidden 16, one layer, dropout 0.2, with max 300 epochs, patience 30, learning rate 0.001 and weight decay `1e-4`. Leakage arms are the disciplined aligned panel, a zero-lag panel (`L_i=0`), a zero-lag panel with full-sample standardization, and a zero-lag probit. Leakage premiums use a circular 12-month block bootstrap with 5,000 replicates; positive means the leaked arm looks better (lower Brier or higher AUC).\n\n### 9.2 Results\n\nTable 14: Q3B test-block comparison (105 origins, 34 positives). Source: `results/approach6/macro/metrics.json`.\n\n| arm | Brier | AUC | accuracy |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n| probit | 0.239616 | 0.692833 | 0.638095 |\n| LSTM disciplined | 0.260401 | 0.492543 | 0.676190 |\n| LSTM zero lag | 0.254945 | 0.530240 | 0.676190 |\n| LSTM zero lag, full-sample standardization | 0.247648 | 0.615023 | 0.679365 |\n| probit zero lag | 0.233271 | 0.694698 | 0.704762 |\n| prior | 0.248216 | 0.603977 | 0.676190 |\n| persistence | 0.228571 | 0.739022 | 0.771429 |\n\nTable 15: Q3B leakage premiums (positive means leaked arm better). Source: `results/approach6/macro/metrics.json`.\n\n| comparison | Brier premium | 95% interval |\n|---|---:|---:|\n| LSTM zero lag vs disciplined | 0.005666 | [0.000314, 0.013600] |\n| LSTM full-sample standardization vs disciplined | 0.017594 | [0.004511, 0.033008] |\n| LSTM standardization only | 0.011928 | [0.002488, 0.023989] |\n| probit zero lag vs probit | 0.006345 | [-0.019564, 0.032379] |\n\nTable 16: Q3B post-hoc retraining (test block already seen; not pre-registered). Source: `results/approach6/macro/metrics.json`.\n\n| arm | Brier | AUC | accuracy |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n| probit | 0.239616 | 0.692833 | 0.638095 |\n| LSTM disciplined, original | 0.260401 | 0.492543 | 0.676190 |\n| LSTM disciplined, retrained | 0.256110 | 0.642226 | 0.676190 |\n| LSTM zero lag, retrained | 0.256565 | 0.631455 | 0.676190 |\n| LSTM zero lag full-sample, retrained | 0.252233 | 0.613781 | 0.676190 |\n| prior | 0.248216 | 0.603977 | 0.676190 |\n| persistence | 0.228571 | 0.739022 | 0.771429 |\n\nThe retrained LSTM never exceeds 0.5 on the test block. In `results/approach6/macro/post_hoc_predictions.csv`, the disciplined arm has 0 of 105 predictions above 0.5 for each seed; the maxima are 0.176730 (seed 42), 0.317224 (seed 43) and 0.223370 (seed 44). Its accuracy 0.676190 is therefore the all-negative rate. The latent bridge uses correlation vectors between each indicator and the 16 hidden dimensions over 2023-01-31 to 2025-12-31, clusters them with `k=9`, and compares with Q3A's latest indicator labels: ARI 0.412380 and NMI 0.638510. After retraining, ARI is 0.521881 and NMI 0.735385; a 1,000-permutation null gives mean ARI 0.001082, 95th percentile 0.092549 and p=0.000999, with NMI null mean 0.438911 and 95th percentile 0.509250. Figures: `results/approach6/macro/probabilities.html` and `latent.html`.\n\n### 9.3 Discussion and limitations\n\nThe original LSTM is a training/optimization failure relative to the probit: test AUC 0.492543 is essentially random, and its accuracy is the all-negative rate. The post-hoc diagnostics show that the training loop can fit (the shifted-label train AUC reaches 0.996158 and the overfit test reaches 0.989528), so the failure is not a broken loss; the retrained model improves AUC to 0.642226 but still does not beat persistence (0.739022) or the probit (0.692833) on Brier score (0.256110 vs 0.228571 and 0.239616). The leakage premiums are small but positive for the LSTM: zero-lag alignment improves Brier by 0.005666, full-sample standardization by 0.017594, and standardization alone by 0.011928; the probit premium is not resolved (interval includes zero). Because NBS PMI has `L_i=0` in both arms and the label is built from PMI, the measured lag leakage premium is structurally limited. The final LSTM is trained through 2026-09, so it embeds test months in-sample; the latent analysis is descriptive only. The bridge partitions indicators on both sides, but `h_t` is computed from those indicators, so the ARI significance may be partly mechanical; the null test permutes indicator labels against fixed bridge clusters, not the full construction.\n\n## 10. Indicative benchmarks\n\nThe brief text is not present as a file in the repository. The numerical targets below are the explicit targets recorded in the working instructions and `AGENTS.md`; qualitative targets are marked as such. Source: session instructions and the metrics files named in Sections 4-9.\n\n| benchmark | target | reported result | met? |\n|---|---|---:|---|\n| Q1A butterfly, audit grid | zero at 1e-8 | settle 0, close 0 | met |\n| Q1A butterfly, strict | zero | settle 1, close 3 | not met |\n| Q1A calendar, audit grid | zero at 1e-8 | settle 0, close 0 | met |\n| Q1A calendar, strict | zero | settle 12, close 11 | not met |\n| Q1B vs SVI on same quotes | competitive | median 0.008687 vs 0.008214; p95 0.123426 vs 0.054525 | partly met; tail not met |\n| Q2A European MC | within 3 standard errors of BS | max abs z 0.561096 | met |\n| Q2A Asian variance reduction | >= 5x | 308.257474x to 1973.512115x (CV); 312.026020x to 1955.162451x (CV+anti) | met |\n| Q2A convergence slope | approximately -0.5 | -0.474494 to -0.516441 | met |\n| Q2B kappa=0 vs BS daily | close; ratio <= 1.25 per code | 0.978632 brief, 0.985404 self-financing | met |\n| Q2B CVaR at 50 bp | lower than BS daily | deep 2.085485 vs BS 1d 2.974087 brief | met |\n| Q3A AUC | >= 0.75 | 0.692833 | not met |\n| Q3A beat persistence | Brier and AUC better than persistence | Brier 0.239616 vs 0.228571; AUC 0.692833 vs 0.739022 | not met |\n| Q3B beat persistence | Brier and AUC better than persistence | retrained Brier 0.256110 vs 0.228571; AUC 0.642226 vs 0.739022 | not met |\n| Q3 test block only | report test block only | 105 origins, 2018-01-31 to 2026-09-30 | met |\n\n## 11. Differences from the brief\n\n1. **Butterfly formula.** The printed `g(k)` omits `w''/2`; the code uses the correct Gatheral form for decisions and reports both. On settle, raw strict violations are 8 with `w''/2` and 382 without; repaired strict violations are 1 and 390. On close, raw strict counts are 23 and 418; repaired strict counts are 3 and 423. Source: `results/approach1/io/metrics.json`, `results/approach1/io_close/metrics.json`.\n2. **Hedging P&L.** The printed brief P&L omits the financing cost of the stock position, so it is not exactly self-financing. The brief-minus-self-financing CVaR gap is -0.179622 for daily BS at kappa 0 and -0.209375 for the deep policy at kappa 0; the mean across all cells is -0.195962. The negative sign means the brief formula reports lower CVaR than the self-financing formula. Source: `results/approach4/IF/metrics.json`.\n3. **GBM drift.** The brief specifies drift `r`; the code follows the brief. A futures price has zero drift under Q, so this is a modelling simplification, recorded in `params.drift_note`. Source: `results/approach3/IF/metrics.json`.\n4. **No bid-ask data.** Daily CFFEX data have no bid-ask spread, so volume >= 10 stands in for liquidity/spread. On settle this filter removes 8,008 quotes; the full sequential filter removes 11,297. Source: `results/approach1/io/metrics.json`.\n5. **LSTM refit frequency.** Q3B refits the LSTM every six months and reuses the last refit between refits; Q3A refits the probit monthly. Source: `results/approach6/macro/metrics.json`.\n6. **Cluster bridge.** Q3A clusters partition indicators, while the LSTM's month-level `h_t` clusters partition months, so a direct ARI is undefined. The bridge maps each indicator to a correlation vector with the 16 hidden dimensions and clusters those vectors with `k=9`; the resulting ARI (0.412380 original, 0.521881 retrained) may be partly mechanical because `h_t` is computed from those indicators. Source: `results/approach6/macro/metrics.json`.\n7. **SVI eta bounds.** The current bounds are `[0.01,1.0]`, narrower than the legacy `[1e-6,2.0]`. This changes bound hits but not median RMSE materially; it is a documented robustness choice. Source: `results/approach1/io/metrics.json`.\n8. **Q1B sample date.** Q1B uses 2024-03-14, while the metadata sample date is 2024-03-15. The selection rule chooses the nearest mid-month date with at least 80% of the month's maximum quote count. Source: `results/approach2/io_scaled/metrics.json`.\n9. **Q3B inputs.** The LSTM excludes `gdp_yoy` from the 12-month input panel to avoid a mixed-frequency quarterly series; the probit also excludes it from the factors. Source: `results/approach6/macro/metrics.json`.\n10. **Q2B scope.** Only IF is used, with one training seed and no terminal unwind; the brief permits this but it limits generalisation. Source: `results/approach4/IF/metrics.json`.\n\n## 12. Limitations\n\n- SVI and neural fits are audited only on the reported grids. The neural surface has 30 butterfly and 4 calendar violations on the dense grid outside its training collocation, so it must not be called globally arbitrage-free. SVI is not proved arbitrage-free off the audit grid either.\n- Both models are weak in the wings and at short tenors: Q1A settle worst per-fit max repricing is 0.325137 and close is 0.262438; Q1B wing p95 is 0.780917 and max 1.518873, versus SVI 0.559186.\n- SVI fits frequently sit on the eta bounds (31/67 lower/upper on settle; 72/46 on close), and the cause is not established.\n- Main-contract futures series have no roll flags. The fields named `roll_jump` in `metrics.json` are tail-return counts (IF 106, CU 113, RB 131, SC 119), not identified roll dates.\n- Q2B used one training seed, only IF, no terminal unwind cost, and no previous position in the policy inputs; it cannot represent a no-trade region.\n- Macro data are current revised vintages, not real-time vintages. Most publication lags are conservative assumptions, not observed release dates. GDP is derived from cumulative real levels (79 derived quarters; validation maximum absolute difference 0.828623 points).\n- The retrained LSTM never exceeds 0.5 on the test block (maximum 0.317224) and does not beat persistence (Brier 0.256110 vs 0.228571; AUC 0.642226 vs 0.739022). Its accuracy is the all-negative rate.\n- The PCA rank is chosen on 12 quarterly nowcast observations; the test block is short for regime classification, and the AUC intervals are wide (for example, the original probit minus persistence interval is `[-0.237456, 0.035180]`).\n- The Q3 nowcast improvement over the random walk is concentrated in the COVID period; ex-COVID month 3 is worse than month 1, and the paired interval includes zero.\n- The Q3 clustering is unstable across windows (adjacent ARI median 0.164828) and is descriptive only.\n\n## 13. ### 9.3 Discussion and limitations

The original LSTM is a training/optimization failure relative to the probit: test AUC 0.492543 is essentially random, and its accuracy is the all-negative rate. The post-hoc diagnostics show that the training loop can fit (the shifted-label train AUC reaches 0.996158 and the overfit test reaches 0.989528), so the failure is not a broken loss; the retrained model improves AUC to 0.642226 but still does not beat persistence (0.739022) or the probit (0.692833) on Brier score (0.256110 vs 0.228571 and 0.239616). The leakage premiums are small but positive for the LSTM: zero-lag alignment improves Brier by 0.005666, full-sample standardization by 0.017594, and standardization alone by 0.011928; the probit premium is not resolved (interval includes zero). Because NBS PMI has `L_i=0` in both arms and the label is built from PMI, the measured lag leakage premium is structurally limited. The final LSTM is trained through 2026-09, so it embeds test months in-sample; the latent analysis is descriptive only. The bridge partitions indicators on both sides, but `h_t` is computed from those indicators, so the ARI significance may be partly mechanical; the null test permutes indicator labels against fixed bridge clusters, not the full construction.

def matched_q_stats(group: pd.DataFrame, basis_col: str) -> dict:
    matched = group[np.isfinite(group[basis_col].to_numpy(dtype=float))]
    if matched.empty:
        return {
            "n": 0,
            "implied_q_mean": float("nan"),
            "implied_q_median": float("nan"),
            "if_basis_mean": float("nan"),
            "if_basis_median": float("nan"),
            "q_minus_if_basis_mean": float("nan"),
            "q_minus_if_basis_median": float("nan"),
        }
    q = matched.q.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    basis = matched[basis_col].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    diff = q - basis
    return {
        "n": int(len(matched)),
        "implied_q_mean": float(np.mean(q)),
        "implied_q_median": float(np.median(q)),
        "if_basis_mean": float(np.mean(basis)),
        "if_basis_median": float(np.median(basis)),
        "q_minus_if_basis_mean": float(np.mean(diff)),
        "q_minus_if_basis_median": float(np.median(diff)),
    }


def forward_check(forwards: pd.DataFrame, futures: pd.DataFrame, source_stats: dict) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
    obs = forwards[["date", "expiry", "T", "days", "r", "DF", "S0", "F", "q"]].copy()
    obs["month"] = obs.date.dt.strftime("%Y-%m")
    obs["expiry_month"] = obs.expiry.dt.strftime("%Y-%m")
    obs["tenor_bucket"] = obs.days.map(tenor_bucket)
    if futures.empty:
        obs["if_close"] = np.nan
        obs["if_settle"] = np.nan
        obs["contract"] = None
    else:
        obs = obs.merge(
            futures[["date", "fut_expiry_month", "contract", "if_close", "if_settle"]],
            left_on=["date", "expiry_month"],
            right_on=["date", "fut_expiry_month"],
            how="left",
        ).drop(columns=["fut_expiry_month"])
    obs["if_rel_settle"] = (obs.F / obs.if_settle - 1.0).abs()
    obs["if_rel_close"] = (obs.F / obs.if_close - 1.0).abs()
    obs["if_basis_settle"] = np.where(
        (obs.if_settle > 0) & np.isfinite(obs.if_settle),
        obs.r - np.log(obs.if_settle / obs.S0) / obs["T"],
        np.nan,
    )
    obs["if_basis_close"] = np.where(
        (obs.if_close > 0) & np.isfinite(obs.if_close),
        obs.r - np.log(obs.if_close / obs.S0) / obs["T"],
        np.nan,
    )
    obs["q_minus_if_basis_settle"] = obs.q - obs.if_basis_settle
    obs["q_minus_if_basis_close"] = obs.q - obs.if_basis_close

    def dist(values: pd.Series) -> dict:
        arr = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
        arr = arr[np.isfinite(arr)]
        return {
            "n": int(arr.size),
            "median": float(np.median(arr)) if arr.size else float("nan"),
            "p95": float(np.quantile(arr, 0.95)) if arr.size else float("nan"),
            "max": float(np.max(arr)) if arr.size else float("nan"),
        }

    by_month = []
    for month, group in obs.groupby("month", sort=True):
        settle_stats = matched_q_stats(group, "if_basis_settle")
        close_stats = matched_q_stats(group, "if_basis_close")
        by_month.append({
            "month": month,
            "forwards": int(len(group)),
            "matched_settle": settle_stats["n"],
            "matched_close": close_stats["n"],
            "implied_q_median": settle_stats["implied_q_median"],
            "implied_q_matched_median": settle_stats["implied_q_median"],
            "implied_q_all_median": float(group.q.median()),
            "if_basis_settle_median": settle_stats["if_basis_median"],
            "if_basis_close_median": close_stats["if_basis_median"],
            "q_minus_if_basis_settle_mean": settle_stats["q_minus_if_basis_mean"],
            "q_minus_if_basis_settle_median": settle_stats["q_minus_if_basis_median"],
            "q_minus_if_basis_close_mean": close_stats["q_minus_if_basis_mean"],
            "q_minus_if_basis_close_median": close_stats["q_minus_if_basis_median"],

The q-minus-basis median stays between -0.00846 and -0.00413, so the 2026 rise is common to both series rather than a widening of the gap.\")\nadd()\nadd(\"Figures: `results/approach1/io/surface.html` and `results/approach1/io/fit_slices.html`; close versions under `results/approach1/io_close/`.\")\nadd()\nadd(\"### 4.3 Discussion and limitations\")\nadd()\nadd(\"The settle fit removes all tolerance-level butterfly and calendar violations on the audit grid, but the strict counts (1 butterfly, 12 calendar) show that arbitrage-free holds only at numerical tolerance, not exactly. The printed butterfly formula records 382 raw strict violations instead of 8 and 390 repaired strict violations instead of 1, so the omitted `w''/2` term is material. The close run is worse: 23 raw strict butterfly violations and 3 after repair. The median per-fit median repricing is 0.77% on settle and 1.27% on close, but the median per-fit maximum is 2.58% and 4.33%. The forward check shows implied q about 0.60 to 0.85 percentage points below the IF basis on matched pairs; the mean is more negative than the median, which is consistent with short-dated annualization amplifying small forward differences, but this was not tested as a separate cause.\")\nadd()\nadd(\"SVI fits at the eta bounds are common: 98 of 693 settle fits and 118 of 693 close fits sit on a bound. Whether these are genuine optima or optimizer/ill-conditioning effects was not tested. The audit is only on `|k| <= 0.14`; no global arbitrage proof is claimed. The 252 unmatched forwards are explained by the four-contract IF listing and month matching, as stated in Section 3.1.\")\nadd()\nadd(\"## 5. Q1 Option B: neural surface\")\nadd()\nadd(\"### 5.1 Model\")\nadd()\nadd(\"Q1B uses the same OTM quotes as Q1A on six sample dates (2024-03-14, 2024-09-13, 2025-03-14, 2025-09-15, 2026-03-16, 2026-09-15), giving 30 date-expiry fits and 470 quotes. The 2024-03 date is one day before the metadata date 2024-03-15 because the selection rule takes the nearest mid-month date with at least 80% of that month's maximum quote count. The surface is one MLP across all expiries: inputs `k/0.2` and `sqrt(T)/sqrt(T_max)`, four layers (three hidden layers of 24 units), `tanh` activation, and a softplus output plus `1e-6` for `sigma`. The loss is the mean squared undiscounted OTM price per unit forward plus `lambda1 * mean(max(0,-g)^2)` and `lambda2 * mean(max(0,-dw/dT)^2)` on a collocation grid `k in [-0.14,0.14]` crossed with expiry tenors; `g` includes `w''/2`. The whole objective is multiplied by `c = 1 / initial_price_loss`, which leaves the minimizer unchanged. Optimization is 3,000 Adam steps followed by bounded L-BFGS (1,000 iterations, strong Wolfe, 45 s cap). Seeds are derived from date, design and replication but not lambda, so lambda pairs share an initialization.\")\nadd()\nadd(\"Selection is pre-declared: complete fit coverage, then zero butterfly and calendar violations at 1e-8 on the Q1A grid, then the lowest pooled in-sample OTM relative repricing median, with ties broken by the smallest `lambda1 + lambda2`. The chosen pair is `lambda1=0.01`, `lambda2=0.0`.\")\nadd()\nadd(\"### 5.2 Results\")\nadd()\nab = a2[\"metrics\"][\"ablation\"][\"aggregate\"]\nadd(\"Table 8: Q1B 3x3 lambda ablation. The dense-grid audit means the surface must not be called globally arbitrage-free. The cold-start comparison shows that scipy is the reliable solver in this setting; Adam reaches tolerance on 0/30 cold starts at the single setting tested, and L-BFGS on 14/30. `results/approach2/io/metrics.json` is the optimization failure that motivated the fix: median 4.43%, p95 67.84%, max 98.19%, with no penalties. The diagnosis recorded in `NOTES_OPEN_ISSUES.md` is that L-BFGS stopped at 100 iterations and the loss scale was tiny; the fix was whole-objective scaling by `c = 1/initial_price_loss`, shared initialization independent of lambda, 3,000 Adam steps, 1,000 L-BFGS iterations, and 24 units in three hidden layers. The diagnosis was not independently re-tested for this report.\")\nadd()\nadd(\"## 6. Q2 Option A: Monte Carlo pricing\")\nadd()\nadd(\"### 6.1 Model and estimators\")\nadd()\nadd(\"Under the brief's GBM, `dS_t = r S_t dt + sigma S_t dW_t`, with `S0` the last close, `K=S0`, `T=1`, `m=252`, barrier `B=1.3 S0`, and `r` the SHIBOR zero at `T`. A futures price has zero drift under Q; the brief specifies drift `r`, so the code follows the brief and flags this as a modelling simplification. `sigma` is the standard deviation of daily log returns times `sqrt(252)` on a five-year window. The payoffs are arithmetic Asian `max(mean(S_{t_i})-K,0)`, discretely monitored up-and-out `max(S_T-K,0) * 1{max S_{t_i}<B}`, cash-or-nothing digital `1{S_T>K}`, and European `max(S_T-K,0)`. All are discounted by `exp(-rT)`.\")\nadd()\nadd(\"Estimators are naive Monte Carlo, antithetic `(Z,-Z)` at equal path count, a control variate using the discrete geometric Asian closed form with `ln G ~ N(ln S0 + (r-sigma^2/2)T(m+1)/(2m), sigma^2 T (m+1)(2m+1)/(6m^2))`, and control variate plus antithetic. The control-variate beta is estimated on an independent pilot of 100,000 paths so the estimator is unbiased. European and Asian delta/vega use pathwise estimators; digital and barrier use likelihood-ratio estimators because pathwise is invalid at discontinuities. Finite differences use common random numbers and relative bumps `h in {0.1, 0.01, 0.001}` for spot and sigma. European and digital references are closed form; Asian and barrier references are high-precision control-variate estimates (524,288 paths per dataset, 2,097,152 paths in the IF study). The convergence study uses `N = 2^10` to `2^16`, 30 replications and a `2^22` reference.\")\nadd()\nadd(\"### 6.2 Results\")\nadd()\nadd(\"Table 14: Q2A calibration. Source: `results/approach3/{IF,CU,RB,SC}/metrics.json`.\")\nadd()\nrows = []\nfor ds in [\"IF\",\"CU\",\"RB\",\"SC\"]:\n    params = a3[ds][\"params\"]; c = a3[ds][\"metrics\"][\"calibration\"]\n    rows.append([ds, g(params[\"S0\"]), g(c[\"sigma_annualized\"]), g(c[\"sigma_annualized_mad\"]), g(c[\"mu_annualized_mean\"]), g(c[\"mu_annualized_log_regression\"]), g(c[\"excess_kurtosis\"]), g(c[\"max_abs_log_return\"]), g(c[\"roll_jump_count\"])])\nadd(T([\"dataset\",\"S0\",\"sigma\",\"sigma MAD\",\"mu mean\",\"mu log-reg\",\"excess kurtosis\",\"max abs log return\",\"tail-return count\"], rows))\nadd()\nadd(\"Table 15: Q2A prices for every payoff and estimator. Cells are price (standard error), all paths 200,000. Source: `results/approach3/{IF,CU,RB,SC}/metrics.json`.\")\nadd()\nrows = []\nfor ds in [\"IF\",\"CU\",\"RB\",\"SC\"]:\n    for payoff in [\"european\",\"asian\",\"barrier\",\"digital\"]:\n        x = a3[ds][\"metrics\"][\"pricing\"][payoff]\n        cells = []\n        for name in [\"vectorized_naive\",\"antithetic\",\"control_variate\",\"cv_antithetic\"]:\n            est = x[name]\n            cells.append(f\"{g(est['price'])} ({g(est['se'])})\")\n        rows.append([ds, payoff] + cells)\nadd(T([\"dataset\",\"payoff\",\"naive\",\"antithetic\",\"control variate\",\"CV + antithetic\"], rows))\nadd()\nadd(\"Table 16: Q2A both-engine agreement z-scores. Source: `results/approach3/{IF,CU,RB,SC}/metrics.json`.\")\nadd()\nrows = []\nfor ds in [\"IF\",\"CU\",\"RB\",\"SC\"]:\n    pr = a3[ds][\"metrics\"][\"pricing\"]\n    rows.append([ds, g(pr[\"european\"][\"engine_agreement_z\"]), g(pr[\"asian\"][\"engine_agreement_z\"]), g(pr[\"barrier\"][\"engine_agreement_z\"]), g(pr[\"digital\"][\"engine_agreement_z\"])])\nadd(T([\"dataset\",\"European\",\"Asian\",\"barrier\",\"digital\"], rows))\nadd()\nadd(\"Table 17: Q2A Greeks versus reference. Source: `results/approach3/{IF,CU,RB,SC}/metrics.json`.\")\nadd()\nrows = []\nfor ds in [\"IF\",\"CU\",\"RB\",\"SC\"]:\n    gr = a3[ds][\"metrics\"][\"greeks\"]\n    for payoff in [\"european\",\"asian\",\"digital\",\"barrier\"]:\n        d = gr[payoff][\"delta\"]; v = gr[payoff][\"vega\"]\n        rows.append([ds, payoff, g(d[\"value\"]), g(d[\"reference\"]), g(d[\"z\"]), g(v[\"value\"]), g(v[\"reference\"]), g(v[\"z\"])])\nadd(T([\"dataset\",\"payoff\",\"delta\",\"delta ref\",\"delta z\",\"vega\",\"vega ref\",\"vega z\"], rows))\nadd()\nadd(\"Table 18: Q2A full finite-difference bias and variance. Source: `results/approach3/IF_study/metrics.json`.\")\nadd()\nrows = []\nfor greek in [\"delta\",\"vega\"]:\n    for payoff in [\"european\",\"asian\",\"barrier\",\"digital\"]:\n        for bump in [\"0.1\",\"0.01\",\"0.001\"]:\n            x = a3s[\"metrics\"][\"bias_variance\"][\"table\"][greek][payoff][bump]\n            rows.append([payoff, greek, bump, g(x[\"mean\"]), g(x[\"bias\"]), g(x[\"variance\"]), g(x[\"rmse\"]), g(x[\"z\"])])\nadd(T([\"payoff\",\"greek\",\"bump\",\"mean\",\"bias\",\"variance\",\"RMSE\",\"z\"], rows))\nadd()\nadd(\"Table 19: Q2A convergence slopes. Source: `results/approach3/IF_study/metrics.json`.\")\nadd()\nrows = []\nfor payoff in [\"european\",\"asian\",\"barrier\",\"digital\"]:\n    c = a3s[\"metrics\"][\"convergence\"][\"pricing\"][payoff]\n    rows.append([payoff, g(c[\"naive\"][\"slope\"]), g(c[\"antithetic\"][\"slope\"]), g(c[\"control_variate\"][\"slope\"]), g(c[\"cv_antithetic\"][\"slope\"])])\nadd(T([\"payoff\",\"naive\",\"antithetic\",\"control variate\",\"CV + antithetic\"], rows))\nadd()\nadd(\"The complete pricing slope range is -0.4601 to -0.5368. The committed IF study does not contain convergence slopes for Greeks; Greek agreement is reported through the z-scores in Table 17.\")\nadd()\nperf = a3s[\"metrics\"][\"performance\"]\nadd(\"Table 20: Q2A timing. Source: `results/approach3/IF_study/metrics.json`.\")\nadd()\nadd(T([\"paths\",\"monitoring dates\",\"loop seconds\",\"vectorized seconds\",\"speedup\",\"loop paths/s\",\"vectorized paths/s\"], [[g(perf[\"paths\"]), g(perf[\"monitoring_dates\"]), g(perf[\"loop_seconds\"]), g(perf[\"vectorized_seconds\"]), g(perf[\"speedup\"]), g(perf[\"loop_paths_per_second\"]), g(perf[\"vectorized_paths_per_second\"])]]))\nadd()\nadd(\"The line profile excerpt (source: `results/approach3/line_profile.txt`) shows where the loop spends its time:\")\nadd()\nadd(\"```\")\nadd(\"Line #      Hits         Time  Per Hit   % Time  Line Contents\")\nadd(\"   414    126500   32700000.0    258.5     17.9          for j in range(m):\")\nadd(\"   415    126000   49282000.0    391.1     26.9              log_s += drift + vol * z[i, j]\")\nadd(\"   416    126000   33841000.0    268.6     18.5              value = math.exp(log_s)\")\nadd(\"   417    126000   32671000.0    259.3     17.8              sum_s += value\")\nadd(\"   418    126000   30840000.0    244.8     16.8              if value > max_s:\")\nadd(\"```\")\nadd()\nadd(\"The digital antithetic ratio is strongly dataset-dependent. Table 21 reports `r - sigma^2/2` next to the ratio. Source: `results/approach3/{IF,CU,RB,SC}/metrics.json`.\")\nadd()\nrows = []\nfor ds in [\"IF\",\"CU\",\"RB\",\"SC\"]:\n    p = a3[ds][\"params\"]; ratio = a3[ds][\"metrics\"][\"pricing\"][\"digital\"][\"variance_ratio_vs_naive\"][\"antithetic\"]\n    rows.append([ds, g(p[\"r\"] - 0.5*p[\"sigma\"]**2), g(ratio)])\nadd(T([\"dataset\",\"r - sigma^2/2\",\"digital antithetic ratio\"], rows))\nadd()\nadd(\"Hypothesis, supported by the ordering but not proved: for an ATM digital, when `r - sigma^2/2` is near zero, a `Z, -Z` pair almost always has exactly one in-the-money leg, so the pair mean is nearly constant. CU has the value closest to zero and the largest ratio; SC has the most negative value and the smallest ratio. This is an explanation of the ordering, not a tested theorem.\")\nadd()\nadd(\"### 6.3 Discussion and limitations\")\nadd()\nadd(\"The Asian control variate is very effective because the geometric Asian is strongly correlated with the arithmetic payoff. The barrier control variate is weak: control-variate ratios are 1.008 to 1.055, while CV+antithetic ratios are 1.162 to 1.624. Finite differences are noisy for discontinuous payoffs: barrier vega RMSE grows from 59.87 at `h=0.1` to 670.0 at `h=0.001`, so smaller bumps do not help. The roll-jump counts in Table 14 are tail-return counts above the reported threshold, not identified roll dates; the main-contract series carry no roll flags. The calibration uses a five-year window and is sensitive to the large returns retained in the sample. The GBM drift is `r` as specified, not the zero drift of a futures price under Q.\")\nadd()\nadd(\"## 7. Q2 Option B: deep hedging\")\nadd()\nadd(\"### 7.1 Model\")\nadd()\nadd(\"The hedge is a European ATM call on IF with `S0=100`, `K=100`, `T=0.25`, `m=63`, `sigma=0.1911` (the Q2A five-year IF calibration) and `r=0.01417` (SHIBOR zero at `T`). The policy is a small MLP with two hidden layers of 32 units mapping `(S_t/S0, t/T)` to a delta in `[0,1]` through a sigmoid; it does not see the previous position. The objective is empirical CVaR at 0.95 of `-V_T`, the mean of the worst 5% of losses per batch. Training uses `2^17` paths, batches of `2^12`, 100 epochs, Adam at learning rate 0.005, and one policy per cost `kappa in {0,10,50}` bp. The same network initialization is used for every kappa. Validation uses three independent seeds with `2^17` paths each; training uses one seed (42).\")\nadd()\nadd(\"The brief P&L is `V_T = sum_t exp(r(T-t)) D_t (S_{t+1}-S_t) - kappa sum_t |D_t-D_{t-1}| S_t - payoff`, with `D_{-1}=0` and no terminal unwind. The self-financing P&L is `V_T = sum_t exp(r(T-t-dt)) D_t (S_{t+1}-exp(r dt) S_t) - kappa sum_t exp(r(T-t)) |D_t-D_{t-1}| S_t - payoff`. The brief formula omits the financing cost of the stock position. Training uses the brief P&L; evaluation reports both. Net CVaR is CVaR minus the future value of the Black-Scholes premium. Benchmarks are Black-Scholes deltas rebalanced every 1, 5 and 21 days at the same kappas, on the same validation paths.\")\nadd()\nadd(\"### 7.2 Results\")\nadd()\ntbl = a4[\"metrics\"][\"table\"]\nadd(\"Table 22: Q2B full results for every strategy, kappa and P&L definition. Source: `results/approach4/IF/metrics.json`.\")\nadd()\nrows = []\nfor x in tbl:\n    rows.append([x[\"method\"], g(x[\"rebalance_days\"]) if x[\"rebalance_days\"] is not None else \"n/a\", g(x[\"policy_kappa_bp\"]) if x[\"policy_kappa_bp\"] is not None else \"n/a\", x[\"eval_kappa_bp\"], x[\"pnl\"], g(x[\"cvar_mean\"]), g(x[\"net_cvar_mean\"]), g(x[\"variance_mean\"]), g(x[\"mean_pnl_mean\"]), g(x[\"turnover_mean\"])])\nadd(T([\"method\",\"rebalance d\",\"policy kappa bp\",\"eval kappa bp\",\"P&L\",\"CVaR\",\"net CVaR\",\"variance\",\"E[P&L]\",\"turnover\"], rows))\nadd()\ncross = a4[\"metrics\"][\"cross_kappa\"]\nadd(\"Table 23: Q2B 3x3 cross-evaluation. The gap is systematic and is larger for the deep policy at high cost, because the omitted stock financing scales with the position and the position is held through the path. The training used one seed only; three validation seeds reduce evaluation noise but do not establish training robustness. The study covers only IF, uses no terminal unwind cost, and the policy cannot represent a no-trade region because the previous position is not an input.\")\nadd()\nadd(\"## 8. Q3 Option A: classical probit\")\nadd()\nadd(\"### 8.1 Model and protocol\")\nadd()\nadd(\"The information set is implemented by shifting each series forward by its lag `L_i`: row `t` contains only values public at the end of month `t`. The label is `d_t = 1{PMI_t < 50 and PMI_{t-1} < 50}`. The model is `P(d_{t+1}=1) = Phi(beta' z_t)`, where `z_t` contains an intercept, the first `r` principal components of the standardized aligned factor panel (excluding `gdp_yoy`, `cgb10y`, `spread_10y_2y`, `shibor_3m`) and the controls `cgb10y` and `spread_10y_2y`. PCA and standardization use only rows public at the origin; missing values become zero after standardization; series with under 50% training-window coverage are dropped. The probit is fitted by maximum likelihood with a ridge of `1e-4` and a Newton/BFGS fallback. Validation is expanding walk-forward, refit monthly, minimum 60 training months, a 36-month tuning block and a test block of 105 origins from 2018-01-31 to 2026-09-30. The PCA rank is chosen on the tuning block by cross-validated nowcast RMSE at month 3 of the quarter.\")\nadd()\nadd(\"The nowcast is `y_q = b0 + b' fbar_q`, where `fbar_q` averages the aligned factors over the months of the quarter elapsed by `t`; training quarters are those with GDP public by `t`. The benchmark is a random walk with drift estimated from the same information set. Clustering uses rolling 36-month correlations, `d_ij = sqrt(2(1-rho_ij))`, Ward linkage, `k` chosen by silhouette, adjacent-window adjusted Rand indices, and lead-lag correlations with GDP.\")\nadd()\nadd(\"### 8.2 Results\")\nadd()\nadd(\"Table 25: Q3A test-block classification (105 origins, 34 positives, class share 0.3238). The first principal component explains 0.3098 of variance. No slope coefficient is significant at 5% with Newey-West standard errors; the largest are PC1 (`z=-1.892`) and `spread_10y_2y` (`z=-1.678`). The only strongly significant term is the intercept (`z=-8.180`).\")\nadd()\nadd(\"Table 26: Q3A label sensitivity, including the prior. Source: `results/approach5/macro/metrics.json`.\")\nadd()\nrows = []\nfor label, block in [(\"threshold 50, two-month (main)\", \"test\"), (\"threshold 49.5, two-month\", \"threshold_49.5\"), (\"threshold 50, one-month\", \"one_month\")]:\n    x = a5[\"metrics\"][\"probit\"][block]\n    rows.append([label, g(x[\"probit\"][\"Brier\"]), g(x[\"probit\"][\"AUC\"]), g(x[\"probit\"][\"accuracy\"]), g(x[\"prior\"][\"Brier\"]), g(x[\"prior\"][\"AUC\"]), g(x[\"prior\"][\"accuracy\"]), g(x[\"persistence\"][\"Brier\"]), g(x[\"persistence\"][\"AUC\"]), g(x[\"persistence\"][\"accuracy\"])])\nadd(T([\"specification\",\"probit Brier\",\"probit AUC\",\"probit acc\",\"prior Brier\",\"prior AUC\",\"prior acc\",\"persistence Brier\",\"persistence AUC\",\"persistence acc\"], rows))\nadd()\nadd(\"The probit loses to the prior on accuracy at the main threshold (0.6381 vs 0.6762) and at 49.5 (0.7714 vs 0.8667), and on Brier at 49.5 (0.1715 vs 0.1235). The original probit's AUC difference versus persistence is -0.04619 with interval `[-0.2375, 0.03518]`.\")\nadd()\nadd(\"Figures: `results/approach5/macro/regime.html`, `nowcast_revision.html`, `dendrogram.html` and `stability.html`.\")\nadd()\nadd(\"### 8.3 Discussion and limitations\")\nadd()\nadd(\"The probit has genuine but modest signal against the prior; persistence is stronger because the two-month label is highly persistent and PMI itself is in the information set. The AUC is 0.6928, below the 0.75 indicative target. The rank is chosen on only 12 quarterly nowcast observations, so the rank choice is noisy. The test block is 105 months but only 35 quarters are available for the nowcast, and the AUC bootstrap intervals are wide. The nowcast beats the random walk in all periods, including ex-COVID; the month-3 ex-COVID RMSE being higher than month-1 is unexplained and is not attributed to a cause. Clustering is descriptive and unstable, and it is not used for forecasting.\")\nadd()\nadd(\"## 9. Q3 Option B: LSTM and leakage\")\nadd()\nadd(\"### 9.1 Model and protocol\")\nadd()\nadd(\"Q3B uses 12-month windows of the standardized aligned panel, excluding `gdp_yoy`, as input to an LSTM with at most two layers and a linear logit head. Training pairs are `(window ending s, d_{s+1})` with `s+1 <= origin t`. The loss is `BCEWithLogits` with `pos_weight = n_neg/n_pos`, and probabilities are corrected by `p_cal = sigmoid(logit - log(pos_weight))`. The walk-forward scheme is expanding, with the LSTM refit every six months while the Q3A probit refits monthly. Hyperparameters are selected on the 36-month tuning block only by mean Brier over three seeds.\")\nadd()\nadd(\"The original run used 18-month validation blocks. The retrained model, which is the primary Q3B result, uses the chosen setting hidden 8, one layer, dropout 0.2 and weight decay `1e-2`, an expanding split with the last 36 training-pair months held out for validation, minimum 30 epochs, patience 30 and maximum 300 epochs, with three seeds. Leakage arms are the disciplined aligned panel, a zero-lag panel (`L_i=0`), a zero-lag panel with full-sample standardization, and a zero-lag probit. Leakage premiums use a circular 12-month block bootstrap with 5,000 replicates; positive means the leaked arm looks better (lower Brier or higher AUC).\")\nadd()\nadd(\"### 9.2 Results\")\nadd()\nrc = a6[\"metrics\"][\"post_hoc\"][\"retrain\"][\"comparison\"]\nadd(\"Table 34: Q3B primary comparison, retrained LSTM (test block, 105 origins, 34 positives). Source: `results/approach6/macro/metrics.json`.\")\nadd()\nrows = []\nfor arm in [\"probit\",\"lstm_disciplined\",\"lstm_zero_lag\",\"lstm_zero_lag_full_sample\",\"prior\",\"persistence\"]:\n    x = rc[arm]\n    rows.append([arm, g(x[\"Brier_mean\"]), g(x[\"AUC_mean\"]), g(x[\"accuracy_mean\"])])\nadd(T([\"arm\",\"Brier\",\"AUC\",\"accuracy\"], rows))\nadd()\nadd(\"The retrained disciplined LSTM has Brier 0.2561, AUC 0.6422 and accuracy 0.6762; it does not beat persistence (0.2286, 0.7390, 0.7714) or the probit (0.2396, 0.6928, 0.6381) on Brier or AUC. Its accuracy equals the all-negative rate because it never predicts a probability above 0.5 on the test block. In `results/approach6/macro/post_hoc_predictions.csv`, the disciplined arm has 0 of 105 predictions above 0.5 for each seed; the maxima are 0.1767 (seed 42), 0.3172 (seed 43) and 0.2234 (seed 44).\")\nadd()\nlr = a6[\"metrics\"][\"post_hoc\"][\"retrain\"][\"leakage\"][\"retrained\"]\nadd(\"Table 35: Q3B retrained leakage premiums (positive means leaked arm better). Source: `results/approach6/macro/metrics.json`.\")\nadd()\nrows = []\nfor key,label in [(\"lstm_lag_discipline\",\"LSTM zero lag vs disciplined\"),(\"lstm_full_sample_standardisation\",\"LSTM full-sample standardization vs disciplined\"),(\"lstm_standardisation_only\",\"LSTM standardization only\"),(\"probit_lag_discipline\",\"probit zero lag vs probit\")]:\n    x = lr[key]\n    rows.append([label, g(x[\"premium_brier\"]), f\"[{g(x['premium_brier_ci_low'])}, {g(x['premium_brier_ci_high'])}]\", g(x[\"premium_auc\"]), f\"[{g(x['premium_auc_ci_low'])}, {g(x['premium_auc_ci_high'])}]\"])\nadd(T([\"comparison\",\"Brier premium\",\"Brier 95% CI\",\"AUC premium\",\"AUC 95% CI\"], rows))\nadd()\nadd(\"After retraining, the Brier premium is -0.00085 for zero-lag alignment (CI includes zero), 0.00368 for full-sample standardization (CI excludes zero) and 0.00453 for standardization only (CI includes zero); the AUC premiums are 0.00456, -0.00953 and -0.01408, all with intervals including zero. The disciplined and leaked arms are therefore mostly indistinguishable. The larger original premiums came from the original 18-month validation design, which was unreliable: 4 of 24 refits had a single-class validation block, and the tuning AUC was far below the test AUC. The original LSTM is shown as a failed run, not as the primary result.\")\nadd()\norig = a6[\"metrics\"][\"comparison\"]\norigtune = a6[\"metrics\"][\"post_hoc\"][\"retrain\"][\"protocol\"]\nadd(\"Table 36: Q3B original failed run and tuning/test gap. Source: `results/approach6/macro/metrics.json`.\")\nadd()\nadd(T([\"arm\",\"tuning AUC\",\"test AUC\",\"test Brier\",\"test accuracy\"], [\n [\"original LSTM disciplined\",\"0.2677\", g(orig[\"lstm_disciplined\"][\"AUC_mean\"]), g(orig[\"lstm_disciplined\"][\"Brier_mean\"]), g(orig[\"lstm_disciplined\"][\"accuracy_mean\"])],\n [\"retrained LSTM disciplined\",\"0.9146\", g(rc[\"lstm_disciplined\"][\"AUC_mean\"]), g(rc[\"lstm_disciplined\"][\"Brier_mean\"]), g(rc[\"lstm_disciplined\"][\"accuracy_mean\"])],\n]))\nadd()\nadd(\"The original tuning AUC is the chosen setting's seed-mean from `history.tuning` (setting 3); the retrained tuning AUC is the chosen setting's seed-mean from `post_hoc.retrain.tuning_table` (setting 3). The original validation design produced 4 single-class blocks out of 24 refits; the retrained scheme uses 36 validation months and a minimum of 30 epochs.\")\nadd()\nlat = a6[\"metrics\"][\"post_hoc\"][\"retrain\"][\"latent\"]\nnull = lat[\"null\"]\nadd(\"Table 37: Q3B latent bridge and null. Source: `results/approach6/macro/metrics.json`.\")\nadd()\nadd(T([\"quantity\",\"value\"], [\n [\"latest cluster window\", f\"{lat['bridge']['window_start']} to {lat['bridge']['window_end']}\"],\n [\"k\", g(lat[\"bridge\"][\"k\"])],\n [\"indicators\", g(lat[\"bridge\"][\"n_indicators\"])],\n [\"ARI\", g(lat[\"bridge\"][\"ARI\"])],\n [\"NMI\", g(lat[\"bridge\"][\"NMI\"])],\n [\"null ARI mean / p95\", f\"{g(null['null_ARI_mean'])} / {g(null['null_ARI_q95'])}\"],\n [\"null ARI p-value\", g(null[\"null_ARI_p_value\"])],\n [\"null NMI mean / p95\", f\"{g(null['null_NMI_mean'])} / {g(null['null_NMI_q95'])}\"],\n [\"null NMI p-value\", g(null[\"null_NMI_p_value\"])],\n]))\nadd()\nadd(\"The bridge maps each indicator to a correlation vector with the 16 hidden dimensions over 2023-01-31 to 2025-12-31, clusters those vectors with `k=9`, and compares with Q3A's latest indicator labels. Hindsight: `h_t` is computed from those indicators, so the ARI significance may be partly mechanical; the null permutes indicator labels against fixed bridge clusters, not the full construction. The latent analysis is descriptive.\")\nadd()\nadd(\"Figures: `results/approach6/macro/probabilities.html` and `latent.html`.\")\nadd()\nadd(\"### 9.3 Discussion and limitations\")\nadd()\nadd(\"The original LSTM is a failed run: test AUC 0.4925 is essentially random, and its accuracy is the all-negative rate. The diagnostics show that the training loop can fit (shifted-label train AUC 0.9962; overfit test train AUC 0.9895), so the failure is not a broken loss. The retrained model improves test AUC to 0.6422 but still does not beat persistence or the probit on Brier score. The leakage premiums after retraining are small and mostly include zero, so the disciplined and leaked arms are mostly indistinguishable. Because NBS PMI has `L_i=0` in both arms and the label is built from PMI, the measured lag leakage premium is structurally limited. The final LSTM is trained through 2026-09, so it embeds test months in-sample; the latent analysis is descriptive only.\")\nadd()\nadd(\"## 10. Other checks in this report, such as the kappa=0 deep-hedge comparison or the cluster ARI, are my additions and are not brief targets.\")\nadd()\nadd(\"## 11. Differences from the brief\")\nadd()\nadd(\"1. **Butterfly formula.** The printed `g(k)` omits `w''/2`; the code uses the correct Gatheral form for decisions and reports both. On settle, raw strict violations are 8 with `w''/2` and 382 without; repaired strict violations are 1 and 390. On close, raw strict counts are 23 and 418; repaired strict counts are 3 and 423. Source: `results/approach1/io/metrics.json`, `results/approach1/io_close/metrics.json`.\")\nadd(\"2. **Hedging P&L.** The printed brief P&L omits the financing cost of the stock position, so it is not exactly self-financing. The brief-minus-self-financing CVaR gap is -0.1796 for daily BS at kappa 0 and -0.2094 for the deep policy at kappa 0; the mean across all cells is -0.1960. The negative sign means the brief formula reports lower CVaR than the self-financing formula. Source: `results/approach4/IF/metrics.json`.\")\nadd(\"3. **GBM drift.** The brief specifies drift `r`; the code follows the brief. A futures price has zero drift under Q, so this is a modelling simplification, recorded in `params.drift_note`. Source: `results/approach3/IF/metrics.json`.\")\nadd(\"4. **No bid-ask data.** Daily CFFEX data have no bid-ask spread, so volume >= 10 stands in for liquidity/spread. On settle this filter removes 8,008 quotes; the full sequential filter removes 11,297. Source: `results/approach1/io/metrics.json`.\")\nadd(\"5. **LSTM refit frequency.** Q3B refits the LSTM every six months and reuses the last refit between refits; Q3A refits the probit monthly. Source: `results/approach6/macro/metrics.json`.\")\nadd(\"6. **Cluster bridge.** Q3A clusters partition indicators, while the LSTM's month-level `h_t` clusters partition months, so a direct ARI is undefined. The bridge maps each indicator to a correlation vector with the 16 hidden dimensions and clusters those vectors with `k=9`; the resulting ARI may be partly mechanical because `h_t` is computed from those indicators. Source: `results/approach6/macro/metrics.json`.\")\nadd(\"7. **SVI eta bounds.** The current bounds are `[0.01,1.0]`, narrower than the legacy `[1e-6,2.0]`. # Advanced Programming 2026 Project Report

Hao Lu

## 1. Summary

The repository implements Q1, Q2 and Q3 of the Advanced Programming 2026 brief, options A and B of each. Q1 fits an arbitrage-free implied-volatility surface to CFFEX IO options, with SVI slices (Q1A) and a neural surface (Q1B). Q2 prices path-dependent payoffs under GBM by Monte Carlo (Q2A) and learns a CVaR-optimal hedge (Q2B). Q3 forecasts the PMI contraction regime with a classical probit/PCA model (Q3A) and an LSTM with leakage ablations (Q3B).

The results are mixed and are reported plainly. Q1A fits all 693 liquid date-expiry slices on the settle price and reaches zero butterfly and zero calendar violations at the 1e-8 tolerance on its audit grid, but 1 butterfly and 12 calendar checks remain strictly negative after repair. The median per-fit median repricing error is 0.77% on settle and 1.27% on close; the median per-fit maximum is 2.58% and 4.33%. Q1B is close to SVI in median repricing on the same 470 OTM quotes (0.87% vs 0.82%) but much worse in the tail (p95 12.34% vs 5.45%; maximum 98.30% vs 17.37%), and it violates arbitrage on a denser grid outside its training collocation. Q2A passes the Black-Scholes and closed-form checks; the Asian control-variate variance ratio is 308x to 1973x across four futures, above the 5x benchmark. Q2B's deep policy has lower gross and net CVaR than daily Black-Scholes hedging on the brief P&L at zero and at 50 bp cost. Q3A beats the expanding prior on Brier score but not persistence (AUC 0.6928 vs 0.7390), and its nowcast beats a random-walk-with-drift benchmark in all periods, including ex-COVID. Q3B does not beat persistence either; the retrained LSTM never predicts a probability above 0.5 on the test block and its test AUC is 0.6422 versus 0.7390 for persistence.

What was not achieved: Q1B is not globally arbitrage-free and is not competitive with SVI in the wings; Q2B covers only IF and uses one training seed; Q3A and Q3B do not reach the indicative AUC target of 0.75 or beat persistence. The data are daily, without bid-ask quotes or real-time macro vintages.

## 2. Environment and one-command reproduction

The project uses Python 3.13 under `uv` with pinned dependencies. From the repository root:

```bash
uv sync --python 3.13
source .venv/bin/activate
./reproduce.sh --quick   # tests + compare only
./reproduce.sh           # offline data check, tests, all approaches, post-hoc scripts, compare
python code/check_reproduction.py
```

`./reproduce.sh` runs `data/fetch.py --offline`, all tests, approach1 through approach6 including post-hoc scripts, and `compare.py`. The offline check verifies the nine committed clean artifacts against `data/metadata.json` and reports that all checksums match. The test suite ran 33 tests and passed.

The clean-clone check (`python code/check_reproduction.py`) compares `.cache/clean_clone_full/results` with the committed results. The cached clone predates three post-run commits: the `io_close` refresh, the Q3B `origin_date` label fix, and the Q1B cold-start addition. Each was checked separately: the refreshed `io_close` results match 6,972 numeric values exactly; the label fix was checked by parsed-JSON before/after comparison and no metric changed; the cold-start block was checked by two temporary runs with identical numbers excluding timings. The current checker reports 36,982 compared numeric values, all 36,982 exact, with maximum absolute and relative differences 0. It excludes `results/approach2/io/metrics.json` as historical, not rerun. The checker exits `FAIL` only because of key sets: `results/approach2/io_scaled/metrics.json` has 74 numeric keys only in the committed run (the cold-start block), and `results/approach6/macro/metrics.json` has 216 numeric keys only in the reproduced run (`history.refits[*].min_epochs` config echoes). There are zero numeric differences among shared keys.

The sum of committed `fit_seconds` is 4,668.2 s; excluding the historical Q1B run it is 3,869.8 s, about 64.5 minutes.

### 3.2 Q1 filtering, parity and implied volatility

Q1 uses the CFFEX `settle` field as the primary price and repeats the pipeline on `close`. There is no bid-ask snapshot, so liquidity is proxied by volume. Filters are volume >= 10, price >= 1, `|k| <= 0.20` and days-to-expiry >= 7. On settle, sequential removals are 8,008 by volume, 1,303 by price, 1,380 by strike band and 606 by days, leaving 18,771 liquid quotes. There are 750 date-expiry groups, 728 with liquid quotes, 693 fits and 57 skipped groups (34 with fewer than six strikes, 23 with no liquid OTM quote). The OTM quote set has 11,146 quotes. Rate convention is `r(tau) = ln(1 + L/100 * tau * 365/360) / tau` from SHIBOR, linear in tenor and flat outside pillars. The forward is a volume-weighted mean of `F_K = K + (C-P)/DF` within `|ln(F_K / median(F_K))| <= 0.05`; `q = r - ln(F/S0)/T`.

### 3.3 Q3 panel, lags and revisions

The macro panel has 202 month-end observations and 34 series. Publication lags follow `F_t = {x_{i,s}: s + L_i <= t}`. Thirteen series have `L_i = 0` (market rates, yields, PMI and market-based series); twenty-one have `L_i = 1` (CPI, PPI, money, credit, trade, activity, GDP and similar). Most lags are conservative assumptions because the raw interfaces carry no genuine release date; lag zero is definitional only for market rates and yields. Jin10 announcement-date interfaces were saved but mostly stop in 2025 and are not used for the panel, except `macro_china_gdp_yearly` as a cross-check. GDP is derived from cumulative real levels and the current revised vintage: 79 quarters derived, 59 validation quarters, maximum absolute difference 0.83 percentage points and mean absolute difference 0.17 points. The data are the current revised vintage, not real-time vintages.

January and February are missing for: `retail_yoy` (Jan/Feb missing share 0.8824), `industrial_production_yoy` (Jan 1.000, Feb 0.7059), `fai_ytd_yoy` (Jan 1.000, Feb 0.1765), `electricity_yoy` (Jan 0.9412, Feb 0.000) and `industrial_profit_yoy` (Jan 1.000, Feb 0.000). These values are left missing rather than imputed.

Largest missing shares are `gdp_yoy` 0.6683, `lpr_5y` 0.5693, `unemployment` 0.4802, `tsf_12m_yoy` 0.4406 and `shibor_3m` 0.4257. At threshold 50, the full-sample PMI-below share is 0.3069 and the two-month regime share is 0.2079 (42 months); at 49.5 the regime share is 0.0743 (15 months).

## 4. Q1 Option A: SVI surface

### 4.1 Model

For each date-expiry slice, with `k = ln(K/F)` and total variance `w = sigma^2 T`, the raw SVI form is `w(k) = a + b (rho (k-m) + sqrt((k-m)^2 + eta^2))`, with `b >= 0`, `|rho| < 1`, `eta > 0`, and bounds `a in [-2,2]`, `b in [0,5]`, `rho in [-0.999,0.999]`, `m in [-2,2]`, `eta in [0.01,1.0]`. Implied volatility is obtained by inverting the Black-76 price with `brentq` on `[1e-4,5]`. Fitting is bounded nonlinear least squares (`scipy.optimize.least_squares`, TRF, `x_scale="jac"`) with equal weights on liquid OTM quotes and eight documented starting points plus an optional warm start. Each raw fit is audited on `k in [-0.14,0.14]` step 0.01 with the correct Gatheral butterfly function `g(k) = (1 - k w'/(2w))^2 - (w'^2/4)(1/w + 1/4) + w''/2`, and with the printed form that omits `w''/2`. Calendar arbitrage is checked by linear interpolation of total variance in `T` at fixed `k`, requiring nondecreasing `w`. Violations are repaired by penalized refits at levels `1e2`, `1e4`, `1e6`, followed by a forward calendar repair against the previous expiry. Strict counts use `g<0`; tolerance counts use `g<-1e-8`.
