The settle fit removes all tolerance-level butterfly and calendar violations on the audit grid, but the strict counts (1 butterfly, 12 calendar) show that arbitrage-free holds only at numerical tolerance, not exactly. The printed butterfly formula records 382 raw strict violations instead of 8 and 390 repaired strict violations instead of 1, so the omitted `w''/2` term is material. The close run is worse: 23 raw strict butterfly violations and 3 after repair. The median per-fit median repricing is 0.77% on settle and 1.27% on close, but the median per-fit maximum is 2.58% and 4.33%. The forward check shows implied q about 0.60 to 0.85 percentage points below the IF basis on matched pairs; the mean is more negative than the median, which is consistent with short-dated annualization amplifying small forward differences, but this was not tested as a separate cause.

SVI fits at the eta bounds are common: 98 of 693 settle fits and 118 of 693 close fits sit on a bound. Whether these are genuine optima or optimizer/ill-conditioning effects was not tested. The audit is only on `|k| <= 0.14`; no global arbitrage proof is claimed. The 252 unmatched forwards are explained by the four-contract IF listing and month matching, as stated in Section 3.1.

## 5. Q1 Option B: neural surface

### 5.1 Model

Q1B uses the same OTM quotes as Q1A on six sample dates (2024-03-14, 2024-09-13, 2025-03-14, 2025-09-15, 2026-03-16, 2026-09-15), giving 30 date-expiry fits and 470 quotes. The 2024-03 date is one day before the metadata date 2024-03-15 because the selection rule takes the nearest mid-month date with at least 80% of that month's maximum quote count. The surface is one MLP across all expiries: inputs `k/0.2` and `sqrt(T)/sqrt(T_max)`, four layers (three hidden layers of 24 units), `tanh` activation, and a softplus output plus `1e-6` for `sigma`. The loss is the mean squared undiscounted OTM price per unit forward plus `lambda1 * mean(max(0,-g)^2)` and `lambda2 * mean(max(0,-dw/dT)^2)` on a collocation grid `k in [-0.14,0.14]` crossed with expiry tenors; `g` includes `w''/2`. The whole objective is multiplied by `c = 1 / initial_price_loss`, which leaves the minimizer unchanged. Optimization is 3,000 Adam steps followed by bounded L-BFGS (1,000 iterations, strong Wolfe, 45 s cap). Seeds are derived from date, design and replication but not lambda, so lambda pairs share an initialization.

Selection is pre-declared: complete fit coverage, then zero butterfly and calendar violations at 1e-8 on the Q1A grid, then the lowest pooled in-sample OTM relative repricing median, with ties broken by the smallest `lambda1 + lambda2`. The chosen pair is `lambda1=0.01`, `lambda2=0.0`.

### 5.3 Discussion and limitations

The neural surface is close to SVI in median repricing but worse in the tail and in the wing holdout. The dense-grid audit means the surface must not be called globally arbitrage-free. The cold-start comparison shows that scipy is the reliable solver in this setting; Adam reaches tolerance on 0/30 cold starts at the single setting tested, and L-BFGS on 14/30. `results/approach2/io/metrics.json` is the optimization failure that motivated the fix: median 4.43%, p95 67.84%, max 98.19%, with no penalties. The diagnosis recorded in `NOTES_OPEN_ISSUES.md` is that L-BFGS stopped at 100 iterations and the loss scale was tiny; the fix was whole-objective scaling by `c = 1/initial_price_loss`, shared initialization independent of lambda, 3,000 Adam steps, 1,000 L-BFGS iterations, and 24 units in three hidden layers. The diagnosis was not independently re-tested for this report.

## 6. Q2 Option A: Monte Carlo pricing

### 6.1 Model and estimators
---Q2B---
The Asian control variate is very effective because the geometric Asian is strongly correlated with the arithmetic payoff. The barrier control variate is weak: control-variate ratios are 1.008 to 1.055, while CV+antithetic ratios are 1.162 to 1.624. Finite differences are noisy for discontinuous payoffs: barrier vega RMSE grows from 59.87 at `h=0.1` to 670.0 at `h=0.001`, so smaller bumps do not help. The roll-jump counts in Table 14 are tail-return counts above the reported threshold, not identified roll dates; the main-contract series carry no roll flags. The calibration uses a five-year window and is sensitive to the large returns retained in the sample. The GBM drift is `r` as specified, not the zero drift of a futures price under Q.

## 7. Q2 Option B: deep hedging

### 7.1 Model

The hedge is a European ATM call on IF with `S0=100`, `K=100`, `T=0.25`, `m=63`, `sigma=0.1911` (the Q2A five-year IF calibration) and `r=0.01417` (SHIBOR zero at `T`). The policy is a small MLP with two hidden layers of 32 units mapping `(S_t/S0, t/T)` to a delta in `[0,1]` through a sigmoid; it does not see the previous position. The objective is empirical CVaR at 0.95 of `-V_T`, the mean of the worst 5% of losses per batch. Training uses `2^17` paths, batches of `2^12`, 100 epochs, Adam at learning rate 0.005, and one policy per cost `kappa in {0,10,50}` bp. The same network initialization is used for every kappa. Validation uses three independent seeds with `2^17` paths each; training uses one seed (42).

The brief P&L is `V_T = sum_t exp(r(T-t)) D_t (S_{t+1}-S_t) - kappa sum_t |D_t-D_{t-1}| S_t - payoff`, with `D_{-1}=0` and no terminal unwind. The self-financing P&L is `V_T = sum_t exp(r(T-t-dt)) D_t (S_{t+1}-exp(r dt) S_t) - kappa sum_t exp(r(T-t)) |D_t-D_{t-1}| S_t - payoff`. The brief formula omits the financing cost of the stock position. Training uses the brief P&L; evaluation reports both. Net CVaR is CVaR minus the future value of the Black-Scholes premium. Benchmarks are Black-Scholes deltas rebalanced every 1, 5 and 21 days at the same kappas, on the same validation paths.

The deep policy has higher variance than daily BS at kappa 0 (0.2323 vs 0.1815 brief; 0.2370 vs 0.1733 self-financing) and lower variance at kappa 50 (0.3018 vs 0.4371 brief; 0.3178 vs 0.4273 self-financing). Figures: `results/approach4/IF/training.html` and `results/approach4/IF/policy.html`.

### 7.3 Discussion and limitations

The deep hedge improves CVaR over daily BS on the brief basis at all three costs, with lower turnover at higher cost. The gap is systematic and is larger for the deep policy at high cost, because the omitted stock financing scales with the position and the position is held through the path. The training used one seed only; three validation seeds reduce evaluation noise but do not establish training robustness. The study covers only IF, uses no terminal unwind cost, and the policy cannot represent a no-trade region because the previous position is not an input.
---Q3B---
The probit has genuine but modest signal against the prior; persistence is stronger because the two-month label is highly persistent and PMI itself is in the information set. The AUC is 0.6928, below the 0.75 indicative target. The rank is chosen on only 12 quarterly nowcast observations, so the rank choice is noisy. The test block is 105 months but only 35 quarters are available for the nowcast, and the AUC bootstrap intervals are wide. The nowcast beats the random walk in all periods, including ex-COVID; the month-3 ex-COVID RMSE being higher than month-1 is unexplained and is not attributed to a cause. Clustering is descriptive and unstable, and it is not used for forecasting.

## 9. Q3 Option B: LSTM and leakage

### 9.1 Model and protocol

Q3B uses 12-month windows of the standardized aligned panel, excluding `gdp_yoy`, as input to an LSTM with at most two layers and a linear logit head. Training pairs are `(window ending s, d_{s+1})` with `s+1 <= origin t`. The loss is `BCEWithLogits` with `pos_weight = n_neg/n_pos`, and probabilities are corrected by `p_cal = sigmoid(logit - log(pos_weight))`. The walk-forward scheme is expanding, with the LSTM refit every six months while the Q3A probit refits monthly. Hyperparameters are selected on the 36-month tuning block only by mean Brier over three seeds.

The original run used 18-month validation blocks. The retrained model, which is the primary Q3B result, uses the chosen setting hidden 8, one layer, dropout 0.2 and weight decay `1e-2`, an expanding split with the last 36 training-pair months held out for validation, minimum 30 epochs, patience 30 and maximum 300 epochs, with three seeds. Leakage arms are the disciplined aligned panel, a zero-lag panel (`L_i=0`), a zero-lag panel with full-sample standardization, and a zero-lag probit. Leakage premiums use a circular 12-month block bootstrap with 5,000 replicates; positive means the leaked arm looks better (lower Brier or higher AUC).

### 9.3 Discussion and limitations

The original LSTM is a failed run: test AUC 0.4925 is essentially random, and its accuracy is the all-negative rate. The diagnostics show that the training loop can fit (shifted-label train AUC 0.9962; overfit test train AUC 0.9895), so the failure is not a broken loss. The retrained model improves test AUC to 0.6422 but still does not beat persistence or the probit on Brier score. The leakage premiums after retraining are small and mostly include zero, so the disciplined and leaked arms are mostly indistinguishable. Because NBS PMI has `L_i=0` in both arms and the label is built from PMI, the measured lag leakage premium is structurally limited. The final LSTM is trained through 2026-09, so it embeds test months in-sample; the latent analysis is descriptive only.

The original LSTM is a failed run: test AUC 0.4925 is essentially random, and its accuracy is the all-negative rate. The diagnostics show that the training loop can fit (shifted-label train AUC 0.9962; overfit test train AUC 0.9895), so the failure is not a broken loss. The final LSTM is trained through 2026-09, so it embeds test months in-sample; the latent analysis is descriptive only.

The deep hedge improves CVaR over daily BS on the brief basis at all three costs, with lower turnover at higher cost. The gap is systematic and is larger for the deep policy at high cost. ### 9.3 Discussion and limitations

The original LSTM is a failed run: test AUC 0.4925 is essentially random, and its accuracy is the all-negative rate. The diagnostics show that the training loop can fit (shifted-label train AUC 0.9962; overfit test train AUC 0.9895), so the failure is not a broken loss. The retrained model improves test AUC to 0.6422 but still does not beat persistence or the probit on Brier score. The leakage premiums after retraining are small and mostly include zero, so the disciplined and leaked arms are mostly indistinguishable. Because NBS PMI has `L_i=0` in both arms and the label is built from PMI, the measured lag leakage premium is structurally limited. The final LSTM is trained through 2026-09, so it embeds test months in-sample; the latent analysis is descriptive only.

        log.error("metadata missing: %s", METADATA)
        return 1
    metadata = json.loads(METADATA.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    artifacts = metadata.get("artifacts", {})
    if not artifacts:
        log.error("metadata contains no artifacts")
        return 1
    failed = []
    for relative, info in artifacts.items():
        path = ROOT / relative
        if not path.exists():
            log.error("OFFLINE missing %s", relative)
            failed.append(relative)
            continue
        actual = sha256(path)
        expected = info.get("sha256")
        if actual != expected:
            log.error("OFFLINE checksum mismatch %s expected=%s actual=%s", relative, expected, actual)
            failed.append(relative)
        else:
            log.info("OFFLINE OK %s rows=%s sha256=%s", relative, info.get("rows"), actual)
    if failed:
        return 1
    log.info("offline verification complete; all checksums match")
    return 0


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Fetch Q1 option, index and rates data")
    group = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
    group.add_argument("--online", action="store_true", help="download missing raw data and rebuild clean artifacts")
    group.add_argument("--offline", action="store_true", help="verify clean artifacts against metadata checksums")
    group.add_argument("--futures", action="store_true", help="fetch or refresh only the Q2 futures snapshots")
    group.add_argument("--q3-fetch", action="store_true", help="fetch only the Q3 macro raw snapshots")
    group.add_argument("--q3", action="store_true", help="fetch and build the Q3 macro panel and metadata")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s")
    if args.online:
        return online()
    if args.offline:
        return offline()
    if args.q3_fetch:
        fetch_q3_raw()
        return 0
    if args.q3:
        return q3_run()
    return futures_only()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

    return log_path

def _read_q3_raw(name: str) -> pd.DataFrame | None:
    path = Q3_DIR / f"{name}.csv"
    if not path.exists() or path.stat().st_size == 0:
        return None
    return pd.read_csv(path, dtype=str)


def _period_month(value) -> pd.Period | None:
    if value is None or (isinstance(value, float) and pd.isna(value)):
        return None
    match = re.search(r"(\d{4})年(\d{1,2})月", str(value))

"""Verification tests for the Q2B deep-hedging module."""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import math
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import torch

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
MODULE_PATH = ROOT / "code" / "approach4_q2b_deephedge.py"
SPEC = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("approach4_q2b_deephedge", MODULE_PATH)
assert SPEC is not None and SPEC.loader is not None
Q2B = importlib.util.module_from_spec(SPEC)
SPEC.loader.exec_module(Q2B)

S0 = 100.0
K = 100.0
R = 0.03
SIGMA = 0.20
T = 0.25
M = 63


class TestDeepHedgeQ2B(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_empirical_cvar_matches_manual(self):
        losses = np.arange(1, 101, dtype=float)
        manual = float(np.mean(np.sort(losses)[-5:]))
        self.assertAlmostEqual(Q2B.empirical_cvar(losses, 0.95), manual, places=12)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(Q2B.empirical_cvar(losses, 0.95), 98.0, places=12)

        uneven = np.arange(37, dtype=float) ** 2
        k = math.ceil(0.10 * len(uneven))
        manual_uneven = float(np.mean(np.sort(uneven)[-k:]))
        self.assertAlmostEqual(Q2B.empirical_cvar(uneven, 0.90), manual_uneven, places=12)

        tensor = torch.tensor(losses, dtype=torch.float64)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(
            float(Q2B.empirical_cvar_torch(tensor, 0.95)), manual, places=12
        )

    def test_hand_computed_brief_and_selffin_pnl(self):
        S = np.array([100.0, 101.0, 99.0])
        deltas = np.array([0.6, 0.4])
        kappa = 0.001
        r = 0.02
        m = 2
        dt = T / m
        payoff = max(S[-1] - K, 0.0)

        disc_brief = np.array([math.exp(r * (T - 0.0)), math.exp(r * (T - dt))])
        gains_brief = float(
            np.sum(disc_brief * deltas * np.diff(S))
        )
        cost_brief = kappa * (
            abs(deltas[0] - 0.0) * S[0] + abs(deltas[1] - deltas[0]) * S[1]
        )
        expected_brief = gains_brief - cost_brief - payoff

        disc_selffin = np.array(
            [math.exp(r * (T - dt)), math.exp(r * (T - 2.0 * dt))]
        )
        gains_selffin = float(
            np.sum(disc_selffin * deltas * (S[1:] - math.exp(r * dt) * S[:-1]))
        )
        cost_selffin = kappa * (
            math.exp(r * T) * abs(deltas[0] - 0.0) * S[0]
            + math.exp(r * (T - dt)) * abs(deltas[1] - deltas[0]) * S[1]
        )
        expected_selffin = gains_selffin - cost_selffin - payoff

        self.assertAlmostEqual(
            Q2B.pnl_brief(S, deltas, kappa, r, T, K), expected_brief, places=12
        )
        self.assertAlmostEqual(
            Q2B.pnl_selffin(S, deltas, kappa, r, T, K), expected_selffin, places=12
        )

    def test_bs_daily_selffin_mean_zero_and_std_decreases(self):
        rng = np.random.default_rng(2026)
        n = 80_000
        S = Q2B.gbm_paths(rng, S0, R, SIGMA, T, M, n)
        premium, _ = Q2B.bs_call_price_delta(S0, K, R, SIGMA, T)
        premium_fv = premium * math.exp(R * T)
        stds = {}
        for rebalance_days in (21, 5, 1):
            deltas = Q2B.bs_delta_path(S, K, R, SIGMA, T, M, rebalance_days)
            pnl = Q2B.pnl_selffin(S, deltas, 0.0, R, T, K)
            hedged = pnl + premium_fv
            mean = float(np.mean(hedged))
            se = float(np.std(hedged, ddof=1) / math.sqrt(n))
            self.assertLess(abs(mean), 5.0 * se)
            stds[rebalance_days] = float(np.std(pnl, ddof=1))
        self.assertLess(stds[1], stds[5])
        self.assertLess(stds[5], stds[21])

    def test_constant_policy_reproduces_expected_pnl(self):
        delta_value = 0.37
        kappa = 0.001
        r = 0.02
        m = 2
        policy = Q2B.make_constant_policy(delta_value)
        S = np.array([[100.0, 101.0, 99.0], [100.0, 98.0, 102.0]])
        deltas = Q2B.policy_deltas(policy, S, S0, T, m)
        np.testing.assert_allclose(deltas, delta_value, atol=1e-6, rtol=0.0)

        dt = T / m
        disc_brief = np.array([math.exp(r * (T - 0.0)), math.exp(r * (T - dt))])
        disc_selffin = np.array(
            [math.exp(r * (T - dt)), math.exp(r * (T - 2.0 * dt))]
        )
        payoff = np.maximum(S[:, -1] - K, 0.0)
        expected_brief = (
            delta_value * np.sum(disc_brief * np.diff(S, axis=1), axis=1)
            - kappa * delta_value * S[:, 0]
            - payoff
        )
        expected_selffin = (
            delta_value
            * np.sum(disc_selffin * (S[:, 1:] - math.exp(r * dt) * S[:, :-1]), axis=1)
            - kappa * math.exp(r * T) * delta_value * S[:, 0]
            - payoff
        )
        np.testing.assert_allclose(
            Q2B.pnl_brief(S, deltas, kappa, r, T, K), expected_brief, atol=1e-5, rtol=0.0
        )
        np.testing.assert_allclose(
            Q2B.pnl_selffin(S, deltas, kappa, r, T, K), expected_selffin, atol=1e-5, rtol=0.0
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main(verbosity=2)

"""Verification tests for the Q2A Monte Carlo engine and estimators."""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import math
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from scipy.integrate import quad
from scipy.stats import norm

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
MODULE_PATH = ROOT / "code" / "approach3_q2a_mc.py"
SPEC = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("approach3_q2a_mc", MODULE_PATH)
assert SPEC is not None and SPEC.loader is not None
Q2A = importlib.util.module_from_spec(SPEC)
SPEC.loader.exec_module(Q2A)

S0 = 100.0
K = 100.0
R = 0.03
SIGMA = 0.2
T = 1.0
M = 252
B = 1.3 * S0


def zscore(value: float, se: float, reference: float) -> float:
    return (value - reference) / se


class TestQ2AMonteCarlo(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_gbm_moments(self):
        rng = np.random.default_rng(2026)
        n = 120_000
        z = rng.standard_normal((n, M))
        stats = Q2A.stats_chunk(z, S0, K, R, SIGMA, T, M, B)
        log_return = np.log(stats["ST"] / S0)
        expected_mean = (R - 0.5 * SIGMA * SIGMA) * T
        expected_var = SIGMA * SIGMA * T
        mean = float(np.mean(log_return))
        se_mean = float(np.std(log_return, ddof=1) / math.sqrt(n))
        variance = float(np.var(log_return, ddof=1))
        se_var = float(np.sqrt(2.0 / (n - 1)) * variance)
        self.assertLess(abs(zscore(mean, se_mean, expected_mean)), 4.0)
        self.assertLess(abs(zscore(variance, se_var, expected_var)), 4.0)
        expected_st = S0 * math.exp(R * T)
        se_st = float(np.std(stats["ST"], ddof=1) / math.sqrt(n))
        self.assertLess(abs(zscore(float(np.mean(stats["ST"])), se_st, expected_st)), 4.0)

    def test_geometric_closed_form_against_numerical_integration(self):
        closed = Q2A.geometric_call_closed(S0, K, R, SIGMA, T, M)
        mean_log = closed["mean_log"]
        sqrt_var = math.sqrt(closed["var_log"])
        df = math.exp(-R * T)

        def payoff(z):
            G = math.exp(mean_log + sqrt_var * z)
            return max(G - K, 0.0) * norm.pdf(z)

        integral, _ = quad(payoff, -10.0, 10.0, limit=200)
        price = df * integral
        self.assertLess(abs(price - closed["price"]), 1e-8)
        mean_integral, _ = quad(
            lambda z: math.exp(mean_log + sqrt_var * z) * norm.pdf(z), -10.0, 10.0, limit=200
        )
        self.assertLess(abs(mean_integral - closed["mean_G"]), 1e-8)

    def test_geometric_closed_form_against_mc(self):
        rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
        n = 120_000
        z = rng.standard_normal((n, M))
        stats = Q2A.stats_chunk(z, S0, K, R, SIGMA, T, M, B)
        closed = Q2A.geometric_call_closed(S0, K, R, SIGMA, T, M)
        df = math.exp(-R * T)
        price = df * float(np.mean(stats["geometric_call"]))
        se = df * float(np.std(stats["geometric_call"], ddof=1) / math.sqrt(n))
        self.assertLess(abs(zscore(price, se, closed["price"])), 4.0)
        mean_g = float(np.mean(stats["G"]))
        se_g = float(np.std(stats["G"], ddof=1) / math.sqrt(n))
        self.assertLess(abs(zscore(mean_g, se_g, closed["mean_G"])), 4.0)

    def test_pathwise_european_delta_vega_against_closed_form(self):
        rng = np.random.default_rng(11)
        n = 120_000
        z = rng.standard_normal((n, M))
        stats = Q2A.stats_chunk(z, S0, K, R, SIGMA, T, M, B)
        closed = Q2A.bs_call(S0, K, R, SIGMA, T)
        delta = float(np.mean(stats["european_pw_delta"]))
        delta_se = float(np.std(stats["european_pw_delta"], ddof=1) / math.sqrt(n))
        vega = float(np.mean(stats["european_pw_vega"]))
        vega_se = float(np.std(stats["european_pw_vega"], ddof=1) / math.sqrt(n))
        self.assertLess(abs(zscore(delta, delta_se, closed["delta"])), 4.0)
        self.assertLess(abs(zscore(vega, vega_se, closed["vega"])), 4.0)

    def test_digital_likelihood_ratio_against_closed_form(self):
        rng = np.random.default_rng(13)
        n = 120_000
        z = rng.standard_normal((n, M))
        stats = Q2A.stats_chunk(z, S0, K, R, SIGMA, T, M, B)
        closed = Q2A.digital_call(S0, K, R, SIGMA, T)
        delta = float(np.mean(stats["digital_lr_delta"]))
        delta_se = float(np.std(stats["digital_lr_delta"], ddof=1) / math.sqrt(n))
        vega = float(np.mean(stats["digital_lr_vega"]))
        vega_se = float(np.std(stats["digital_lr_vega"], ddof=1) / math.sqrt(n))
        self.assertLess(abs(zscore(delta, delta_se, closed["delta"])), 4.0)
        self.assertLess(abs(zscore(vega, vega_se, closed["vega"])), 4.0)
        price = math.exp(-R * T) * float(np.mean(stats["digital_call"]))
        price_se = math.exp(-R * T) * float(np.std(stats["digital_call"], ddof=1) / math.sqrt(n))
        self.assertLess(abs(zscore(price, price_se, closed["price"])), 4.0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main(verbosity=2)

"""Verification tests for the Q1B differentiable SVI and neural surface."""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import math
import unittest
import unittest.mock
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import torch

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
MODULE_PATH = ROOT / "code" / "approach2_q1b_neural.py"
SPEC = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("approach2_q1b_neural", MODULE_PATH)
assert SPEC is not None and SPEC.loader is not None
Q1B = importlib.util.module_from_spec(SPEC)
SPEC.loader.exec_module(Q1B)
A1 = Q1B.A1

torch.set_num_threads(1)
torch.manual_seed(0)

TRUE_PARAMS = np.array([-0.005, 0.15, -0.40, -0.03, 0.12])
TRUE_F = 4000.0
TRUE_R = 0.02
TRUE_T = 0.50


class TestNeuralQ1B(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_autograd_w_and_dwdT_match_finite_differences(self):
        k = np.linspace(-0.12, 0.12, 9)
        params = np.array([0.02, 0.12, -0.45, -0.02, 0.14])
        model = Q1B.TorchSVI(params)
        k_tensor = torch.tensor(k, dtype=torch.float64, requires_grad=True)
        w, w1, _, _ = Q1B.torch_svi_g(k_tensor, model)
        w1_auto = torch.autograd.grad(w.sum(), k_tensor, create_graph=True)[0]
        w2_auto = torch.autograd.grad(w1_auto.sum(), k_tensor)[0]

        h = 1e-5
        w_plus = A1.svi_w(k + h, params)
        w_minus = A1.svi_w(k - h, params)
        w1_fd = (w_plus - w_minus) / (2.0 * h)
        w2_fd = (w_plus - 2.0 * A1.svi_w(k, params) + w_minus) / (h * h)
        np.testing.assert_allclose(w1_auto.detach().numpy(), w1_fd, rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-8)
        np.testing.assert_allclose(w2_auto.detach().numpy(), w2_fd, rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-7)

        network = Q1B.IVSurface(hidden=12, hidden_layers=2)
        k_point = torch.tensor(k, dtype=torch.float64, requires_grad=True)
        T_point = torch.tensor(np.linspace(0.08, 1.1, len(k)), dtype=torch.float64, requires_grad=True)
        t_scale = math.sqrt(1.1)
        sigma = network(k_point, T_point, t_scale)
        w_network = sigma * sigma * T_point
        w_k_auto = torch.autograd.grad(w_network.sum(), k_point, create_graph=True)[0]
        w_T_auto = torch.autograd.grad(w_network.sum(), T_point, create_graph=True)[0]

        h_k = 1e-5
        with torch.no_grad():
            w_k_plus = network(k_point + h_k, T_point, t_scale) ** 2 * T_point
            w_k_minus = network(k_point - h_k, T_point, t_scale) ** 2 * T_point
            w_T_plus = network(k_point, T_point + h_k, t_scale) ** 2 * (T_point + h_k)
            w_T_minus = network(k_point, T_point - h_k, t_scale) ** 2 * (T_point - h_k)
        w_k_fd = (w_k_plus - w_k_minus) / (2.0 * h_k)
        w_T_fd = (w_T_plus - w_T_minus) / (2.0 * h_k)
        np.testing.assert_allclose(w_k_auto.detach().numpy(), w_k_fd.numpy(), rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-8)
        np.testing.assert_allclose(w_T_auto.detach().numpy(), w_T_fd.numpy(), rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-8)

    def test_torch_g_matches_approach1_analytic_g(self):
        k = np.linspace(-0.14, 0.14, 29)
        model = Q1B.TorchSVI(TRUE_PARAMS)
        k_tensor = torch.tensor(k, dtype=torch.float64)
        _, _, _, g_torch = Q1B.torch_svi_g(k_tensor, model)
        _, _, _, g_analytic, _ = A1.svi_g(k, TRUE_PARAMS)
        np.testing.assert_allclose(g_torch.detach().numpy(), g_analytic, rtol=1e-9, atol=1e-10)

    def test_torch_price_matches_approach1_black(self):
        DF = math.exp(-TRUE_R * TRUE_T)
        cases = [
            ("C", 1.0, 0.90, TRUE_T, DF, 0.22),
            ("C", 1.0, 1.00, TRUE_T, DF, 0.18),
            ("C", 1.0, 1.15, TRUE_T, DF, 0.31),
            ("P", 1.0, 0.85, TRUE_T, DF, 0.27),
            ("P", 1.0, 1.00, TRUE_T, DF, 0.18),
            ("P", 1.0, 1.20, TRUE_T, DF, 0.35),
            ("C", 4000.0, 3800.0, 0.08, 0.999, 0.15),
            ("P", 4000.0, 4300.0, 1.50, 0.970, 0.25),
        ]
        for cp, F, K, T, DF, sigma in cases:
            expected = A1.bs_price(cp, F, K, T, DF, sigma)
            got = float(Q1B.bs_price_torch(cp, F, K, T, DF, sigma))
            self.assertLess(abs(got - expected), 1e-10, msg=f"{cp} F={F} K={K} T={T}")

    def test_torch_svi_recovers_known_parameters(self):
        k = np.linspace(-0.25, 0.25, 81)
        w = A1.svi_w(k, TRUE_PARAMS)
        x0 = np.array([-0.010, 0.14, -0.42, -0.02, 0.13])
        fit = Q1B.fit_svi_torch(
            k, w, x0,
            adam_steps=30000,
            lbfgs_steps=500,
            lr=0.03,
            seed=42,
        )
        self.assertLess(fit["objective"], 1e-14)
        for name, true, got in zip(("a", "b", "rho", "m", "eta"), TRUE_PARAMS, fit["params"]):
            self.assertLess(abs(got - true), 1e-5, msg=f"{name}: true={true} got={got}")

    def test_positive_scaling_preserves_quadratic_minimizer(self):
        target = torch.tensor([1.25, -0.75], dtype=torch.float64)

        def fit(scale: float) -> np.ndarray:
            x = torch.zeros(2, dtype=torch.float64, requires_grad=True)
            optimizer = torch.optim.LBFGS(
                [x],
                lr=1.0,
                max_iter=50,
                tolerance_grad=1e-12,
                tolerance_change=1e-14,
                line_search_fn="strong_wolfe",
            )

            def closure() -> torch.Tensor:
                optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
                loss = scale * ((x - target) ** 2).sum()
                loss.backward()
                return loss

            optimizer.step(closure)
            return x.detach().numpy().copy()

        np.testing.assert_allclose(fit(1.0), fit(9.0), atol=1e-8)

    def test_neural_loss_scaling_is_a_constant_multiple(self):
        torch.manual_seed(7)
        model = Q1B.IVSurface(hidden=4, hidden_layers=1)
        k = torch.tensor([-0.10, 0.0, 0.10], dtype=torch.float64)
        T = torch.tensor([0.10, 0.20, 0.50], dtype=torch.float64)
        unit = torch.tensor([0.01, 0.02, 0.03], dtype=torch.float64)
        colloc_k = torch.tensor(
            np.tile(np.linspace(Q1B.COLLOC_K_START, Q1B.COLLOC_K_STOP, 5), 3),
            dtype=torch.float64,
        )
        colloc_T = torch.tensor(
            np.repeat(np.array([0.10, 0.20, 0.50]), 5),
            dtype=torch.float64,
        )

        def evaluate(scale: float):
            model.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            total, price, butterfly, calendar = Q1B.neural_loss(
                model, k, T, unit, colloc_k, colloc_T,
                math.sqrt(0.50), 0.3, 0.2, scale=scale,
            )
            total.backward()
            gradients = [param.grad.detach().clone() for param in model.parameters()]
            return float(total.detach()), price, butterfly, calendar, gradients

        total_a, price_a, butterfly_a, calendar_a, gradients_a = evaluate(1.0)
        total_b, price_b, butterfly_b, calendar_b, gradients_b = evaluate(4.0)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(total_b, 4.0 * total_a, places=12)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(price_b, price_a, places=15)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(butterfly_b, butterfly_a, places=15)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(calendar_b, calendar_a, places=15)
        for grad_a, grad_b in zip(gradients_a, gradients_b):
            np.testing.assert_allclose(grad_b.numpy(), 4.0 * grad_a.numpy(), rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-15)

    def test_lambda_pairs_share_one_initialization(self):
        date = pd.Timestamp("2025-09-15")
        records = []
        for expiry, expiry_T in (("2025-10-17", 0.08), ("2025-11-21", 0.18)):
            for k in (-0.10, 0.10):
                records.append({

        otm = pd.DataFrame(records)

        def fake_fit(group, fit_args, lambda1, lambda2, seed, design, rep, *rest, **kwargs):
            captured.append((float(lambda1), float(lambda2), int(seed)))

            Q1B.run_ablation(

"""Leakage, alignment, probit, RMSE and AUC tests for Q3 Option A."""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import sys
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from scipy.special import ndtr
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
MODULE_PATH = ROOT / "code" / "approach5_q3a_classical.py"
SPEC = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("approach5_q3a_classical", MODULE_PATH)
assert SPEC is not None and SPEC.loader is not None
Q3A = importlib.util.module_from_spec(SPEC)
sys.modules[SPEC.name] = Q3A
SPEC.loader.exec_module(Q3A)

PANEL = ROOT / "data" / "clean" / "macro_panel.csv"
META = ROOT / "data" / "clean" / "macro_meta.csv"


class TestQ3ALeakage(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.raw, cls.meta, cls.lags, cls.series = Q3A.load_inputs(PANEL, META)
        cls.cfg = Q3A.RunConfig()
        cls.origin = 120
        cls.rank = 3

    def test_alignment_shifts_by_lag(self):
        aligned = Q3A.align_information_set(self.raw, self.lags)
        for name in ("pmi", "gdp_yoy", "cgb10y"):
            lag = self.lags[name]
            left = aligned[name].iloc[50]
            right = self.raw[name].iloc[50 - lag]
            if np.isnan(left) or np.isnan(right):
                self.assertTrue(np.isnan(left) and np.isnan(right))
            else:
                self.assertEqual(left, right)
        lag = self.lags["gdp_yoy"]
        self.assertTrue(np.isnan(aligned["gdp_yoy"].iloc[lag - 1]))

    def test_future_values_cannot_change_z_or_probability(self):
        baseline = Q3A.predict_at_origin(
            self.raw, self.meta, self.origin, self.cfg, self.rank
        )
        mutated = self.raw.copy()
        for name in self.series:
            lag = self.lags[name]
            rows = np.arange(len(mutated))
            future = rows + lag > self.origin
            mutated.loc[future, name] = 1e9
        perturbed = Q3A.predict_at_origin(
            mutated, self.meta, self.origin, self.cfg, self.rank
        )
        np.testing.assert_array_equal(baseline["z_t"], perturbed["z_t"])
        self.assertEqual(baseline["probability"], perturbed["probability"])

    def test_training_labels_never_exceed_origin(self):
        result = Q3A.predict_at_origin(
            self.raw, self.meta, self.origin, self.cfg, self.rank
        )
        self.assertLessEqual(int(np.max(result["train_target_idx"])), self.origin)
        self.assertLessEqual(int(np.max(result["train_feature_idx"])), self.origin - 1)


class TestQ3AEstimators(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_probit_recovers_simulated_coefficients(self):
        rng = np.random.default_rng(2026)
        n = 6000
        x = np.column_stack(
            [np.ones(n), rng.normal(size=(n, 3))]
        )
        beta = np.array([-0.3, 0.8, -0.5, 0.4])
        y = (rng.random(n) < ndtr(x @ beta)).astype(float)
        fit = Q3A.fit_probit(x, y, ridge=1e-6)
        self.assertTrue(fit["converged"])
        self.assertLess(float(np.max(np.abs(fit["beta"] - beta))), 0.15)
        se = Q3A.probit_standard_errors(x, y, fit["beta"], nw_lag=4)
        self.assertTrue(np.all(np.isfinite(se["info_se"])))
        self.assertTrue(np.all(se["info_se"] > 0.0))
        self.assertTrue(np.all(np.isfinite(se["nw_se"])))
        self.assertTrue(np.all(se["nw_se"] > 0.0))

    def test_rmse(self):
        self.assertAlmostEqual(Q3A.rmse([1.0, 2.0, 3.0], [1.0, 4.0, 3.0]), np.sqrt(4.0 / 3.0))
        self.assertEqual(Q3A.rmse([1.0, np.nan], [1.0, 2.0]), 0.0)

    def test_auc_matches_sklearn_with_ties(self):
        y = np.array([0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1])
        p = np.array([0.1, 0.4, 0.35, 0.8, 0.2, 0.35])
        expected = roc_auc_score(y, p)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(Q3A.auc_score(y, p), expected, places=12)
        y2 = np.array([0, 1, 0, 1])
        p2 = np.array([0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5])
        self.assertAlmostEqual(Q3A.auc_score(y2, p2), 0.5, places=12)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util

import unittest
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

sys.modules[Q3A_SPEC.name] = Q3A
Q3A_SPEC.loader.exec_module(Q3A)

Q3B_SPEC = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
    "approach6_q3b_sequence", CODE / "approach6_q3b_sequence.py"
)
assert Q3B_SPEC is not None and Q3B_SPEC.loader is not None
Q3B = importlib.util.module_from_spec(Q3B_SPEC)
sys.modules[Q3B_SPEC.name] = Q3B
Q3B_SPEC.loader.exec_module(Q3B)

PANEL = ROOT / "data" / "clean" / "macro_panel.csv"
META = ROOT / "data" / "clean" / "macro_meta.csv"


def synthetic_panel(months: int = 200) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray]:
    rng = np.random.default_rng(2026)
    dates = pd.date_range("2000-01-31", periods=months, freq="ME")
    state = np.zeros(months)
    for index in range(1, months):
        state[index] = 0.8 * state[index - 1] + rng.normal(scale=0.6)
    pmi = 50.0 + 3.0 * state + rng.normal(scale=1.0, size=months)
    aligned = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "date": dates,
            "pmi": pmi,
            "signal": state + rng.normal(scale=0.1, size=months),
            "noise": rng.normal(size=months),
            "other": rng.normal(size=months),
        }
    )
    label = Q3A.build_label(aligned, 50.0, "two_month")
    return aligned, label


class TestQ3BLeakage(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.raw, cls.meta, cls.lags, cls.series = Q3A.load_inputs(PANEL, META)
        cls.aligned = Q3A.align_information_set(cls.raw, cls.lags)
        cls.cfg = Q3A.RunConfig()
        cls.origin = 120
        cls.window = 12

    def test_windows_at_origin_ignore_future_values(self):
        fit_idx = np.arange(0, self.origin + 1)
        means, stds, columns = Q3B.fit_feature_scaler(self.aligned, fit_idx, 0.5)
        baseline = Q3B.standardised_window(
            self.aligned, self.origin, self.window, columns, means, stds
        )
        mutated = self.raw.copy()
        rows = np.arange(len(mutated))
        for name in self.series:
            lag = self.lags[name]
            future = rows + lag > self.origin
            mutated.loc[future, name] = 1e9
        aligned_mutated = Q3A.align_information_set(mutated, self.lags)
        means_m, stds_m, columns_m = Q3B.fit_feature_scaler(aligned_mutated, fit_idx, 0.5)
        self.assertEqual(columns, columns_m)
        np.testing.assert_array_equal(means, means_m)
        np.testing.assert_array_equal(stds, stds_m)
        perturbed = Q3B.standardised_window(
            aligned_mutated, self.origin, self.window, columns_m, means_m, stds_m
        )
        np.testing.assert_array_equal(baseline, perturbed)

    def test_training_labels_never_exceed_origin(self):
        d = Q3A.build_label(self.aligned, 50.0, "two_month")
        ends = Q3B.training_pair_ends(self.origin, d, self.window)
        self.assertGreater(len(ends), 0)
        self.assertLessEqual(int(np.max(ends + 1)), self.origin)
        self.assertLessEqual(int(np.max(ends)), self.origin - 1)


class TestQ3BCalibration(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_hand_computed_odds_correction(self):
        self.assertAlmostEqual(Q3B.calibrate_probability(0.8, 4.0), 0.5, places=12)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(Q3B.calibrate_probability(0.5, 2.0), 1.0 / 3.0, places=12)
        raw = 0.8
        weight = 4.0
        odds_weighted = raw / (1.0 - raw)
        expected = odds_weighted / weight / (1.0 + odds_weighted / weight)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(Q3B.calibrate_probability(raw, weight), expected, places=12)
        logit = np.log(raw / (1.0 - raw))
        self.assertAlmostEqual(Q3B.calibrate_logit(logit, weight), 0.5, places=12)

    def test_pos_weight_uses_only_training_labels(self):
        weight, n_pos, n_neg = Q3B.positive_weight(np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0]))
        self.assertAlmostEqual(weight, 3.0, places=12)
        self.assertEqual((n_pos, n_neg), (1, 3))


class TestQ3BSignal(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_lstm_beats_prior_on_synthetic_signal(self):
        aligned, label = synthetic_panel()
        cfg = Q3A.RunConfig(seed=42, min_train=80, tuning_months=40, min_coverage=0.5)
        args = Q3B.parse_args([])
        args.max_epochs = 200
        args.patience = 40
        args.lr = 5e-3
        origins = np.arange(80, len(aligned) - 1)
        hp = {"hidden": 8, "layers": 1, "dropout": 0.0}
        run = Q3B.run_lstm_walk(
            aligned, label, origins, cfg, 42, hp, args, "synthetic", log=None
        )
        test = run["frame"][run["frame"]["block"] == "test"]
        lstm_brier = float(np.mean((test["p"] - test["y_true"]) ** 2))
        prior = np.array(
            [np.nanmean(label[1 : int(origin) + 1]) for origin in test["origin_index"]]
        )
        prior_brier = float(np.mean((prior - test["y_true"].to_numpy()) ** 2))
        self.assertLess(lstm_brier, prior_brier - 0.01)
        self.assertLess(lstm_brier, 0.20)

    def test_min_epochs_blocks_early_stopping(self):
        aligned, label = synthetic_panel()
        means, stds, columns = Q3B.fit_feature_scaler(aligned, np.arange(0, 121), 0.5)
        data = Q3B.build_training_arrays(
            aligned, label, 120, 12, 18, columns, means, stds
        )
        args = Q3B.parse_args([])
        args.max_epochs = 40
        args.patience = 1
        args.min_epochs = 10
        hp = {"hidden": 8, "layers": 1, "dropout": 0.2}
        _, info = Q3B.train_lstm(
            data["X_train"], data["y_train"], data["X_val"], data["y_val"], hp, 7, args
        )
        self.assertGreaterEqual(info["epochs_run"], 10)
        self.assertEqual(info["min_epochs"], 10)

    def test_same_seed_same_result(self):
        aligned, label = synthetic_panel()
        cfg = Q3A.RunConfig(seed=42, min_train=80, tuning_months=0, min_coverage=0.5)
        means, stds, columns = Q3B.fit_feature_scaler(aligned, np.arange(0, 121), 0.5)
        data = Q3B.build_training_arrays(
            aligned, label, 120, 12, 18, columns, means, stds
        )
        args = Q3B.parse_args([])
        args.max_epochs = 40
        args.patience = 20
        hp = {"hidden": 8, "layers": 1, "dropout": 0.2}
        model_a, _ = Q3B.train_lstm(
            data["X_train"], data["y_train"], data["X_val"], data["y_val"], hp, 7, args
        )
        model_b, _ = Q3B.train_lstm(
            data["X_train"], data["y_train"], data["X_val"], data["y_val"], hp, 7, args
        )
        window = Q3B.standardised_window(aligned, 120, 12, columns, means, stds)
        p_a, raw_a, h_a = Q3B.predict_lstm(model_a, window[None], 2.0)
        p_b, raw_b, h_b = Q3B.predict_lstm(model_b, window[None], 2.0)
        np.testing.assert_array_equal(p_a, p_b)
        np.testing.assert_array_equal(raw_a, raw_b)
        np.testing.assert_array_equal(h_a, h_b)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Synthetic recovery checks for the Q1A SVI pipeline."""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import math
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

MODULE_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "code" / "approach1_q1a_svi.py"
SPEC = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("approach1_q1a_svi", MODULE_PATH)
assert SPEC is not None and SPEC.loader is not None
SVI = importlib.util.module_from_spec(SPEC)
SPEC.loader.exec_module(SVI)

TRUE_PARAMS = np.array([-0.005, 0.15, -0.40, -0.03, 0.12])
TRUE_F = 4000.0
TRUE_R = 0.02
TRUE_T = 0.25


def synthetic_chain(noise: float = 0.0, seed: int = 42):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    DF = math.exp(-TRUE_R * TRUE_T)
    S0 = TRUE_F * DF
    k = np.round(np.linspace(-0.20, 0.20, 41), 12)
    K = TRUE_F * np.exp(k)
    w = SVI.svi_w(k, TRUE_PARAMS)
    iv = np.sqrt(w / TRUE_T)
    C = np.array([SVI.bs_price("C", TRUE_F, strike, TRUE_T, DF, vol) for strike, vol in zip(K, iv)])
    P = np.array([SVI.bs_price("P", TRUE_F, strike, TRUE_T, DF, vol) for strike, vol in zip(K, iv)])
    if noise:
        C = C * (1.0 + noise * rng.standard_normal(len(C)))
        P = P * (1.0 + noise * rng.standard_normal(len(P)))
    vols = np.full_like(C, 100.0)
    return k, K, C, P, vols, DF, S0, w


class TestSVIRecovery(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_forward_recovery_within_ten_basis_points(self):
        k, K, C, P, vols, DF, S0, _ = synthetic_chain(noise=1e-6)
        estimate = SVI.estimate_forward_pair(K, C, P, vols, vols, DF, S0, TRUE_R, TRUE_T)
        self.assertLess(abs(estimate["F"] / TRUE_F - 1.0), 1e-3)
        self.assertGreaterEqual(estimate["in_band"].sum(), len(K) - 1)

    def test_svi_parameter_recovery_within_five_percent(self):
        k, K, C, P, vols, DF, S0, w = synthetic_chain()
        estimate = SVI.estimate_forward_pair(K, C, P, vols, vols, DF, S0, TRUE_R, TRUE_T)
        self.assertLess(abs(estimate["F"] / TRUE_F - 1.0), 1e-3)
        fit = SVI.fit_svi(k, w)
        self.assertIsNotNone(fit)
        params = fit["params"]
        for name, true, got in zip(("a", "b", "rho", "m", "eta"), TRUE_PARAMS, params):
            scale = max(abs(true), 1e-3)
            self.assertLess(abs(got - true) / scale, 0.05, msg=f"{name}: true={true} got={got}")
        self.assertLess(fit["rmse"], 1e-10)

    def test_analytic_g_matches_finite_difference(self):
        k = np.linspace(-0.13, 0.13, 11)
        h = 1e-5
        w = SVI.svi_w(k, TRUE_PARAMS)
        w_plus = SVI.svi_w(k + h, TRUE_PARAMS)
        w_minus = SVI.svi_w(k - h, TRUE_PARAMS)
        w1_fd = (w_plus - w_minus) / (2.0 * h)
        w2_fd = (w_plus - 2.0 * w + w_minus) / (h * h)
        g_fd = (
            (1.0 - k * w1_fd / (2.0 * w)) ** 2
            - (w1_fd * w1_fd / 4.0) * (1.0 / w + 1.0 / 4.0)
            + w2_fd / 2.0
        )
        _, _, _, g, _ = SVI.svi_g(k, TRUE_PARAMS)
        self.assertTrue(np.allclose(g, g_fd, rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-6), msg=f"max diff={np.max(np.abs(g - g_fd))}")

        w1_analytic = SVI.svi_g(k, TRUE_PARAMS)[1]
        w2_analytic = SVI.svi_g(k, TRUE_PARAMS)[2]
        self.assertTrue(np.allclose(w1_analytic, w1_fd, rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-6))
        self.assertTrue(np.allclose(w2_analytic, w2_fd, rtol=1e-4, atol=1e-5))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main(verbosity=2)

# Open issues

## Q1B neural surface: optimization cause verified and fixed

The 2025-09-15 diagnostic verified that the original underperformance was an
optimization failure at the tiny price-loss scale, not a lambda-weighting effect
and not a capacity limit.

On that date (92 OTM quotes, 5 expiries, shared lambda-independent seed):

| run | fit MSE | median | p95 | max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| approach1 SVI target | 2.278e-08 | 0.00685 | 0.04207 | 0.08194 |
| neural before, unscaled | 7.632e-07 | 0.05304 | 0.72232 | 0.96369 |
| neural after, scaled | 2.001e-08 | 0.00697 | 0.05418 | 0.14782 |

Before, L-BFGS stopped at `max_iter=100`; the final gradient norm was `5.34e-7`
(versus `tolerance_grad=1e-10`) and the loss moved only from `7.6324e-7` after
Adam to `7.6321e-7` after L-BFGS. Scaling the whole objective by
`c=1/initial_price_loss=162.65`, with 3000 Adam steps and 1000 L-BFGS steps,
reduced the fit MSE by 38x and let L-BFGS reduce the Adam-end loss by 6.1x.
An unscaled 3000/500 control reached only `1.271e-7`; a 64-unit capacity test
was worse (`2.330e-8` fit MSE), so capacity is not the bottleneck.

The lambda ablation was inactive on the diagnostic date: all 10 lambda pairs
gave bit-identical results and the penalty terms were exactly zero at
initialization, end of Adam and end of L-BFGS. The old apparent lambda effect
was seed confounding.

## Result after the full rerun (`results/approach2/io_scaled`)

Configuration: seeds independent of lambda; `c=1/initial_price_loss` applied to
the whole objective; lambda unchanged; 3000 Adam steps; L-BFGS `max_iter=1000`,
`max_evals=1500`, `max_seconds=45`, `tolerance_grad=1e-8`,
`tolerance_change=1e-12`; 24 units, 3 hidden layers; 60-minute guard.
Runtime: 1638 s. Coverage: 54/54 ablation fits, 18/18 random robustness fits,
6/6 wing robustness fits, 0 failed fits, determinism check passed.

Chosen lambdas: `lambda1=0.01`, `lambda2=0.0`, selected by complete coverage,
zero violations at 1e-8 on the approach1 audit grid, lowest pooled median, then
smallest `lambda1+lambda2`.

Overall comparison with approach1 on the same 470 OTM quotes:

| model | median | p95 | max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| approach1 repaired SVI | 0.008214 | 0.054525 | 0.173657 |
| neural chosen | 0.008687 | 0.123426 | 0.982950 |

| design | model | fits | n | median | p95 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| random 30% | SVI | 18/18 | 407 | 0.016297 | 0.126115 |
| random 30% | neural | 18/18 | 407 | 0.018359 | 0.221206 |
| wing 15% | SVI | 6/6 | 83 | 0.050337 | 0.559186 |
| wing 15% | neural | 6/6 | 83 | 0.093261 | 0.780917 |

The neural surface is now competitive in overall price MSE and in median
relative error, but it is still worse in the tails, on the shortest tenor and
on the wing holdout.

## Penalty activity on all dates

`penalty_max` is the largest unweighted penalty term seen during Adam/L-BFGS.
"Differs from (0,0)" means the lambda pair changed the final metrics or
violation counts relative to the unpenalized fit on that date.

| date | max butterfly penalty | max calendar penalty | differs from (0,0) | outcome |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| 2024-03-14 | 0 | 0 | no | all lambda pairs identical |
| 2024-09-13 | 4.270e-04 | 2.243e-06 | no | penalties transient; final metrics identical |
| 2025-03-14 | 2.444e-08 | 0 | no | final metrics identical |
| 2025-09-15 | 0 | 0 | no | all lambda pairs identical |
| 2026-03-16 | 6.733e-05 | 0 | yes | `lambda1=0.01` removes 3 approach1-grid butterfly violations and improves median 0.00816 -> 0.00641; `lambda1=1` is worse (median 0.01436, 1 violation) |
| 2026-09-15 | 9.899e-01 (lambda1=1); 4.357e-05 (lambda1=0.01) | 4.553e-08 | yes | `lambda1=0.01` improves median 0.00987 -> 0.00869 and keeps zero approach1-grid violations; `lambda1=1` gives median 0.01235 with 1 butterfly violation |

So the penalties were not inactive on every date. They were active in training
on four of six dates, but changed final results only on 2026-03-16 and
2026-09-15. `lambda1=1` is too strong when it binds: it dominates the O(1e-6)
fit term and produces a worse surface. `lambda1=0.01` is useful on those two
dates.

## Remaining issue: dense-grid arbitrage outside the training collocation

Chosen model on the approach1 audit grid (k in [-0.14,0.14]): 0 butterfly and
0 calendar violations at strict and 1e-8. On the denser grid (k from -0.20 to
0.20 step 0.005, listed expiries plus midpoints), the chosen model has
30 butterfly and 4 calendar violations, all outside the training collocation
range |k|<=0.14:

- dense butterfly: 2024-09-13 (15), 2025-03-14 (14), 2026-03-16 (1);
  minimum dense `g = -0.5603`.
- dense calendar: 2026-09-15 (4); minimum dense forward variance `-0.00502`.

The worst relative repricing error is also a wing quote outside the collocation
range: 2026-09-15, 2026-10-16 expiry, `k=0.181`, price 1.4, relative error
0.983. The price-space loss barely penalizes it because its unit-forward price
is tiny. The training and selection grids therefore overstate arbitrage
freeness; extending the collocation to the full `kband` (+/-0.20) and adding
wing collocation points is the next change to consider.

## Superseded result

`results/approach2/io` is kept for the record and labeled in `compare.py` as
"superseded: optimization failure, kept for the record". `io_scaled` is the
primary Q1B result.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Compare numeric values in a reproduced results tree against committed results."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path

from rich.console import Console
from rich.table import Table

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
DEFAULT_REFERENCE = ROOT / "results"
DEFAULT_CANDIDATE = ROOT / ".cache" / "clean_clone_full" / "results"
RELATIVE_TOLERANCE = 1e-6
TIMING_TOKENS = (
    "second",
    "time",
    "duration",
    "elapsed",
    "speedup",
    "per_second",
    "timestamp",
)
HISTORICAL_SCENARIOS = {"approach2/io"}


def is_timing_key(key: str) -> bool:
    lower = key.lower()
    return any(token in lower for token in TIMING_TOKENS)


def flatten(value, path: str = "", out: dict[str, float] | None = None) -> dict[str, float]:
    if out is None:
        out = {}
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        for key, item in value.items():
            if is_timing_key(str(key)):
                continue
            child = f"{path}.{key}" if path else str(key)
            flatten(item, child, out)
    elif isinstance(value, list):
        for index, item in enumerate(value):
            flatten(item, f"{path}[{index}]", out)
    elif isinstance(value, bool):
        return out
    elif isinstance(value, (int, float)):
        out[path] = value
    return out


def relative_difference(reference: float, candidate: float) -> float:
    scale = max(abs(reference), abs(candidate))
    if scale == 0.0:
        return 0.0
    return abs(candidate - reference) / scale


def compare_file(reference_path: Path, candidate_path: Path) -> dict:
    reference = flatten(json.loads(reference_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
    candidate = flatten(json.loads(candidate_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
    shared = sorted(set(reference) & set(candidate))
    differences = []
    exact = 0
    max_abs = 0.0
    max_rel = 0.0
    max_abs_key = ""
    max_rel_key = ""
    for key in shared:
        left = float(reference[key])
        right = float(candidate[key])
        if left == right:
            exact += 1
            continue
        absolute = abs(right - left)
        relative = relative_difference(left, right)
        if absolute > max_abs:
            max_abs = absolute
            max_abs_key = key
        if relative > max_rel:
            max_rel = relative
            max_rel_key = key
        differences.append(
            {
                "key": key,
                "reference": left,
                "candidate": right,
                "abs": absolute,
                "rel": relative,
            }
        )
    differences.sort(key=lambda item: (item["abs"], item["rel"]), reverse=True)
    return {
        "reference": str(reference_path),
        "candidate": str(candidate_path),
        "compared": len(shared),
        "exact": exact,
        "max_abs": max_abs,
        "max_abs_key": max_abs_key,
        "max_rel": max_rel,
        "max_rel_key": max_rel_key,
        "differences": differences,
        "only_candidate": sorted(set(candidate) - set(reference)),
        "only_reference": sorted(set(reference) - set(candidate)),
    }


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Compare reproduced metrics.json against committed metrics.json")
    parser.add_argument("--reference", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_REFERENCE)
    parser.add_argument("--candidate", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_CANDIDATE)
    parser.add_argument("--tolerance", type=float, default=RELATIVE_TOLERANCE)
    parser.add_argument("--top", type=int, default=5)
    parser.add_argument("--json-out", type=Path, default=None)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    reference_root = args.reference.resolve()
    candidate_root = args.candidate.resolve()
    if not reference_root.is_dir():
        raise SystemExit(f"missing reference directory: {reference_root}")
    if not candidate_root.is_dir():
        raise SystemExit(f"missing candidate directory: {candidate_root}")

    reference_files = {path.relative_to(reference_root): path for path in reference_root.glob("approach*/*/metrics.json")}
    candidate_files = {path.relative_to(candidate_root): path for path in candidate_root.glob("approach*/*/metrics.json")}
    if not candidate_files:
        raise SystemExit(f"no metrics.json files under {candidate_root}")

    console = Console(width=220)
    table = Table(title="Reproduction numeric comparison")
    for column in ("file", "compared", "exact", "max_abs", "max_rel", "top differing keys"):
        table.add_column(column, justify="right" if column not in {"file", "top differing keys"} else "left")

    reports = []
    failures = []
    historical = sorted(
        relative
        for relative in set(reference_files) | set(candidate_files)
        if str(relative.parent) in HISTORICAL_SCENARIOS
    )
    for relative in historical:
        table.add_row(str(relative), "-", "-", "n/a", "n/a", "historical, not rerun")
        reports.append({"file": str(relative), "status": "historical_not_rereproduced"})
    for relative in sorted(candidate_files):
        if relative in historical:
            continue
        if relative not in reference_files:
            reports.append({"file": str(relative), "status": "missing_reference"})
            table.add_row(str(relative), "0", "0", "n/a", "n/a", "missing committed reference")
            failures.append(str(relative))
            continue
        report = compare_file(reference_files[relative], candidate_files[relative])
        report["file"] = str(relative)
        reports.append(report)
        top_keys = ", ".join(item["key"] for item in report["differences"][: args.top]) or "-"
        table.add_row(
            str(relative),
            f"{report['compared']}",
            f"{report['exact']}",
            f"{report['max_abs']:.3e}",
            f"{report['max_rel']:.3e}",
            top_keys,
        )
        if report["max_rel"] > args.tolerance or report["only_candidate"]:
            failures.append(str(relative))

    console.print(table)

    detail = Table(title=f"Top differing keys (relative tolerance {args.tolerance:g})")
    for column in ("file", "key", "committed", "reproduced", "abs_diff", "rel_diff"):
        detail.add_column(column, justify="left" if column in {"file", "key"} else "right")
    for report in reports:
        for item in report.get("differences", [])[: args.top]:
            detail.add_row(
                report["file"],
                item["key"],
                f"{item['reference']:.17g}",
                f"{item['candidate']:.17g}",
                f"{item['abs']:.3e}",
                f"{item['rel']:.3e}",
            )
    if any(report.get("differences") for report in reports):
        console.print(detail)
    else:
        console.print("[green]all compared numeric values are exact[/green]")

    for report in reports:
        if report.get("only_candidate"):
            console.print(f"[yellow]{report['file']}: {len(report['only_candidate'])} numeric keys only in reproduced run[/yellow]")
        if report.get("only_reference"):
            console.print(f"[yellow]{report['file']}: {len(report['only_reference'])} numeric keys only in committed run[/yellow]")

    missing = sorted(set(reference_files) - set(candidate_files) - set(historical))
    if missing:
        console.print("[yellow]committed scenarios not present in the reproduced tree (not rerun by design):[/yellow]")
        for relative in missing:
            console.print(f"  {relative}")
    if historical:
        console.print("[yellow]historical scenarios (not rerun, excluded from reproduction):[/yellow]")
        for relative in historical:
            console.print(f"  {relative}  historical, not rerun")

    if args.json_out is not None:
        args.json_out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        args.json_out.write_text(
            json.dumps({"tolerance": args.tolerance, "reports": reports}, indent=2, allow_nan=False),
            encoding="utf-8",
        )

    if failures:
        console.print(f"[red]FAIL: {len(failures)} file(s) exceed tolerance or have unmatched keys[/red]")
        return 1
    console.print("[green]PASS: every compared numeric value is within tolerance[/green]")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Cross-approach comparison tables, read only from results/**/metrics.json."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import math
from pathlib import Path

import plotly.graph_objects as go
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots
from rich.console import Console
from rich.table import Table

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
RESULTS = ROOT / "results"
OUT_HTML = RESULTS / "comparison.html"

console = Console()


def fmt(value, digits: int = 4) -> str:
    if value is None:
        return "n/a"
    try:
        number = float(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return str(value)
    if not math.isfinite(number):
        return "n/a"
    return f"{number:.{digits}f}"


def fmt_pm(mean, std, digits: int = 4) -> str:
    if mean is None:
        return "n/a"
    if std is None or not math.isfinite(float(std)):
        return fmt(mean, digits)
    return f"{fmt(mean, digits)} ± {fmt(std, digits)}"


def load_all() -> list[dict]:
    paths = sorted(RESULTS.glob("approach*/*/metrics.json"))
    if not paths:
        raise SystemExit(f"no metrics.json files under {RESULTS}")
    payloads = []
    for path in paths:
        payload = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        if list(payload) != ["params", "metrics", "fit_seconds", "history"]:
            raise ValueError(f"{path}: unexpected top-level keys {list(payload)}")
        payloads.append(
            {
                "path": path,
                "rel": str(path.relative_to(ROOT)),
                "approach": path.parts[-3],
                "dataset": path.parts[-2],
                "payload": payload,
            }
        )
    return payloads

7:The repository implements Q1, Q2 and Q3 of the Advanced Programming 2026 brief, options A and B of each. Q1 fits an arbitrage-free implied-volatility surface to CFFEX IO options, with SVI slices (Q1A) and a neural surface (Q1B). Q2 prices path-dependent payoffs under GBM by Monte Carlo (Q2A) and learns a CVaR-optimal hedge (Q2B). Q3 forecasts the PMI contraction regime with a classical probit/PCA model (Q3A) and an LSTM with leakage ablations (Q3B).
9:The results are mixed and are reported plainly. Q1A fits all 693 liquid date-expiry slices on the settle price and reaches zero butterfly and zero calendar violations at the 1e-8 tolerance on its audit grid, but 1 butterfly and 12 calendar checks remain strictly negative after repair. The median per-fit median repricing error is 0.77% on settle and 1.27% on close; the median per-fit maximum is 2.58% and 4.33%. Q1B is close to SVI in median repricing on the same 470 OTM quotes (0.87% vs 0.82%) but much worse in the tail (p95 12.34% vs 5.45%; maximum 98.30% vs 17.37%), and it violates arbitrage on a denser grid outside its training collocation. Q2A passes the Black-Scholes and closed-form checks; the Asian control-variate variance ratio is 308x to 1974x across four futures, above the 5x benchmark. Q2B's deep policy has lower gross and net CVaR than daily Black-Scholes hedging on the brief P&L at zero and at 50 bp cost. Q3A beats the expanding prior on Brier score but not persistence (AUC 0.6928 vs 0.7390), and its nowcast beats a random-walk-with-drift benchmark in all periods, including ex-COVID. Q3B does not beat persistence either; the retrained LSTM never predicts a probability above 0.5 on the test block and its test AUC is 0.6422 versus 0.7390 for persistence.
11:What was not achieved: Q1B is not globally arbitrage-free and is not competitive with SVI in the wings; Q2B covers only IF and uses one training seed; Q3A and Q3B do not reach the indicative AUC target of 0.75 or beat persistence. The data are daily, without bid-ask quotes or real-time macro vintages.

55:### 3.2 Q1 filtering, parity and implied volatility
57:Q1 uses the CFFEX `settle` field as the primary price and repeats the pipeline on `close`. There is no bid-ask snapshot, so liquidity is proxied by volume. Filters are volume >= 10, price >= 1, `|k| <= 0.20` and days-to-expiry >= 7. The volume floor stands in for a missing spread, the price floor removes near-zero quotes, the strike band keeps the fit local enough for a raw SVI slice, and the days floor avoids degenerate short tenors. On settle, sequential removals are 8,008 by volume, 1,303 by price, 1,380 by strike band and 606 by days, leaving 18,771 liquid quotes. There are 750 date-expiry groups, 728 with liquid quotes, 693 fits and 57 skipped groups (34 with fewer than six strikes, 23 with no liquid OTM quote). The OTM quote set has 11,146 quotes. Rate convention is `r(tau) = ln(1 + L/100 * tau * 365/360) / tau` from SHIBOR, linear in tenor and flat outside pillars. The forward is a volume-weighted mean of `F_K = K + (C-P)/DF` within `|ln(F_K / median(F_K))| <= 0.05`; `q = r - ln(F/S0)/T`.

157:## 5. Q1 Option B: neural surface
161:Q1B uses the same OTM quotes as Q1A on six sample dates (2024-03-14, 2024-09-13, 2025-03-14, 2025-09-15, 2026-03-16, 2026-09-15), giving 30 date-expiry fits and 470 quotes. The 2024-03 date is one day before the metadata date 2024-03-15 because the selection rule takes the nearest mid-month date with at least 80% of that month's maximum quote count. The surface is one MLP across all expiries: inputs `k/0.2` and `sqrt(T)/sqrt(T_max)`, four layers (three hidden layers of 24 units), `tanh` activation, and a softplus output plus `1e-6` for `sigma`. The loss is the mean squared undiscounted OTM price per unit forward plus `lambda1 * mean(max(0,-g)^2)` and `lambda2 * mean(max(0,-dw/dT)^2)` on a collocation grid `k in [-0.14,0.14]` crossed with expiry tenors; `g` includes `w''/2`. The whole objective is multiplied by `c = 1 / initial_price_loss`, which leaves the minimizer unchanged. Optimization is 3,000 Adam steps followed by bounded L-BFGS (1,000 iterations, strong Wolfe, 45 s cap). Seeds are derived from date, design and replication but not lambda, so lambda pairs share an initialization.
163:Selection is pre-declared: complete fit coverage, then zero butterfly and calendar violations at 1e-8 on the Q1A grid, then the lowest pooled in-sample OTM relative repricing median, with ties broken by the smallest `lambda1 + lambda2`. The chosen pair is `lambda1=0.01`, `lambda2=0.0`.
167:Table 8: Q1B 3x3 lambda ablation. Source: `results/approach2/io_scaled/metrics.json`.
183:Table 9: Q1B chosen model and SVI comparison on the same 470 OTM quotes. Source: `results/approach2/io_scaled/metrics.json`.
191:The chosen neural surface has 0 butterfly and 0 calendar violations on the Q1A grid (`min g = 0.002068`), but 30 butterfly and 4 calendar violations on the dense grid (`k` from -0.20 to 0.20 step 0.005, listed expiries plus midpoints), with dense minimum `g = -0.5603` and dense minimum forward variance -0.005021. All dense violations are outside the training collocation `|k| <= 0.14`; this is consistent with extrapolation failure, but the cause was not separately tested.
193:Table 10: Q1B cold-start SVI solver comparison (primary solver result). Source: `results/approach2/io_scaled/metrics.json`.
201:The cold-start comparison uses a documented cold point `a = 0.5*min(w)`, `b=0.1`, `rho=-0.3`, `m=0`, `eta=0.1`, the same for all solvers, with a strict 0.1% relative tolerance against the best known objective. Adam is one setting only (5,000 iterations, learning rate 0.03, cosine schedule); the result does not support a general claim that Adam is poor. The warm-started comparison in `svi_solver` starts all solvers at approach1's optimum: torch reaches the 0.1% tolerance on 29/30 fits and scipy on 30/30, with torch's median iterations to tolerance equal to 0 because the start is already at the optimum. That comparison is not a convergence test. The cold-start table above is the primary solver result.
203:Table 11: Q1B penalty activity by date. Source: `results/approach2/io_scaled/metrics.json`.
216:Table 12: Q1B random and wing robustness. Source: `results/approach2/io_scaled/metrics.json`.
225:Table 13: Q1B per-tenor comparison with SVI. Source: `NOTES_OPEN_ISSUES.md` (diagnostic record, not a metrics file); this table is not regenerated by `reproduce.sh`.
234:The committed Q1B metrics do not contain the per-tenor breakdown; the table above is the previously recorded diagnostic in `NOTES_OPEN_ISSUES.md`, included because the brief asks for it, and is not a `metrics.json` result.
238:The neural surface is close to SVI in median repricing but worse in the tail and in the wing holdout. The dense-grid audit means the surface must not be called globally arbitrage-free. The cold-start comparison shows that scipy is the reliable solver in this setting; Adam reaches tolerance on 0/30 cold starts at the single setting tested, and L-BFGS on 14/30. `results/approach2/io/metrics.json` is the optimization failure that motivated the fix: median 4.43%, p95 67.84%, max 98.19%, with no penalties. The diagnosis recorded in `NOTES_OPEN_ISSUES.md` is that L-BFGS stopped at 100 iterations and the loss scale was tiny; the fix was whole-objective scaling by `c = 1/initial_price_loss`, shared initialization independent of lambda, 3,000 Adam steps, 1,000 L-BFGS iterations, and 24 units in three hidden layers. The diagnosis was not independently re-tested for this report.
240:## 6. Q2 Option A: Monte Carlo pricing
244:Under the brief's GBM, `dS_t = r S_t dt + sigma S_t dW_t`, with `S0` the last close, `K=S0`, `T=1`, `m=252`, barrier `B=1.3 S0`, and `r` the SHIBOR zero at `T`. A futures price has zero drift under Q; the brief specifies drift `r`, so the code follows the brief and flags this as a modelling simplification. `sigma` is the standard deviation of daily log returns times `sqrt(252)` on a five-year window. The payoffs are arithmetic Asian `max(mean(S_{t_i})-K,0)`, discretely monitored up-and-out `max(S_T-K,0) * 1{max S_{t_i}<B}`, cash-or-nothing digital `1{S_T>K}`, and European `max(S_T-K,0)`. All are discounted by `exp(-rT)`.

393:## 7. Q2 Option B: deep hedging
397:The hedge is a European ATM call on IF with `S0=100`, `K=100`, `T=0.25`, `m=63`, `sigma=0.1911` (the Q2A five-year IF calibration) and `r=0.01417` (SHIBOR zero at `T`). The policy is a small MLP with two hidden layers of 32 units mapping `(S_t/S0, t/T)` to a delta in `[0,1]` through a sigmoid; it does not see the previous position. The objective is empirical CVaR at 0.95 of `-V_T`, the mean of the worst 5% of losses per batch. Training uses `2^17` paths, batches of `2^12`, 100 epochs, Adam at learning rate 0.005, and one policy per cost `kappa in {0,10,50}` bp. The same network initialization is used for every kappa. Validation uses three independent seeds with `2^17` paths each; training uses one seed (42).

463:## 8. Q3 Option A: classical probit
467:The information set is implemented by shifting each series forward by its lag `L_i`: row `t` contains only values public at the end of month `t`. The label is `d_t = 1{PMI_t < 50 and PMI_{t-1} < 50}`. The model is `P(d_{t+1}=1) = Phi(beta' z_t)`, where `z_t` contains an intercept, the first `r` principal components of the standardized aligned factor panel (excluding `gdp_yoy`, `cgb10y`, `spread_10y_2y`, `shibor_3m`) and the controls `cgb10y` and `spread_10y_2y`. PCA and standardization use only rows public at the origin; missing values become zero after standardization; series with under 50% training-window coverage are dropped. The probit is fitted by maximum likelihood with a ridge of `1e-4` and a Newton/BFGS fallback. Validation is expanding walk-forward, refit monthly, minimum 60 training months, a 36-month tuning block and a test block of 105 origins from 2018-01-31 to 2026-09-30. The PCA rank is chosen on the tuning block by cross-validated nowcast RMSE at month 3 of the quarter.

592:## 9. Q3 Option B: LSTM and leakage
596:Q3B uses 12-month windows of the standardized aligned panel, excluding `gdp_yoy`, as input to an LSTM with at most two layers and a linear logit head. Training pairs are `(window ending s, d_{s+1})` with `s+1 <= origin t`. The loss is `BCEWithLogits` with `pos_weight = n_neg/n_pos`, and probabilities are corrected by `p_cal = sigmoid(logit - log(pos_weight))`. The walk-forward scheme is expanding, with the LSTM refit every six months while the Q3A probit refits monthly. Hyperparameters are selected on the 36-month tuning block only by mean Brier over three seeds.
598:The original run used 18-month validation blocks. The retrained model, which is the primary Q3B result, uses the chosen setting hidden 8, one layer, dropout 0.2 and weight decay `1e-2`, an expanding split with the last 36 training-pair months held out for validation, minimum 30 epochs, patience 30 and maximum 300 epochs, with three seeds. Leakage arms are the disciplined aligned panel, a zero-lag panel (`L_i=0`), a zero-lag panel with full-sample standardization, and a zero-lag probit. Leakage premiums use a circular 12-month block bootstrap with 5,000 replicates; positive means the leaked arm looks better (lower Brier or higher AUC).
602:Table 34: Q3B primary comparison, retrained LSTM (test block, 105 origins, 34 positives). Source: `results/approach6/macro/metrics.json`.
613:The retrained disciplined LSTM has Brier 0.2561, AUC 0.6422 and accuracy 0.6762; it does not beat persistence (0.2286, 0.7390, 0.7714) or the probit (0.2396, 0.6928, 0.6381) on Brier or AUC. Its accuracy equals the all-negative rate because it never predicts a probability above 0.5 on the test block. In `results/approach6/macro/post_hoc_predictions.csv`, the disciplined arm has 0 of 105 predictions above 0.5 for each seed; the maxima are 0.1767 (seed 42), 0.3172 (seed 43) and 0.2234 (seed 44).
615:Table 35: Q3B retrained leakage premiums (positive means leaked arm better). Source: `results/approach6/macro/metrics.json`.
626:Table 36: Q3B original failed run and tuning/test gap. Source: `results/approach6/macro/metrics.json`.
635:Table 37: Q3B latent bridge and null. Source: `results/approach6/macro/metrics.json`.
649:The bridge maps each indicator to a correlation vector with the 16 hidden dimensions over 2023-01-31 to 2025-12-31, clusters those vectors with `k=9`, and compares with Q3A's latest indicator labels. Because `h_t` is computed from those indicators, the ARI significance may be partly mechanical; the null permutes indicator labels against fixed bridge clusters, not the full construction. The latent analysis is descriptive.

674:The Q1 median is 0.77% on settle and 1.27% on close, so the 2% target is met on both price fields. The benchmark table contains only the brief's indicative targets. Other checks in this report, such as the kappa=0 deep-hedge comparison or the cluster ARI, are my additions and are not brief targets.
678:1. **Butterfly formula.** The printed `g(k)` omits `w''/2`; the code uses the correct Gatheral form for decisions and reports both. On settle, raw strict violations are 8 with `w''/2` and 382 without; repaired strict violations are 1 and 390. On close, raw strict counts are 23 and 418; repaired strict counts are 3 and 423. Source: `results/approach1/io/metrics.json`, `results/approach1/io_close/metrics.json`.
679:2. **Hedging P&L.** The printed brief P&L omits the financing cost of the stock position, so it is not exactly self-financing. The brief-minus-self-financing CVaR gap is -0.1796 for daily BS at kappa 0 and -0.2094 for the deep policy at kappa 0; the mean across all cells is -0.1960. The negative sign means the brief formula reports lower CVaR than the self-financing formula. Source: `results/approach4/IF/metrics.json`.
680:3. **GBM drift.** The brief specifies drift `r`; the code follows the brief. A futures price has zero drift under Q, so this is a modelling simplification, recorded in `params.drift_note`. Source: `results/approach3/IF/metrics.json`.
681:4. **No bid-ask data.** Daily CFFEX data have no bid-ask spread, so volume >= 10 stands in for liquidity/spread. On settle this filter removes 8,008 quotes; the full sequential filter removes 11,297. Source: `results/approach1/io/metrics.json`.
682:5. **LSTM refit frequency.** Q3B refits the LSTM every six months and reuses the last refit between refits; Q3A refits the probit monthly. Source: `results/approach6/macro/metrics.json`.
683:6. **Cluster bridge.** Q3A clusters partition indicators, while the LSTM's month-level `h_t` clusters partition months, so a direct ARI is undefined. The bridge maps each indicator to a correlation vector with the 16 hidden dimensions and clusters those vectors with `k=9`; the resulting ARI may be partly mechanical because `h_t` is computed from those indicators. Source: `results/approach6/macro/metrics.json`.
684:7. **SVI eta bounds.** The current bounds are `[0.01,1.0]`, narrower than the legacy `[1e-6,2.0]`. This changes bound hits but not median RMSE materially. Source: `results/approach1/io/metrics.json`.
685:8. **Q1B sample date.** Q1B uses 2024-03-14, while the metadata sample date is 2024-03-15. The selection rule chooses the nearest mid-month date with at least 80% of the month's maximum quote count. Source: `results/approach2/io_scaled/metrics.json`.
686:9. **Q3B inputs.** The LSTM excludes `gdp_yoy` from the 12-month input panel to avoid a mixed-frequency quarterly series; the probit also excludes it from the factors. Source: `results/approach6/macro/metrics.json`.
687:10. **Q2B scope.** Only IF is used, with one training seed and no terminal unwind; the brief permits this but it limits generalisation. Source: `results/approach4/IF/metrics.json`.
690:13. **Only IO options.** Only CFFEX IO options are used for the surface; SSE ETF options are not fitted. Source: `data/metadata.json` and `results/approach1/io/metrics.json`.
691:14. **Parity forward.** `q` is replaced by the put-call parity forward: `q = r - ln(F/S0)/T` with `F` estimated from parity, rather than a dividend model. Source: `results/approach1/io/metrics.json`.
697:- Both models are weak in the wings and at short tenors: Q1A settle worst per-fit max repricing is 0.3251 and close is 0.2624; Q1B wing p95 is 0.7809 and max 1.519, versus SVI 0.5592.
700:- Q2B used one training seed, only IF, no terminal unwind cost, and no previous position in the policy inputs; it cannot represent a no-trade region.
704:- The Q3 nowcast month-3 ex-COVID error is higher than month-1; the paired interval includes zero, and no cause is asserted.
705:- The Q3 clustering is unstable across windows (adjacent ARI median 0.1648) and is descriptive only.
706:- The Q1B per-tenor table comes from `NOTES_OPEN_ISSUES.md`, not from a committed `metrics.json`.
712:- `/tmp/q1_online.log`, `/tmp/q1_online_resume.log`, `/tmp/q1_online_resume2.log`, `/tmp/q1_expiry_fix.log`: logs from the early Q1 data downloads.
