def to_jsonable(value):
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {str(key): to_jsonable(val) for key, val in value.items()}
    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple, np.ndarray)):
        return [to_jsonable(val) for val in value]
    if isinstance(value, np.integer):
        return int(value)
    if isinstance(value, (np.floating, float)):
        val = float(value)
        return val if math.isfinite(val) else None
    if isinstance(value, (np.bool_, bool)):
        return bool(value)
    if isinstance(value, Path):
        return str(value)
    return value


def sha256_file(path: Path) -> str:
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open("rb") as handle:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: handle.read(1 << 20), b""):
            digest.update(chunk)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def ensure_inside_repo(path: Path) -> Path:
    root = ROOT.resolve()
    resolved = path.resolve()
    if resolved != root and root not in resolved.parents:
        raise ValueError(f"path must stay inside {root}: {resolved}")
    return resolved


def set_torch_threads(threads: int) -> None:
    if threads < 1:
        raise ValueError("--torch-threads must be >= 1")
    torch.set_num_threads(threads)
    try:
        torch.set_num_interop_threads(threads)
    except RuntimeError:
        pass


class RunLog:
    def __init__(self, path: Path) -> None:
        self.path = ensure_inside_repo(path)
        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.start = time.perf_counter()

    def write(self, message: str) -> None:
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - self.start
        line = f"[{elapsed:8.2f}s] {message}"
        with self.path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            handle.write(line + "\n")
        console.print(line)

    def check_budget(self, limit_minutes: float, phase: str) -> None:
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - self.start
        if elapsed > limit_minutes * 60.0:
            raise TimeoutError(
                f"runtime guard: {phase} exceeded {limit_minutes:.1f} minutes "
                f"(elapsed {elapsed / 60.0:.1f} min); stop and report before cutting scope"
            )


def load_approach3():
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("approach3_q2a_mc", APPROACH3_PATH)
    if spec is None or spec.loader is None:
        raise ImportError(f"cannot load {APPROACH3_PATH}")
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


def load_market_setup(dataset: str, T: float, shibor_path: Path) -> dict:
    a3 = load_approach3()
    frame = a3.load_futures(dataset)
    calibration = a3.calibration_stats(frame["close"].to_numpy(dtype=float), frame["date"])
    sigma = float(calibration["sigma_annualized"])
    shibor = a3.load_shibor(shibor_path)
    curves = a3.build_rate_curves(shibor)
    sorted_dates = np.array(sorted(curves), dtype="datetime64[ns]")
    if len(sorted_dates) == 0:
        raise ValueError("no usable SHIBOR curves")
    valuation_date = pd.Timestamp(frame["date"].iloc[-1])
    r, curve_date = a3.zero_rate(curves, sorted_dates, valuation_date, T)
    reference_sigma = None
    if APPROACH3_METRICS.exists():
        payload = json.loads(APPROACH3_METRICS.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        reference_sigma = float(payload["params"]["sigma"])
    return {
        "sigma": sigma,
        "sigma_reference": reference_sigma,
        "sigma_matches_reference": bool(
            reference_sigma is None or abs(reference_sigma - sigma) < 1e-12
        ),
        "r": float(r),
        "rate_convention": (
            "SHIBOR zero from approach3: log(1 + quoted*365/360*tau)/tau, linear in tau"
        ),
        "valuation_date": valuation_date.date().isoformat(),
        "shibor_date": curve_date.date().isoformat(),
        "curve_date": curve_date,
        "calibration_window": {
            "start": calibration["window_start"],
            "end": calibration["window_end"],
            "years": calibration["window_years"],
        },
        "input": str((ROOT / "data" / "clean" / f"futures_{dataset}.csv").relative_to(ROOT)),
        "input_sha256": sha256_file(ROOT / "data" / "clean" / f"futures_{dataset}.csv"),
        "shibor": str(shibor_path.relative_to(ROOT)) if shibor_path.is_relative_to(ROOT) else str(shibor_path),
        "shibor_sha256": sha256_file(shibor_path),
    }

                "min_train_cvar": float(np.min(history["train_cvar"])),
                "seconds": fit_seconds[kappa_bp],
            }
            for kappa_bp, history in histories.items()
        },
        "limitation": params["limitation"],
    }

    history_payload = {
        "training": {str(kappa_bp): value for kappa_bp, value in histories.items()},
        "timings": {
            "fit_seconds": fit_seconds,
            "total_fit_seconds": float(sum(fit_seconds.values())),
            "wall_seconds": float(time.perf_counter() - log.start),
        },
        "config": {
            "seed": args.seed,
            "torch_threads": args.torch_threads,
            "n_train": args.n_train,
            "batch_size": args.batch_size,
            "epochs": args.epochs,
            "lr": args.lr,
            "hidden": args.hidden,
            "hidden_layers": args.hidden_layers,
            "dtype": "float32",
        },
    }

    result = {
        "params": params,
        "metrics": metrics,
        "fit_seconds": float(sum(fit_seconds.values())),
        "history": history_payload,
    }
    (out_dir / "metrics.json").write_text(
        json.dumps(to_jsonable(result), ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding="utf-8"
    )
    log.write(f"wrote {out_dir / 'metrics.json'}")
    print_table(table_rows)
    print_cross(cross_rows)
    print_sensitivity(sensitivities)
    console.print(
        f"Deep kappa=0 selffin CVaR / BS daily selffin CVaR = {ratio:.4f} "
        f"(close_to_bs_daily={deep_zero_check['close_to_bs_daily']})"
    )
    console.print(f"Total fit seconds: {result['fit_seconds']:.2f}")
    log.write("Q2B complete")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

def parse_args(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Cold-start SVI solver comparison")
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
    parser.add_argument("--price-col", choices=["close", "settle"], default="settle")
    parser.add_argument("--out-dir", type=Path, default=ROOT / "results" / "approach2" / "io_scaled")

def load_fits(args: argparse.Namespace, base: argparse.Namespace):
    options, shibor, metadata = A1.load_data(base.options, base.shibor, base.metadata)
    forwards, _ = A1.estimate_forwards(options, shibor, args.price_col)
    data, _ = A1.apply_filters(options, forwards, base)
    iv, _, _ = A1.compute_implied_vols(data[data.liquid])
    sample_dates, _ = q1b.select_sample_dates(options, metadata)
    otm, otm_info = q1b.build_otm_quotes(data, iv, sample_dates, base.min_strikes)
    bounds = A1.svi_bounds(base.eta_min, base.eta_max)
    reference_starts, _ = q1b.load_reference_starts(base.approach1_dir, otm, sample_dates, bounds)
    fits = []
    for date in sample_dates:
        group = q1b.date_quotes(otm, date)
        for expiry, slice_group in group.groupby("expiry", sort=True):
            key = (
                pd.Timestamp(date).strftime("%Y-%m-%d"),
                pd.Timestamp(expiry).strftime("%Y-%m-%d"),
            )
            if key not in reference_starts:
                continue
            fits.append(
                {
                    "date": key[0],
                    "expiry": key[1],
                    "T": float(slice_group["T"].iloc[0]),
                    "n_quotes": int(len(slice_group)),
                    "k": slice_group.k.to_numpy(dtype=float),
                    "w": slice_group.w.to_numpy(dtype=float),
                    "reference": np.asarray(reference_starts[key]["raw"], dtype=float),
                    "reference_source": str(reference_starts[key]["source"]),
                }
            )
    if args.max_fits is not None:
        fits = fits[: int(args.max_fits)]
    return fits, sample_dates, otm_info, bounds


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = parse_args(argv)
    base = q1b.parse_args([])
    base.seed = int(args.seed)

    q1b.set_seed(args.seed)

def latent_month_analysis(
    hidden: np.ndarray,
    frame: pd.DataFrame,
    args: argparse.Namespace,
) -> tuple[list[dict], dict[int, np.ndarray], np.ndarray, np.ndarray, pd.DatetimeIndex]:
    test_mask = (frame["block"] == "test").to_numpy()
    hidden_test = hidden[test_mask]
    y_test = frame.loc[test_mask, "y_true"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    dates_test = pd.DatetimeIndex(frame.loc[test_mask, "target_date"])
    keep = np.isfinite(hidden_test).all(axis=1) & np.isfinite(y_test)
    hidden_test = hidden_test[keep]
    y_test = y_test[keep]
    dates_test = dates_test[keep]
    scaled = StandardScaler().fit_transform(hidden_test)
    rows = []
    labels_by_k = {}
    for k in range(int(args.k_min), int(args.k_max) + 1):
        model = KMeans(n_clusters=k, n_init=20, random_state=int(args.seed))
        labels = model.fit_predict(scaled)
        labels_by_k[k] = labels
        sizes = np.bincount(labels, minlength=k)
        rows.append(
            {
                "k": int(k),
                "ARI": float(adjusted_rand_score(y_test, labels)),
                "NMI": float(normalized_mutual_info_score(y_test, labels)),
                "inertia": float(model.inertia_),
                "cluster_sizes": [int(size) for size in sizes],
                "n_months": int(len(y_test)),
            }
        )
    return rows, labels_by_k, hidden_test, y_test, dates_test


def bridge_to_approach5_clusters(
    hidden_by_origin: dict[int, np.ndarray],
    aligned: pd.DataFrame,
    latest: dict,
    args: argparse.Namespace,
) -> dict:
    idx = np.arange(int(latest["start_index"]), int(latest["end_index"]) + 1)
    hidden = np.vstack([hidden_by_origin[int(t)] for t in idx])
    series = list(latest["series"])
    corr = np.zeros((len(series), hidden.shape[1]), dtype=float)
    for i, name in enumerate(series):
        values = aligned[name].iloc[idx].to_numpy(dtype=float)
        for j in range(hidden.shape[1]):
            mask = np.isfinite(values) & np.isfinite(hidden[:, j])
            if mask.sum() < 12:
                continue
            x = values[mask]
            h = hidden[mask, j]
            if float(np.std(x)) == 0.0 or float(np.std(h)) == 0.0:
                continue
            corr[i, j] = float(np.corrcoef(x, h)[0, 1])
    k = int(latest["k"])
    model = KMeans(n_clusters=k, n_init=20, random_state=int(args.seed))
    labels = model.fit_predict(corr)
    reference = np.asarray(latest["labels"], dtype=int)
    ari = float(adjusted_rand_score(reference, labels))
    nmi = float(normalized_mutual_info_score(reference, labels))
    members = {}
    for label in sorted(set(labels)):
        members[str(int(label))] = [series[i] for i in range(len(series)) if int(labels[i]) == label]
    reference_members = {}
    for label in sorted(set(reference)):
        reference_members[str(int(label))] = [
            series[i] for i in range(len(series)) if int(reference[i]) == label
        ]
    return {
        "construction": (
            "Direct ARI between Option A indicator clusters and month-level h_t clusters is undefined. "
            "Each indicator is mapped to a vector of Pearson correlations between its aligned series and "
            f"each of the {hidden.shape[1]} hidden dimensions over the latest Option A 36-month window "
            f"({latest['start_date']:%Y-%m} to {latest['end_date']:%Y-%m}); those correlation vectors are "
            f"clustered with k={k}, the k of approach5's latest window, and compared with approach5's "
            "latest indicator labels. Both sides then partition indicators."
        ),
        "window_start": str(latest["start_date"].date()),
        "window_end": str(latest["end_date"].date()),
        "k": k,
        "n_indicators": int(len(series)),
        "ARI": ari,
        "NMI": nmi,
        "cluster_sizes": [int(size) for size in np.bincount(labels, minlength=k)],
        "members": members,
        "approach5_members": reference_members,
    }


def comparison_table(comparison: dict) -> Table:
    table = Table(
        title=f"Q3B test-block comparison (same {comparison['probit']['n']} months as approach5)"
    )
    for column in ("arm", "Brier mean", "Brier std", "AUC mean", "AUC std", "accuracy mean", "accuracy std"):
        table.add_column(column)
    for arm in ARM_ORDER:
        values = comparison[arm]
        table.add_row(
            arm,
            f"{values['Brier_mean']:.4f}",
            f"{values['Brier_std']:.4f}",
            "nan" if not np.isfinite(values["AUC_mean"]) else f"{values['AUC_mean']:.4f}",
            f"{values['AUC_std']:.4f}",
            )
    figure.update_xaxes(title_text="k", row=1, col=1)
    figure.update_yaxes(title_text="score", row=1, col=1)
    figure.update_xaxes(title_text="PC1", row=1, col=2)
    figure.update_yaxes(title_text="PC2", row=1, col=2)
    figure.update_layout(
        title="Q3B latent states of the final disciplined LSTM",
        template="plotly_white",
        hovermode="closest",
    )
    return figure


def write_html(figure: go.Figure, path: Path) -> None:
    figure.write_html(path, include_plotlyjs=True, full_html=True)


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = parse_args(argv)
    cfg = q3_config(args)
    log = RunLog(args.log_path)
    start_time = time.perf_counter()
    np.random.seed(args.seed)
    torch.manual_seed(args.seed)
    log.write(f"start args={vars(args)}")
    log.write(f"torch threads={torch.get_num_threads()} interop={torch.get_num_interop_threads()}")
    raw, meta, lags, series = q3.load_inputs(args.panel, args.meta)
    aligned = q3.align_information_set(raw, lags)
    meta_zero = zero_lag_meta(meta)
    aligned_zero = q3.align_information_set(raw, {name: 0 for name in lags})
    d = q3.build_label(aligned, cfg.threshold, "two_month")
    d_zero = q3.build_label(aligned_zero, cfg.threshold, "two_month")
    if not np.allclose(np.nan_to_num(d, nan=-1.0), np.nan_to_num(d_zero, nan=-1.0)):
        raise ValueError("zero-lag label differs from disciplined label")
    T = len(aligned)
    origins = np.arange(cfg.min_train, T - 1)
    test_start = int(cfg.min_train + cfg.tuning_months)
    tuning_origins = origins[origins < test_start]
    test_origins = origins[origins >= test_start]
    if len(tuning_origins) != cfg.tuning_months:
        raise ValueError("tuning block does not match requested length")
    if len(test_origins) == 0:
        raise ValueError("empty test block")
    seeds = [int(args.seed) + offset for offset in range(int(args.n_seeds))]
    log.write(
        f"panel rows={T}  origins={len(origins)}  tuning={len(tuning_origins)}  "
        f"test={len(test_origins)}  seeds={seeds}"
    )

    quarters = q3.quarter_records(aligned)
    chosen_rank, rank_summary = q3.select_rank_by_nowcast(aligned, quarters, tuning_origins, cfg)
    log.write(f"approach5 PCA rank selected on tuning block: {chosen_rank}")
    log.check_budget(args.time_budget_minutes, "probit rank selection")

    tuning_rows = []
    selected_setting = None
    selected_hp = None
    best_brier = float("inf")
    for setting, hp in enumerate(SETTINGS, start=1):
        seed_metrics = {}
        for seed in seeds:
            run = run_lstm_walk(
                aligned, d, tuning_origins, cfg, seed, hp, args, "tuning_lstm", log=log
            )
            metrics = q3.classification_metrics(run["frame"]["y_true"], run["frame"]["p"])
            seed_metrics[seed] = metrics
            if run["failed"]:
                log.write(f"tuning setting {setting} seed {seed} failed fits: {run['failed']}")
        brier_values = np.asarray([seed_metrics[seed]["Brier"] for seed in seeds], dtype=float)
        auc_values = np.asarray([seed_metrics[seed]["AUC"] for seed in seeds], dtype=float)
        row = {
            "setting": int(setting),
            "hidden": int(hp["hidden"]),
            "layers": int(hp["layers"]),
            "dropout": float(hp["dropout"]),
            "Brier_mean": float(np.nanmean(brier_values)),
            "Brier_std": float(np.nanstd(brier_values, ddof=0)),
            "AUC_mean": float(np.nanmean(auc_values)),
            "AUC_std": float(np.nanstd(auc_values, ddof=0)),
            "per_seed": {str(seed): seed_metrics[seed] for seed in seeds},
        }
        tuning_rows.append(row)
        log.write(
            f"tuning setting {setting} {hp}: Brier={row['Brier_mean']:.4f} "
            f"+- {row['Brier_std']:.4f} AUC={row['AUC_mean']:.4f}"
        )
        if row["Brier_mean"] < best_brier - 1e-12:
            best_brier = row["Brier_mean"]
            selected_setting = setting
            selected_hp = dict(hp)
        log.check_budget(args.time_budget_minutes, f"tuning setting {setting}")
    if selected_hp is None:
        raise RuntimeError("no LSTM setting could be evaluated")
    log.write(f"chosen setting {selected_setting}: {selected_hp}")
    console.print(tuning_table(tuning_rows, selected_setting))

    probit_walk = q3.walk_forward_probit(
        aligned, d, origins, cfg, chosen_rank, q3.MAIN_CONTROLS, test_start
    )
    probit_zero_walk = q3.walk_forward_probit(
        aligned_zero, d_zero, origins, cfg, chosen_rank, q3.MAIN_CONTROLS, test_start
    )
    log.write("probit baselines finished")
    log.check_budget(args.time_budget_minutes, "probit walk-forward")

    lstm_runs = {}
    run_meta = []
    for arm, arm_aligned, arm_labels, full_scaler in (
        ("lstm_disciplined", aligned, d, False),
        ("lstm_zero_lag", aligned_zero, d_zero, False),
        ("lstm_zero_lag_full_sample", aligned_zero, d_zero, True),
    ):
        lstm_runs[arm] = {}
        for seed in seeds:
            run = run_lstm_walk(
                arm_aligned,
                arm_labels,
                origins,
                cfg,
                seed,
                selected_hp,
                args,
                arm,
                full_sample_scaler=full_scaler,
                log=log,
            )
            lstm_runs[arm][seed] = run
            run_meta.append(
                {
                    "arm": arm,
                    "seed": int(seed),
                    "n_refits": int(len(run["refits"])),
                    "n_failed": int(len(run["failed"])),
                    "failed": run["failed"],
                }
            )
            log.write(
                f"{arm} seed {seed}: {len(run['refits'])} refits, {len(run['failed'])} failed"
            )
            log.check_budget(args.time_budget_minutes, f"{arm} seed {seed}")

    test_probit = probit_walk[probit_walk["block"] == "test"].sort_values("origin_index").reset_index(drop=True)
    test_probit_zero = probit_zero_walk[
        probit_zero_walk["block"] == "test"
    ].sort_values("origin_index").reset_index(drop=True)
    y_test = test_probit["y_true"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    origin_index = test_probit["origin_index"].to_numpy(dtype=int)
    target_dates = pd.DatetimeIndex(test_probit["target_date"])
    origin_dates = pd.DatetimeIndex(test_probit["origin_date"])
    if not np.allclose(
        test_probit_zero["y_true"].to_numpy(dtype=float), y_test, equal_nan=True
    ):
        raise ValueError("test targets differ between lag arms")

    arm_predictions: dict[str, dict[int, np.ndarray]] = {
        "probit": {int(args.seed): test_probit["p_probit"].to_numpy(dtype=float)},
        "probit_zero_lag": {int(args.seed): test_probit_zero["p_probit"].to_numpy(dtype=float)},
        "prior": {int(args.seed): test_probit["p_prior"].to_numpy(dtype=float)},
        "persistence": {int(args.seed): test_probit["p_persistence"].to_numpy(dtype=float)},
    }
    for arm in ("lstm_disciplined", "lstm_zero_lag", "lstm_zero_lag_full_sample"):
        arm_predictions[arm] = {}
        for seed in seeds:
            frame = lstm_runs[arm][seed]["frame"]
            test_frame = frame[frame["block"] == "test"].set_index("origin_index")
            test_frame = test_frame.reindex(origin_index)
            if not np.allclose(
                test_frame["y_true"].to_numpy(dtype=float), y_test, equal_nan=True
            ):
                raise ValueError(f"{arm} seed {seed} target rows do not align with probit")
            arm_predictions[arm][seed] = test_frame["p"].to_numpy(dtype=float)

    comparison = {}
    stochastic = {"lstm_disciplined", "lstm_zero_lag", "lstm_zero_lag_full_sample"}
    for arm in ARM_ORDER:
        per_seed = {
            seed: q3.classification_metrics(y_test, values)
            for seed, values in arm_predictions[arm].items()
        }
        comparison[arm] = summarise_arm(per_seed)
        comparison[arm]["stochastic"] = arm in stochastic
    console.print(comparison_table(comparison))

    seed_mean = {
        arm: np.nanmean(
            np.vstack([arm_predictions[arm][seed] for seed in sorted(arm_predictions[arm])]), axis=0
        )
        for arm in ARM_ORDER
    }
    leakage = {}
    for name, leaked_arm, disciplined_arm in LEAK_PAIRS:
        bootstrap = block_bootstrap_premium(
            y_test,
            seed_mean[leaked_arm],
            seed_mean[disciplined_arm],
            args.bootstrap_reps,
            args.bootstrap_block,
            args.seed,
        )
        leakage[name] = {
            "leaked_arm": leaked_arm,
            "disciplined_arm": disciplined_arm,
            "Brier_leaked": float(np.mean((seed_mean[leaked_arm] - y_test) ** 2)),
            "Brier_disciplined": float(np.mean((seed_mean[disciplined_arm] - y_test) ** 2)),
            **bootstrap,
        }
    console.print(leakage_table(leakage))

    first_seed_run = lstm_runs["lstm_disciplined"][int(args.seed)]
    latent_rows, labels_by_k, hidden_test, latent_y, latent_dates = latent_month_analysis(
        first_seed_run["hidden"], first_seed_run["frame"], args
    )
    console.print(latent_table(latent_rows))
    raw_cluster_labels, windows = q3.cluster_reference_panel(raw, cfg)
    if not windows:
        raise ValueError("approach5 clustering produced no windows")
    latest = windows[-1]
    hidden_by_origin = {
        int(row.origin_index): first_seed_run["hidden"][index]
        for index, row in enumerate(first_seed_run["frame"].itertuples())
    }
    bridge = bridge_to_approach5_clusters(hidden_by_origin, aligned, latest, args)
    console.print(
        rich_table(
            "Bridge to Option A latest indicator clusters",
            ["item", "value"],
            [
                ["latest window", f"{bridge['window_start']} to {bridge['window_end']}"],
                ["k (approach5 latest)", bridge["k"]],
                ["indicators", bridge["n_indicators"]],
                ["ARI vs approach5 labels", f"{bridge['ARI']:.4f}"],
                ["NMI vs approach5 labels", f"{bridge['NMI']:.4f}"],
                ["construction", bridge["construction"]],
            ],
        )
    )

    for meta_row in run_meta:
        failed_fits.extend(meta_row["failed"])

Q1B is close to SVI in median repricing on the same 470 OTM quotes (0.87% vs 0.82%) but much worse in the tail (p95 12.34% vs 5.45%; maximum 98.30% vs 17.37%), and it violates arbitrage on a denser grid outside its training collocation. Q2A passes the Black-Scholes and closed-form checks; the Asian control-variate variance ratio is 308x to 1974x across four futures, above the 5x benchmark. Q2B's deep policy has lower gross and net CVaR than daily Black-Scholes hedging on the brief P&L at zero and at 50 bp cost. Q3A beats the expanding prior on Brier score but not persistence (AUC 0.6928 vs 0.7390), and its nowcast beats a random-walk-with-drift benchmark in all periods, including ex-COVID. Q3B does not beat persistence either; the retrained LSTM never predicts a probability above 0.5 on the test block and its test AUC is 0.6422 versus 0.7390 for persistence.

# Advanced Programming 2026 Project Report

Hao Lu

## 1. Summary

The repository implements Q1, Q2 and Q3 of the Advanced Programming 2026 brief, options A and B of each. Q1 fits an arbitrage-free implied-volatility surface to CFFEX IO options, with SVI slices (Q1A) and a neural surface (Q1B). Q2 prices path-dependent payoffs under GBM by Monte Carlo (Q2A) and learns a CVaR-optimal hedge (Q2B). Q3 forecasts the PMI contraction regime with a classical probit/PCA model (Q3A) and an LSTM with leakage ablations (Q3B).

The results are mixed and are reported plainly. Q1A fits all 693 liquid date-expiry slices on the settle price and reaches zero butterfly and zero calendar violations at the 1e-8 tolerance on its audit grid, but 1 butterfly and 12 calendar checks remain strictly negative after repair. The median per-fit median repricing error is 0.77% on settle and 1.27% on close; the median per-fit maximum is 2.58% and 4.33%. Q1B is close to SVI in median repricing on the same 470 OTM quotes (0.87% vs 0.82%) but much worse in the tail (p95 12.34% vs 5.45%; maximum 98.30% vs 17.37%), and it violates arbitrage on a denser grid outside its training collocation. Q2A passes the Black-Scholes and closed-form checks; the Asian control-variate variance ratio is 308x to 1974x across four futures, above the 5x benchmark. Q2B's deep policy has lower gross and net CVaR than daily Black-Scholes hedging on the brief P&L at zero and at 50 bp cost. Q3A beats the expanding prior on Brier score but not persistence (AUC 0.6928 vs 0.7390), and its nowcast beats a random-walk-with-drift benchmark in all periods, including ex-COVID. Q3B does not beat persistence either; the retrained LSTM never predicts a probability above 0.5 on the test block and its test AUC is 0.6422 versus 0.7390 for persistence.

What was not achieved: Q1B is not globally arbitrage-free and is not competitive with SVI in the wings; Q2B covers only IF and uses one training seed; Q3A and Q3B do not reach the indicative AUC target of 0.75 or beat persistence. The data are daily, without bid-ask quotes or real-time macro vintages.

## 2. Environment and one-command reproduction

The project uses Python 3.13 under `uv` with pinned dependencies. From the repository root:

```bash
uv sync --python 3.13
source .venv/bin/activate
./reproduce.sh --quick   # tests + compare only
./reproduce.sh           # offline data check, tests, all approaches, post-hoc scripts, compare
python code/check_reproduction.py
```

`./reproduce.sh` runs `data/fetch.py --offline`, all tests, approach1 through approach6 including post-hoc scripts, and `compare.py`. The offline check verifies the nine committed clean artifacts against `data/metadata.json` and reports that all checksums match. The test suite ran 33 tests and passed.

The clean-clone check (`python code/check_reproduction.py`) compares `.cache/clean_clone_full/results` with the committed results. The cached clone predates three post-run commits: the `io_close` refresh, the Q3B `origin_date` label fix, and the Q1B cold-start addition. Each was checked separately: the refreshed `io_close` results match 6,972 numeric values exactly; the label fix was checked by parsed-JSON before/after comparison and no metric changed; the cold-start block was checked by two temporary runs with identical numbers excluding timings. The current checker reports 36,982 compared numeric values, all 36,982 exact, with maximum absolute and relative differences 0. It excludes `results/approach2/io/metrics.json` as historical, not rerun. The checker exits `FAIL` only because of key sets: `results/approach2/io_scaled/metrics.json` has 74 numeric keys only in the committed run (the cold-start block), and `results/approach6/macro/metrics.json` has 216 numeric keys only in the reproduced run (`history.refits[*].min_epochs` config echoes). There are zero numeric differences among shared keys.

The sum of committed `fit_seconds` is 4,668.2 s; excluding the historical Q1B run it is 3,869.8 s, about 64.5 minutes.

### 3.2 Q1 filtering, parity and implied volatility

Q1 uses the CFFEX `settle` field as the primary price and repeats the pipeline on `close`. There is no bid-ask snapshot, so liquidity is proxied by volume. Filters are volume >= 10, price >= 1, `|k| <= 0.20` and days-to-expiry >= 7. The volume floor stands in for a missing spread, the price floor removes near-zero quotes, the strike band keeps the fit local enough for a raw SVI slice, and the days floor avoids degenerate short tenors. On settle, sequential removals are 8,008 by volume, 1,303 by price, 1,380 by strike band and 606 by days, leaving 18,771 liquid quotes. There are 750 date-expiry groups, 728 with liquid quotes, 693 fits and 57 skipped groups (34 with fewer than six strikes, 23 with no liquid OTM quote). The OTM quote set has 11,146 quotes. Rate convention is `r(tau) = ln(1 + L/100 * tau * 365/360) / tau` from SHIBOR, linear in tenor and flat outside pillars. The forward is a volume-weighted mean of `F_K = K + (C-P)/DF` within `|ln(F_K / median(F_K))| <= 0.05`; `q = r - ln(F/S0)/T`.

### 3.3 Q3 panel, lags and revisions

The macro panel has 202 month-end observations and 34 series. Publication lags follow `F_t = {x_{i,s}: s + L_i <= t}`. Thirteen series have `L_i = 0` (market rates, yields, PMI and market-based series); twenty-one have `L_i = 1` (CPI, PPI, money, credit, trade, activity, GDP and similar). Most lags are conservative assumptions because the raw interfaces carry no genuine release date; lag zero is definitional only for market rates and yields. Jin10 announcement-date interfaces were saved but mostly stop in 2025 and are not used for the panel, except `macro_china_gdp_yearly` as a cross-check. GDP is derived from cumulative real levels and the current revised vintage: 79 quarters derived, 59 validation quarters, maximum absolute difference 0.83 percentage points and mean absolute difference 0.17 points. The data are the current revised vintage, not real-time vintages.

January and February are missing for: `retail_yoy` (Jan/Feb missing share 0.8824), `industrial_production_yoy` (Jan 1.000, Feb 0.7059), `fai_ytd_yoy` (Jan 1.000, Feb 0.1765), `electricity_yoy` (Jan 0.9412, Feb 0.000) and `industrial_profit_yoy` (Jan 1.000, Feb 0.000). ## 4. Q1 Option A: SVI surface

### 4.1 Model

For each date-expiry slice, with `k = ln(K/F)` and total variance `w = sigma^2 T`, the raw SVI form is `w(k) = a + b (rho (k-m) + sqrt((k-m)^2 + eta^2))`, with `b >= 0`, `|rho| < 1`, `eta > 0`, and bounds `a in [-2,2]`, `b in [0,5]`, `rho in [-0.999,0.999]`, `m in [-2,2]`, `eta in [0.01,1.0]`. Implied volatility is obtained by inverting the Black-76 price with `brentq` on `[1e-4,5]`. Fitting is bounded nonlinear least squares (`scipy.optimize.least_squares`, TRF, `x_scale="jac"`) with equal weights on liquid OTM quotes and eight documented starting points plus an optional warm start. Each raw fit is audited on `k in [-0.14,0.14]` step 0.01 with the correct Gatheral butterfly function `g(k) = (1 - k w'/(2w))^2 - (w'^2/4)(1/w + 1/4) + w''/2`, and with the printed form that omits `w''/2`. Calendar arbitrage is checked by linear interpolation of total variance in `T` at fixed `k`, requiring nondecreasing `w`. Violations are repaired by penalized refits at levels `1e2`, `1e4`, `1e6`, followed by a forward calendar repair against the previous expiry. Strict counts use `g<0`; tolerance counts use `g<-1e-8`.

## 11. Differences from the brief

1. **Butterfly formula.** The printed `g(k)` omits `w''/2`; the code uses the correct Gatheral form for decisions and reports both. On settle, raw strict violations are 8 with `w''/2` and 382 without; repaired strict violations are 1 and 390. On close, raw strict counts are 23 and 418; repaired strict counts are 3 and 423. Source: `results/approach1/io/metrics.json`, `results/approach1/io_close/metrics.json`.
2. **Hedging P&L.** The printed brief P&L omits the financing cost of the stock position, so it is not exactly self-financing. The brief-minus-self-financing CVaR gap is -0.1796 for daily BS at kappa 0 and -0.2094 for the deep policy at kappa 0; the mean across all cells is -0.1960. The negative sign means the brief formula reports lower CVaR than the self-financing formula. Source: `results/approach4/IF/metrics.json`.
3. **GBM drift.** The brief specifies drift `r`; the code follows the brief. A futures price has zero drift under Q, so this is a modelling simplification, recorded in `params.drift_note`. Source: `results/approach3/IF/metrics.json`.
4. **No bid-ask data.** Daily CFFEX data have no bid-ask spread, so volume >= 10 stands in for liquidity/spread. On settle this filter removes 8,008 quotes; the full sequential filter removes 11,297. Source: `results/approach1/io/metrics.json`.
5. **LSTM refit frequency.** Q3B refits the LSTM every six months and reuses the last refit between refits; Q3A refits the probit monthly. Source: `results/approach6/macro/metrics.json`.
6. **Cluster bridge.** Q3A clusters partition indicators, while the LSTM's month-level `h_t` clusters partition months, so a direct ARI is undefined. The bridge maps each indicator to a correlation vector with the 16 hidden dimensions and clusters those vectors with `k=9`; the resulting ARI may be partly mechanical because `h_t` is computed from those indicators. Source: `results/approach6/macro/metrics.json`.
7. **SVI eta bounds.** The current bounds are `[0.01,1.0]`, narrower than the legacy `[1e-6,2.0]`. This changes bound hits but not median RMSE materially. Source: `results/approach1/io/metrics.json`.
8. **Q1B sample date.** Q1B uses 2024-03-14, while the metadata sample date is 2024-03-15. The selection rule chooses the nearest mid-month date with at least 80% of the month's maximum quote count. Source: `results/approach2/io_scaled/metrics.json`.
9. **Q3B inputs.** The LSTM excludes `gdp_yoy` from the 12-month input panel to avoid a mixed-frequency quarterly series; the probit also excludes it from the factors. Source: `results/approach6/macro/metrics.json`.
10. **Q2B scope.** Only IF is used, with one training seed and no terminal unwind; the brief permits this but it limits generalisation. Source: `results/approach4/IF/metrics.json`.
11. **Individual submission.** This is an individual submission rather than a group submission.
12. **AI-drafted report.** The report was drafted by AI rather than written by a group, with instructor approval as stated by the author in Section 14.
13. **Only IO options.** Only CFFEX IO options are used for the surface; SSE ETF options are not fitted. Source: `data/metadata.json` and `results/approach1/io/metrics.json`.
14. **Parity forward.** `q` is replaced by the put-call parity forward: `q = r - ln(F/S0)/T` with `F` estimated from parity, rather than a dividend model. Source: `results/approach1/io/metrics.json`.
15. **FastboxData not used.** FastboxData was not used as a data source.

## 12. Limitations

- SVI and neural fits are audited only on the reported grids. The neural surface has 30 butterfly and 4 calendar violations on the dense grid outside its training collocation, so it must not be called globally arbitrage-free. SVI is not proved arbitrage-free off the audit grid either.
- Both models are weak in the wings and at short tenors: Q1A settle worst per-fit max repricing is 0.3251 and close is 0.2624; Q1B wing p95 is 0.7809 and max 1.519, versus SVI 0.5592.
- SVI fits frequently sit on the eta bounds (31 lower and 67 upper on settle; 72 lower and 46 upper on close), and the cause is not established.
- Main-contract futures series have no roll flags. The fields named `roll_jump` in `metrics.json` are tail-return counts (IF 106, CU 113, RB 131, SC 119), not identified roll dates.
- Q2B used one training seed, only IF, no terminal unwind cost, and no previous position in the policy inputs; it cannot represent a no-trade region.
- Macro data are current revised vintages, not real-time vintages. Most publication lags are conservative assumptions, not observed release dates. GDP is derived from cumulative real levels (79 derived quarters; validation maximum absolute difference 0.83 points).
- The retrained LSTM never exceeds 0.5 on the test block (maximum 0.3172) and does not beat persistence (Brier 0.2561 vs 0.2286; AUC 0.6422 vs 0.7390). Its accuracy is the all-negative rate.
- The PCA rank is chosen on 12 quarterly nowcast observations; the test block is short for regime classification, and the AUC intervals are wide (for example, the original probit minus persistence interval is `[-0.2375, 0.03518]`).
- The Q3 nowcast month-3 ex-COVID error is higher than month-1; the paired interval includes zero, and no cause is asserted.
- The Q3 clustering is unstable across windows (adjacent ARI median 0.1648) and is descriptive only.
- The Q1B per-tenor table comes from `NOTES_OPEN_ISSUES.md`, not from a committed `metrics.json`.

## 6. Q2 Option A: Monte Carlo pricing

### 6.1 Model and estimators

Under the brief's GBM, `dS_t = r S_t dt + sigma S_t dW_t`, with `S0` the last close, `K=S0`, `T=1`, `m=252`, barrier `B=1.3 S0`, and `r` the SHIBOR zero at `T`. A futures price has zero drift under Q; the brief specifies drift `r`, so the code follows the brief and flags this as a modelling simplification. `sigma` is the standard deviation of daily log returns times `sqrt(252)` on a five-year window. The payoffs are arithmetic Asian `max(mean(S_{t_i})-K,0)`, discretely monitored up-and-out `max(S_T-K,0) * 1{max S_{t_i}<B}`, cash-or-nothing digital `1{S_T>K}`, and European `max(S_T-K,0)`. All are discounted by `exp(-rT)`.

Estimators are naive Monte Carlo, antithetic `(Z,-Z)` at equal path count, a control variate using the discrete geometric Asian closed form with `ln G ~ N(ln S0 + (r-sigma^2/2)T(m+1)/(2m), sigma^2 T (m+1)(2m+1)/(6m^2))`, and control variate plus antithetic. The control-variate beta is estimated on an independent pilot of 100,000 paths so the estimator is unbiased. European and Asian delta/vega use pathwise estimators; digital and barrier use likelihood-ratio estimators because pathwise is invalid at discontinuities. Finite differences use common random numbers and relative bumps `h in {0.1, 0.01, 0.001}` for spot and sigma. European and digital references are closed form; Asian and barrier references are high-precision control-variate estimates (524,288 paths per dataset, 2,097,152 paths in the IF study). The convergence study uses `N = 2^10` to `2^16`, 30 replications and a `2^22` reference.

The digital antithetic ratio is strongly dataset-dependent. Table 21 reports the drift `r`, volatility `sigma`, the derived quantity `r - sigma^2/2` and the ratio. Source: `results/approach3/{IF,CU,RB,SC}/metrics.json`.

| dataset | r | sigma | r - sigma^2/2 (derived) | digital antithetic ratio |

Hypothesis, supported by the ordering but not proved: for an ATM digital, when `r - sigma^2/2` is near zero, a `Z, -Z` pair almost always has exactly one in-the-money leg, so the pair mean is nearly constant. CU has the value closest to zero and the largest ratio; SC has the most negative value and the smallest ratio. This is an explanation of the ordering, not a tested theorem.

### 6.3 Discussion and limitations

The Asian control variate is very effective because the geometric Asian is strongly correlated with the arithmetic payoff. The barrier control variate is weak: control-variate ratios are 1.008 to 1.055, while CV+antithetic ratios are 1.162 to 1.624. Finite differences are noisy for discontinuous payoffs: barrier vega RMSE grows from 59.87 at `h=0.1` to 670.0 at `h=0.001`, so smaller bumps do not help. The roll-jump counts in Table 14 are tail-return counts above the reported threshold, not identified roll dates; the main-contract series carry no roll flags. The calibration uses a five-year window and is sensitive to the large returns retained in the sample. The GBM drift is `r` as specified, not the zero drift of a futures price under Q.

## 7. Q2 Option B: deep hedging

### 7.1 Model

The hedge is a European ATM call on IF with `S0=100`, `K=100`, `T=0.25`, `m=63`, `sigma=0.1911` (the Q2A five-year IF calibration) and `r=0.01417` (SHIBOR zero at `T`). The policy is a small MLP with two hidden layers of 32 units mapping `(S_t/S0, t/T)` to a delta in `[0,1]` through a sigmoid; it does not see the previous position. The objective is empirical CVaR at 0.95 of `-V_T`, the mean of the worst 5% of losses per batch. Training uses `2^17` paths, batches of `2^12`, 100 epochs, Adam at learning rate 0.005, and one policy per cost `kappa in {0,10,50}` bp. The same network initialization is used for every kappa. Validation uses three independent seeds with `2^17` paths each; training uses one seed (42).

The brief P&L is `V_T = sum_t exp(r(T-t)) D_t (S_{t+1}-S_t) - kappa sum_t |D_t-D_{t-1}| S_t - payoff`, with `D_{-1}=0` and no terminal unwind. The self-financing P&L is `V_T = sum_t exp(r(T-t-dt)) D_t (S_{t+1}-exp(r dt) S_t) - kappa sum_t exp(r(T-t)) |D_t-D_{t-1}| S_t - payoff`. The brief formula omits the financing cost of the stock position. Training uses the brief P&L; evaluation reports both. Net CVaR is CVaR minus the future value of the Black-Scholes premium. Benchmarks are Black-Scholes deltas rebalanced every 1, 5 and 21 days at the same kappas, on the same validation paths.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 4.781 | 4.679 | 0.7838 | 0.6817 |
| 50 | 6.971 | 6.083 | 2.974 | 2.085 |

On the brief P&L, the deep policy lowers gross CVaR by 0.10 at kappa 0 and by 0.89 at kappa 50; net CVaR falls by the same amounts because the premium is common. The deep policy has higher variance than daily BS at kappa 0 (0.2323 vs 0.1815 brief; 0.2370 vs 0.1733 self-financing) and lower variance at kappa 50 (0.3018 vs 0.4371 brief; 0.3178 vs 0.4273 self-financing). A plausible cause of the CVaR gain is that the policy optimizes CVaR directly rather than following a delta rule, but the experiment does not isolate optimization from the state-dependent delta; that is a hypothesis.

The brief-minus-self-financing CVaR gap is negative everywhere: -0.1796 for BS daily at kappa 0, -0.2094 for the deep policy at kappa 0, and -0.2486 for the deep policy at kappa 50; the mean across all cells is -0.1960. The negative sign means the brief formula reports lower CVaR than the self-financing formula. Training CVaR falls from 11.01 to 4.70 (kappa 0), 11.08 to 4.98 (kappa 10) and 11.32 to 6.13 (kappa 50).

Figures: `results/approach4/IF/training.html` and `results/approach4/IF/policy.html`.

### 7.3 Discussion and limitations

The deep hedge improves CVaR over daily BS on the brief basis at all three costs, with lower turnover at higher cost. The gap is systematic and is larger for the deep policy at high cost. A plausible explanation, not tested here, is that the omitted stock financing scales with the position and the position is held through the path. The training used one seed only; three validation seeds reduce evaluation noise but do not establish training robustness. The study covers only IF, uses no terminal unwind cost, and the policy cannot represent a no-trade region because the previous position is not an input.

## 8. Q3 Option A: classical probit

### 8.1 Model and protocol

The information set is implemented by shifting each series forward by its lag `L_i`: row `t` contains only values public at the end of month `t`. The label is `d_t = 1{PMI_t < 50 and PMI_{t-1} < 50}`. The model is `P(d_{t+1}=1) = Phi(beta' z_t)`, where `z_t` contains an intercept, the first `r` principal components of the standardized aligned factor panel (excluding `gdp_yoy`, `cgb10y`, `spread_10y_2y`, `shibor_3m`) and the controls `cgb10y` and `spread_10y_2y`. PCA and standardization use only rows public at the origin; missing values become zero after standardization; series with under 50% training-window coverage are dropped. The probit is fitted by maximum likelihood with a ridge of `1e-4` and a Newton/BFGS fallback. Validation is expanding walk-forward, refit monthly, minimum 60 training months, a 36-month tuning block and a test block of 105 origins from 2018-01-31 to 2026-09-30. The PCA rank is chosen on the tuning block by cross-validated nowcast RMSE at month 3 of the quarter.

The nowcast is `y_q = b0 + b' fbar_q`, where `fbar_q` averages the aligned factors over the months of the quarter elapsed by `t`; training quarters are those with GDP public by `t`. The benchmark is a random walk with drift estimated from the same information set. Clustering uses rolling 36-month correlations, `d_ij = sqrt(2(1-rho_ij))`, Ward linkage, `k` chosen by silhouette, adjacent-window adjusted Rand indices, and lead-lag correlations with GDP.

def load_data(options_path: Path, shibor_path: Path, metadata_path: Path) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, dict]:
    options = pd.read_csv(options_path, parse_dates=["date", "expiry"])
    shibor = pd.read_csv(shibor_path, parse_dates=["date"]).sort_values("date").reset_index(drop=True)
    metadata = json.loads(metadata_path.read_text())

    required_options = {"date", "contract", "expiry", "cp", "K", "open", "high", "low", "close", "settle", "volume", "oi", "S"}
    required_shibor = {"date", *PILLAR_DAYS.keys()}
    missing_options = required_options - set(options.columns)
    missing_shibor = required_shibor - set(shibor.columns)
    if missing_options:
        raise ValueError(f"options file missing columns: {sorted(missing_options)}")
    if missing_shibor:
        raise ValueError(f"shibor file missing columns: {sorted(missing_shibor)}")

    checks = {
        "rows": len(options),
        "duplicate_date_contract": int(options.duplicated(["date", "contract"]).sum()),
        "nonpositive_K": int((options.K <= 0).sum()),
        "expiry_not_after_date": int((options.expiry <= options.date).sum()),
        "missing_quotes": int(options[["close", "settle", "volume", "S"]].isna().sum().sum()),
    }
    if any(checks[key] for key in ("duplicate_date_contract", "nonpositive_K", "expiry_not_after_date", "missing_quotes")):
        raise ValueError(f"data verification failed: {checks}")
    if options.groupby(["date", "expiry", "K"]).cp.nunique().max() != 2:
        raise ValueError("some date/expiry/strike groups do not contain both C and P")

    return options, shibor, metadata

def select_sample_dates(options: pd.DataFrame, metadata: dict) -> tuple[list[pd.Timestamp], list[dict]]:
    metadata_dates = [pd.Timestamp(item) for item in metadata.get("sample_dates", [])]
    months = sorted(dict.fromkeys(item.strftime("%Y-%m") for item in metadata_dates))
    if len(months) != 6:
        raise ValueError(f"expected 6 sample months from metadata, got {months}")
    counts = options.groupby([options.date.dt.strftime("%Y-%m"), "date"]).size()
    selected: list[pd.Timestamp] = []
    rows: list[dict] = []
    for month in months:
        series = counts.loc[month]
        maximum = int(series.max())
        threshold = 0.8 * maximum
        eligible = series[series >= threshold]
        mid = pd.Timestamp(f"{month}-15")
        eligible_dates = [pd.Timestamp(item) for item in eligible.index]
        chosen = min(eligible_dates, key=lambda item: (abs((item - mid).days), item))
        metadata_date = next((item for item in metadata_dates if item.strftime("%Y-%m") == month), None)
        selected.append(chosen)
        rows.append({
            "month": month,
            "max_quotes": maximum,
            "threshold_80pct": threshold,
            "eligible_dates": len(eligible),
            "date": chosen.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"),
            "date_rows": int(series.loc[chosen]),
            "days_from_mid_month": int(abs((chosen - mid).days)),
            "metadata_date": metadata_date.strftime("%Y-%m-%d") if metadata_date is not None else None,
            "matches_metadata": bool(metadata_date is not None and metadata_date == chosen),
        })
    return selected, rows

## 2. Cross-question dependencies in code

After the split, all these dependencies stay inside the same repository; none crosses repositories.

| Dependency | Used for | Handling |
|---|---|---|
| Q1B → Q1A code | `approach2_q1b_neural.py` loads `approach1_q1a_svi.py` by `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` for loaders, forwards, filters, IV inversion, SVI functions, bounds, Black price, `to_jsonable`, `rel_path` | both files stay in Q1; paths unchanged |
| Q1B → Q1A results | reads `results/approach1/io/svi_params.csv` for warm starts and the like-for-like comparison | keep `results/approach1/io`; reproduce Q1A before Q1B |
| Q1B cold-start → Q1B/Q1A | imports Q1B, reuses Q1A functions, reads reference starts from Q1A results | both stay in Q1; reproduce order: Q1A settle/close → Q1B neural → Q1B cold-start |
| Q2B → Q2A code | `approach2_q2b_deephedge.py` loads `approach1_q2a_mc.py` for `load_futures`, `calibration_stats`, `load_shibor`, `build_rate_curves`, `zero_rate` | update `APPROACH3_PATH`/loader name; both stay in Q2 |
| Q2B → Q2A results | reads `results/approach1/IF/metrics.json` to verify `params.sigma` against the Q2A calibration; if absent it would silently skip that check | keep Q2A result file; update `APPROACH3_METRICS` to `results/approach1/IF/metrics.json`; reproduce Q2A before Q2B |
| Q2A → SHIBOR | rates for all four futures | shared `data/clean/shibor.csv` copied into Q2 |
| Q3B → Q3A code | `approach2_q3b_sequence.py` imports `approach1_q3a_classical` and calls `load_inputs`, `align_information_set`, `build_label`, `quarter_records`, `select_rank_by_nowcast`, `walk_forward_probit`, `classification_metrics`, `cluster_reference_panel`, `RunConfig`, `MAIN_CONTROLS`, `to_jsonable` | update import/module name; both stay in Q3 |
| Q3B → Q3A results | **none**: Q3B recomputes the probit from the panel; it does not read Q3A `metrics.json` | no result-file dependency to preserve |
| Q3A post-hoc → Q3A code/results | imports Q3A; reads `results/approach1/macro/metrics.json`, `probit_walkforward.csv`, `nowcast_paths.csv`; writes back into the same `metrics.json` | keep paths; reproduce Q3A before its post-hoc |
| Q3B post-hoc → Q3A code/Q3B code/results | imports both; reads `results/approach2/macro/metrics.json` and `predictions.csv`; writes `post_hoc_*` files | keep paths; reproduce Q3B before its post-hoc |
| Q1A → raw CFFEX/legacy | forward check reads `data/raw/cffex/`; eta-bound comparison reads `data/legacy/` | Q1-only snapshots copied |
| Q2A/Q2B → clean futures/SHIBOR | Q2 data | Q2-only futures plus shared SHIBOR |
| Q3 → macro panel/meta | Q3 data | Q3-only clean panel/meta |

Important non-dependency: Q2A only reimplements the SHIBOR zero-rate convention; it does not import Q1 code. Q3 does not import Q1/Q2 code. So there is no cross-repository Python import after the split.

## 3. Data `fetch.py` and `metadata.json` split

`--offline` is entirely metadata-driven: it loads `data/metadata.json`, iterates `artifacts`, and checks `sha256(ROOT / relative)` against the stored hash. Therefore the rule is: copy artifacts byte-for-byte, copy their metadata entries unchanged, and list only files present in that repository.

| Repo | `fetch.py` retained content | CLI | `metadata.json` artifacts |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 | shared helpers + CFFEX/CSI/Sina fetch, option build, SHIBOR build, sample dates, assertions, offline | `--online`, `--offline` | `options_io.csv`, `shibor.csv`, `sina_comparison.csv` |
| Q2 | shared helpers + futures fetch/normalize/verify/metadata/assertions, offline | `--futures`, `--offline` | `futures_IF.csv`, `futures_RB.csv`, `futures_CU.csv`, `futures_SC.csv`, `shibor.csv` |
| Q3 | shared helpers + Q3 raw inspection/fetch, macro panel build, Q3 checks/metadata, offline | `--q3-fetch`, `--q3`, `--offline` | `macro_panel.csv`, `macro_meta.csv`, `shibor.csv` |

Metadata details:
- Q1 keeps `sample_dates`, `sample_month_report`, `sample_date_report`, `build_stats`, `assertions`, and `csi_source` because Q1B reads `sample_dates` and records the sample reports. It drops futures/macro artifacts, `futures_assertions`, and `q3`.
- Q2 keeps `futures_assertions` and futures/SHIBOR interfaces; it drops Q1/Q3 artifacts and `q3`.
- Q3 keeps the whole `q3` block, Q3/SHIBOR interfaces, and the macro artifacts; it drops Q1/Q2 artifacts and assertions.
- No `sha256` or `rows` value is recomputed or edited. Only the set of artifact keys and non-artifact interface blocks changes.
- Shared `shibor.csv` is copied byte-for-byte; its metadata entry is identical in all three.
- Validation: in each repository run `python data/fetch.py --offline` and require exit 0 with “all checksums match”. No `--online`, `--futures`, or `--q3` run in the split repositories, so no snapshot is rewritten.
- Fallback: if a trimmed `fetch.py` fails its smoke test, I will leave the full parent `fetch.py` unchanged in that repository; `--offline` still works because metadata is filtered. This does not affect model numbers.

### Clone and filter
For each question:
1. Fresh clone from `../ap2026` inside this folder, using:
   `DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer`,
   `GIT_EXEC_PATH=$DEVELOPER_DIR/usr/libexec/git-core`,
   `GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR=$DEVELOPER_DIR/usr/share/git-core/templates`.
2. Verify `HEAD == submission == 4521da3`; remove `origin`.
3. Install `git-filter-repo` into `ap2026-split/.tools/venv` (no global install) and run `git filter-repo` with the per-question path set and renames.
4. Copy `.git/filter-repo/commit-map` out before adding split commits.
5. Add the split commit(s), re-tag, and generate `SPLIT_HISTORY.md`.

### First commit and shared commits
- Every repository retains the original root commit `7ee9a86` (AGENTS) and scaffold `bc857ec`, rewritten by filter-repo. There is no synthetic “initial import” commit; a synthetic root would discard the requested history.
- Question-specific history begins at `867a243` for Q1, `5f007e6` for Q2, `4fc1d10` for Q3.
- Because AGENTS/README/pyproject/uv/fetch/metadata/report/SESSION/compare/check/reproduce are shared files, 23 of the 48 commits survive in all three repositories. They receive a different new hash in each repository.
- Surviving commit counts: Q1 34, Q2 29, Q3 31. Unique commits: Q1 11, Q2 6, Q3 8. Pruned commits: Q1 14, Q2 19, Q3 17.
- Some shared commit subjects survive in the “wrong” repository only through a common file: for example, `0b680be feat: Q1A SVI pipeline` survives in Q2/Q3 because it also adds `uv.toml`/README, and `5f007e6 data: add Q2 futures snapshot` survives in Q1/Q3 because it also edits `fetch.py`/`metadata.json`. I will not rewrite subjects; `SPLIT_HISTORY.md` will mark these as “shared via common files”.
- `git filter-repo` maps pruned commits to all-zero hashes. The commit map will have all 48 parent commits per repository: `old_hash`, `subject`, `new_hash` or `0000`, and a disposition note.

### Disclosure and tags

- The final commit message will be e.g. `split: extract Q1 repository from combined ap2026 submission`, with the parent tag/commit in the body.
- Final tag `submission` will point at the split HEAD. I will keep `parent-submission` at the filtered version of `4521da3` for audit.
- No original commit hashes can be preserved; the maps are the audit trail.

## 6. Risks, runtime, and limits

### Estimated runtime

| Repository | Main committed/expected compute | Estimate |
|---|---|---:|
| Q1 | Q1A settle 764.7 s, Q1A close 630.1 s, Q1B 1,638.0 s, cold-start ~30 s, tests/compare | 55–60 min |
| Q2 | Q2A ~98 s, Q2B ~732 s, tests/compare | 14–16 min |
| Q3 | Q3A ~4 s, Q3B ~49 s, Q3B post-hoc retrain ~65 s, diagnostics/tests/compare | 3–6 min |
| Setup | local filter-repo, three clones/filters, metadata/report edits, `uv sync` | 20–30 min |
| Verification | one clean-clone full run per repo, numeric comparison | included above |
| **Total** | | **~75–85 min compute; ~2–2.5 h wall including setup/report/verification** |

Disk estimate: roughly 6–10 GB under `ap2026-split` for filtered clones, three venvs/clean clones, results, and caches; the machine has ample space.

### Main risks and mitigations
- `git filter-repo` is not installed. Install only into `ap2026-split/.tools/venv` with caches inside this folder; no global/user install.
- `git clone` fails without the Xcode env vars. Set all three explicitly; use `--no-local` so no hardlinks point back to `../ap2026`.
- Any accidental write outside this folder: set `TMPDIR`, `HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, `UV_CACHE_DIR`, `UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR`, `PIP_CACHE_DIR`, `TORCH_HOME` inside the workspace; use `--no-cache-dir` for pip.
- Offline checksum failure: copy artifacts with git/filter-repo, never re-serialize CSVs; only edit metadata JSON. Smoke-test every repo’s `data/fetch.py --offline`.
- Numeric drift after renaming: preserve JSON keys/labels; edit only executable path/module references. Gate on all shared numeric values in `metrics.json` with the parent’s `flatten`/timing-ignore logic, requiring zero numeric differences; report known extra-key cases separately.
- Q1B is the long pole and historically had multiprocessing/autograd stalls. Run it from the clean clone with the same `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`/worker setup as the parent; if it fails, do not change parameters, re-run the same clean-clone step and report.
- Q2B depends on Q2A’s `metrics.json` sigma check; if Q2A is not run first, Q2B will fail. Preserve reproduce order.
- `compare.py` and `check_reproduction.py` cannot be copied unchanged into Q2/Q3 and used naively: `compare.py` must be split; `check_reproduction.py` can stay unchanged for self-checks, but parent comparison needs a path map (Q2 `approach3/4 → approach1/2`; Q3 `approach5/6 → approach1/2`). I will use a read-only wrapper reusing its comparator, not alter the original checker.
- Report split is editorial, not a pure git operation. Risk of dropping a caveat or changing a number; mitigate with section extraction and numeric-token checks against the parent.
- `SESSION.md` as a full copy makes each repository larger (~6.5 MB) and contains other questions’ sessions; this is intentional provenance. If you prefer per-question extracts, that requires transcript-level editing and a separate approval.
- Parent `results/comparison.html` is a combined artifact and cannot be preserved unchanged; each repo gets a regenerated per-question HTML.
- Parent commit hashes/tags cannot be preserved; maps and `parent-submission` are the audit trail.

### Things that cannot be done cleanly
- Shared-file history (`fetch.py`, `metadata.json`, `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `report.md`, `SESSION.md`, `reproduce.sh`, `compare.py`, `check_reproduction.py`) cannot be made purely per-question; those commits survive in multiple repos with different hashes and sometimes misleading subjects. Disclosed in the map.
- Q2/Q3 raw data caches (`data/raw/futures_*`, `data/raw/q3`) were gitignored and are absent from the tag. The split repos will be offline-verifiable but not online-rebuildable without refetching; I will not add new raw files to history.
- Q1B `results/approach2/io` is a committed historical run and is not rerun; its numbers remain historical.
- Q3B’s clean run adds known `history.refits[*].min_epochs` config echoes not present in the committed parent metrics. This is the same parent clean-clone discrepancy; all shared numeric values still match.
- `SESSION.md` cannot be split by question without transcript editing; full copy is the clean option.
- Exact original commit hashes, tag hashes, and aggregate `comparison.html` cannot be retained.

### Proposed defaults for approval
1. Q2/Q3 result directories are renamed to `results/approach1/` and `results/approach2/`; Q1 stays as-is.
2. `data/fetch.py` is trimmed per question, with full-file fallback only on smoke-test failure.
3. `SESSION.md` is the full parent export in all three.
4. Each repo gets one extra `SPLIT_HISTORY.md` with the full commit map.
5. Final tag `submission` on split HEAD; `parent-submission` retained for audit.

Stopping here for approval.

def online():
    RAW.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    CLEAN.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    import akshare as ak

    session = requests.Session()
    fetch_cffex(session)
    fetch_csi300()
    fetch_ak_csv("Shibor", RAW / "shibor.csv", ak.macro_china_shibor_all)
    fetch_ak_csv("LPR", RAW / "lpr.csv", ak.macro_china_lpr)
    fetch_ak_csv("SSE option current day", RAW / "option_current_day_sse.csv", ak.option_current_day_sse)
    fetch_etf("510050")
    fetch_etf("510300")

    csi, csi_source = load_csi()
    options, build_stats = build_options(csi)
    shibor = build_shibor()
    options.to_csv(CLEAN / "options_io.csv", index=False, encoding="utf-8")
    shibor.to_csv(CLEAN / "shibor.csv", index=False, encoding="utf-8")
    sample_dates = choose_sample_dates(options)
    sina = fetch_sina_comparison(options, sample_dates)
    sina.to_csv(CLEAN / "sina_comparison.csv", index=False, encoding="utf-8")
    assertions = run_assertions(options, shibor, sample_dates, csi)
    month_report, date_report = write_metadata(
        options, shibor, sina, csi_source, build_stats, sample_dates, assertions
    )
    print_report(month_report, date_report, sina, build_stats, assertions)
    failed = [item["name"] for item in assertions if not item["passed"]]
    futures_results, futures_assertions = fetch_futures()
    update_futures_metadata(futures_results, futures_assertions)
    print_futures_report(futures_results, futures_assertions)
    failed += [
        f"{item['dataset']} futures"
        for item in futures_assertions
        if not (
            item["at_least_5_years"]
            and item["no_duplicate_dates"]
            and item["positive_prices"]
        )
    ]
    if failed:
        log.error("assertion failures: %s", failed)
        return 1
    log.info("online fetch complete; all assertions passed")
    return 0


def futures_only():
    RAW.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    CLEAN.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    futures_results, futures_assertions = fetch_futures()
    update_futures_metadata(futures_results, futures_assertions)
    print_futures_report(futures_results, futures_assertions)
    failed = [
        f"{item['dataset']} futures"
        for item in futures_assertions
        if not (
            item["at_least_5_years"]
            and item["no_duplicate_dates"]
            and item["positive_prices"]
        )
    ]
    if failed:
        log.error("assertion failures: %s", failed)
        return 1
    log.info("futures fetch complete; all assertions passed")
    return 0


def offline():
    if not METADATA.exists():
        log.error("metadata missing: %s", METADATA)
        return 1
    metadata = json.loads(METADATA.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    artifacts = metadata.get("artifacts", {})
    if not artifacts:
        log.error("metadata contains no artifacts")
        return 1
    failed = []
    for relative, info in artifacts.items():
        path = ROOT / relative
        if not path.exists():
            log.error("OFFLINE missing %s", relative)
            failed.append(relative)
            continue
        actual = sha256(path)
        expected = info.get("sha256")
        if actual != expected:
            log.error("OFFLINE checksum mismatch %s expected=%s actual=%s", relative, expected, actual)
            failed.append(relative)
        else:
            log.info("OFFLINE OK %s rows=%s sha256=%s", relative, info.get("rows"), actual)
    if failed:
        return 1
    log.info("offline verification complete; all checksums match")
    return 0


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Fetch Q1 option, index and rates data")
    group = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
    group.add_argument("--online", action="store_true", help="download missing raw data and rebuild clean artifacts")
    group.add_argument("--offline", action="store_true", help="verify clean artifacts against metadata checksums")
    group.add_argument("--futures", action="store_true", help="fetch or refresh only the Q2 futures snapshots")
    group.add_argument("--q3-fetch", action="store_true", help="fetch only the Q3 macro raw snapshots")
    group.add_argument("--q3", action="store_true", help="fetch and build the Q3 macro panel and metadata")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s")
    if args.online:
        return online()
    if args.offline:
        return offline()
    if args.q3_fetch:
        fetch_q3_raw()
        return 0
    if args.q3:
        return q3_run()
    return futures_only()


if __name__ == "__main__":

def build_artifact(path: Path, source: str, interface: str, schema: list[str], rows: int) -> dict:
    return {
        "path": str(path.relative_to(ROOT)),
        "source": source,
        "interface": interface,
        "retrieval_time": datetime.now().astimezone().isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
        "schema": schema,
        "rows": rows,
        "sha256": sha256(path),
    }


def write_metadata(
    options: pd.DataFrame,
    shibor: pd.DataFrame,
    sina: pd.DataFrame,
    csi_source: str,
    build_stats: dict,
    sample_dates: list[str],
    assertions: list[dict],
):
    import akshare

    month_report = []
    for month in SAMPLE_MONTHS:
        subset = options[options["date"].str.startswith(month)] if not options.empty else options
        month_report.append(
            {
                "month": month,
                "trading_days": int(subset["date"].nunique()) if not subset.empty else 0,
                "rows": int(len(subset)),
            }
        )
    date_report = []
    for day in sample_dates:
        subset = options[options["date"] == day]
        date_report.append(
            {
                "date": day,
                "rows": int(len(subset)),
                "expiries": int(subset["expiry"].nunique()),
            }
        )
    metadata = {
        "created_at": datetime.now().astimezone().isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
        "akshare_version": akshare.__version__,
        "artifacts": {
            "data/clean/options_io.csv": build_artifact(
                CLEAN / "options_io.csv",
                f"CFFEX IO daily quotes; CSI 300 close from {csi_source}",
                "http://www.cffex.com.cn/sj/hqsj/rtj/ + akshare index interfaces",
                OPTION_COLUMNS,
                len(options),
            ),
            "data/clean/shibor.csv": build_artifact(
                CLEAN / "shibor.csv",
                "China Shibor",
                "akshare.macro_china_shibor_all",
                SHIBOR_COLUMNS,
                len(shibor),
            ),
            "data/clean/sina_comparison.csv": build_artifact(
                CLEAN / "sina_comparison.csv",
                "CFFEX close vs Sina option daily close",
                "akshare.option_cffex_hs300_daily_sina",
                SINA_COLUMNS,
                len(sina),
            ),
        },
        "interfaces": INTERFACES,
        "csi_source": csi_source,
        "build_stats": build_stats,
        "sample_dates": sample_dates,
        "sample_month_report": month_report,
        "sample_date_report": date_report,
        "assertions": assertions,
    }
    METADATA.write_text(json.dumps(metadata, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    return month_report, date_report


def print_report(month_report, date_report, sina, build_stats, assertions):
    month_table = Table(title="Sample months")
    month_table.add_column("Month")
    month_table.add_column("Trading days", justify="right")
    month_table.add_column("Clean rows", justify="right")
    for item in month_report:
        month_table.add_row(item["month"], str(item["trading_days"]), str(item["rows"]))
    console.print(month_table)

    date_table = Table(title="Sample dates")
    date_table.add_column("Date")
    date_table.add_column("Rows", justify="right")
    date_table.add_column("Expiries", justify="right")
    for item in date_report:
        date_table.add_row(item["date"], str(item["rows"]), str(item["expiries"]))
    console.print(date_table)

    failures = [item for item in INTERFACES if item["status"] in {"failed", "partial"}]
    interface_table = Table(title="Interface failures")
    interface_table.add_column("Interface")
    interface_table.add_column("Status")
    interface_table.add_column("Detail")
    if failures:
        for item in failures:
            interface_table.add_row(item["interface"], item["status"], item["detail"])
    else:
        interface_table.add_row("none", "-", "-")
    console.print(interface_table)

    ok = int((sina["status"] == "ok").sum()) if not sina.empty else 0
    failed = int((sina["status"] == "failed").sum()) if not sina.empty else 0
    no_match = int((sina["status"] == "no_matching_date").sum()) if not sina.empty else 0
    console.print(
        f"Sina comparison: ok={ok} failed={failed} no_matching_date={no_match} total={len(sina)}"
    )

    assertion_table = Table(title="Assertions")
    assertion_table.add_column("Check")
    assertion_table.add_column("Result")
    assertion_table.add_column("Detail")
    for item in assertions:
        assertion_table.add_row(item["name"], "PASS" if item["passed"] else "FAIL", item["detail"])
    console.print(assertion_table)

    validation = build_stats.get("expiry_validation", {})
    if validation.get("rolled") or validation.get("unverified_future"):
        flag_table = Table(title="Expiry validation")
        flag_table.add_column("Nominal")
        flag_table.add_column("Resolved")
        flag_table.add_column("Status")
        for item in validation.get("rolled", []):
            flag_table.add_row(item["nominal"], item["expiry"], "rolled_holiday")
        for expiry in validation.get("unverified_future", []):
            flag_table.add_row(expiry, expiry, "unverified_future")
        console.print(flag_table)

        "hold": "oi",
        "oi": "oi",
    }
    mapping = chinese if "日期" in frame.columns else english
    missing = [column for column in mapping if column not in frame.columns]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"futures raw missing columns: {missing}")
    out = frame[list(mapping)].rename(columns=mapping).copy()
    out["date"] = pd.to_datetime(out["date"], errors="coerce").dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    for column in FUTURES_COLUMNS[1:]:
        out[column] = pd.to_numeric(out[column], errors="coerce")
    out = out.dropna(subset=["date", "close"]).drop_duplicates("date", keep="last")
    return out.sort_values("date").reset_index(drop=True)[FUTURES_COLUMNS]


def verify_futures(code: str, frame: pd.DataFrame) -> dict:
    duplicates = int(frame.duplicated("date").sum())
    price_columns = ["open", "high", "low", "close"]
    nonpositive = int((frame[price_columns] <= 0).sum().sum())
    missing_prices = int(frame[price_columns].isna().sum().sum())
    start = pd.Timestamp(frame["date"].min())
    end = pd.Timestamp(frame["date"].max())
    span_days = int((end - start).days)
    years = span_days / 365.25
    checks = {
        "dataset": code,
        "rows": int(len(frame)),
        "start": start.date().isoformat(),
        "end": end.date().isoformat(),
        "span_days": span_days,
        "years": years,
        "duplicate_dates": duplicates,
        "nonpositive_prices": nonpositive,
        "missing_prices": missing_prices,
        "at_least_5_years": bool(years >= 5.0),
        "no_duplicate_dates": bool(duplicates == 0),
        "positive_prices": bool(nonpositive == 0 and missing_prices == 0),
    }
    return checks


def fetch_futures() -> tuple[list[tuple[str, str, pd.DataFrame]], list[dict]]:
    import akshare as ak

    RAW.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    CLEAN.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    results: list[tuple[str, str, pd.DataFrame]] = []
    assertions: list[dict] = []
    for code, symbol in FUTURES_SYMBOLS.items():
        raw_path = RAW / f"futures_{code}.csv"
        source_path = RAW / f"futures_{code}_source.txt"
        source = "cached"
        if raw_path.exists() and raw_path.stat().st_size > 0:
            if source_path.exists():
                source = source_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()
            record(f"Futures {code}", "skipped", f"using cached source={source}", str(raw_path))
            log.info("Futures %s skipped; cached source=%s", code, source)
            raw = pd.read_csv(raw_path)
        else:
            attempts = [
                (
                    "akshare.futures_main_sina",
                    lambda: ak.futures_main_sina(
                        symbol=symbol, start_date="20050101", end_date="22220101"
                    ),
                ),
                ("akshare.futures_zh_daily_sina", lambda: ak.futures_zh_daily_sina(symbol=symbol)),
            ]
            failures = []
            raw = None
            for name, call in attempts:
                try:
                    with time_limit(180):
                        frame = call()
                    if frame is None or len(frame) == 0:
                        raise ValueError("empty response")
                    frame.to_csv(raw_path, index=False, encoding="utf-8")
                    source_path.write_text(name, encoding="utf-8")
                    source = name
                    raw = frame
                    record(f"Futures {code}", "ok", f"source={name} rows={len(frame)}", str(raw_path))
                    log.info("Futures %s source used: %s (%d rows)", code, name, len(frame))
                    break
                except Exception as exc:
                    message = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
                    failures.append(f"{name}: {message}")
                    log.error("Futures %s %s failed: %s", code, name, message)
            if raw is None:
                record(f"Futures {code}", "failed", " | ".join(failures), str(raw_path))
                assertions.append(
                    {
                        "dataset": code,
                        "rows": 0,
                        "start": None,
                        "end": None,
                        "span_days": 0,
                        "years": 0.0,
                        "duplicate_dates": 0,
                        "nonpositive_prices": 0,
                        "missing_prices": 0,
                        "at_least_5_years": False,
                        "no_duplicate_dates": False,
                        "positive_prices": False,
                    }
                )
                continue
        clean = normalize_futures(raw)
        clean_path = CLEAN / f"futures_{code}.csv"
        clean.to_csv(clean_path, index=False, encoding="utf-8")
        checks = verify_futures(code, clean)
        assertions.append(checks)
        results.append((code, source, clean))
        log.info(
            "Futures %s clean rows=%d %s..%s years=%.2f",
            code,
            checks["rows"],
            checks["start"],
            checks["end"],
            checks["years"],
        )
    return results, assertions


def update_futures_metadata(results: list[tuple[str, str, pd.DataFrame]], assertions: list[dict]):
    if not METADATA.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"metadata missing: {METADATA}")
    metadata = json.loads(METADATA.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    artifacts = metadata.setdefault("artifacts", {})
    for code, source, frame in results:
        relative = f"data/clean/futures_{code}.csv"
        artifacts[relative] = build_artifact(
            ROOT / relative,
            f"Sina main continuous futures {FUTURES_SYMBOLS[code]} ({code}); interface={source}",
            source,
            FUTURES_COLUMNS,
            len(frame),
        )
    metadata["futures_assertions"] = assertions
    metadata["updated_at"] = datetime.now().astimezone().isoformat(timespec="seconds")
    METADATA.write_text(json.dumps(metadata, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")


def print_futures_report(results: list[tuple[str, str, pd.DataFrame]], assertions: list[dict]):
    table = Table(title="Q2 futures snapshots")
    table.add_column("Dataset")
    table.add_column("Source")
    table.add_column("Rows", justify="right")
    table.add_column("Start")
    table.add_column("End")
    table.add_column("Years", justify="right")
    for code, source, frame in results:
        table.add_row(
            code,
            source,
            f"{len(frame):,}",
            str(frame["date"].iloc[0]),
            str(frame["date"].iloc[-1]),
            f"{(pd.Timestamp(frame['date'].iloc[-1]) - pd.Timestamp(frame['date'].iloc[0])).days / 365.25:.2f}",
        )
    console.print(table)

    check_table = Table(title="Futures assertions")
    check_table.add_column("Dataset")
    check_table.add_column("5y")
    check_table.add_column("No duplicate dates")
    check_table.add_column("Positive prices")
    for item in assertions:
        check_table.add_row(
            item["dataset"],
            "PASS" if item["at_least_5_years"] else "FAIL",
            "PASS" if item["no_duplicate_dates"] else "FAIL",
            "PASS" if item["positive_prices"] else "FAIL",
        )
    console.print(check_table)

def futures_only():
    RAW.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    CLEAN.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    futures_results, futures_assertions = fetch_futures()

        )
    ]
    if failed:
        log.error("assertion failures: %s", failed)
        return 1
    log.info("futures fetch complete; all assertions passed")
    return 0

def configure_q3_logging():
    CACHE.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter("%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s"))

    log.info("Q3 log file: %s", log_path)
    return log_path

    profit_path = Q3_DIR / "macro_china_nbs_industrial_profit.csv"

def q3_build():
    CLEAN.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    _print_q3_raw_table()
    panel, meta, missing_rows, outliers, monthly_missing, gdp_info = build_macro_panel()
    panel.to_csv(MACRO_PANEL, index=False, encoding="utf-8", date_format="%Y-%m-%d")
    meta.to_csv(MACRO_META, index=False, encoding="utf-8")
    checks = _q3_checks(panel, meta)
    pmi = panel["pmi"]
    threshold_rows = []
    for threshold in [50.0, 49.5]:
        flag = (pmi < threshold) & (pmi.shift(1) < threshold)
        threshold_rows.append(
            {
                "threshold": threshold,
                "pmi_below_share": float((pmi < threshold).mean()),
                "regime_share": float(flag.mean()),
                "regime_months": int(flag.sum()),
            }
        )
    interfaces = INTERFACES if INTERFACES else []
    _update_q3_metadata(
        panel,
        meta,
        missing_rows,
        checks,
        monthly_missing,
        threshold_rows,
        gdp_info,
        interfaces,
    )
    _print_q3_report(
        panel,
        meta,
        missing_rows,
        outliers,
        monthly_missing,
        checks,
        gdp_info,
        interfaces,
    )
    failed = [item["name"] for item in checks if not item["passed"]]
    if failed:
        log.error("Q3 assertion failures: %s", failed)
        return 1
    log.info("Q3 macro panel built; all assertions passed")
    return 0


def q3_run():
    fetch_q3_raw()
    return q3_build()
