def q2a_rows(payloads: list[dict]) -> tuple[list[dict], list[dict], dict[str, str]]:
    rows = []
    study = []
    used = {}
    for item in payloads:
        if item["approach"] != "approach3":
            continue
        metrics = item["payload"]["metrics"]
        fit_seconds = item["payload"]["fit_seconds"]
        if item["dataset"] == "IF_study":
            convergence = metrics["convergence"]["pricing"]["asian"]
            bias = metrics["bias_variance"]["table"]["delta"]["asian"]["0.01"]
            study.append(
                {
                    "source": item["rel"],
                    "naive_slope": convergence["naive"]["slope"],
                    "control_variate_slope": convergence["control_variate"]["slope"],
                    "speedup": metrics["performance"]["speedup"],
                    "bias": bias["bias"],
                    "variance": bias["variance"],
                    "fit_seconds": fit_seconds,
                }
            )
            used[item["rel"]] = "Q2A convergence and bias-variance study"
            continue
        asian = metrics["pricing"]["asian"]
        barrier = metrics["pricing"]["barrier"]
        rows.append(
            {
                "source": item["rel"],
                "dataset": item["dataset"],
                "validation_z": metrics["validation_european"]["z"],
                "geometric_z": metrics["closed_form_checks"]["geometric_call_z"],
                "engine_z": asian["engine_agreement_z"],
                "asian_antithetic": asian["variance_ratio_vs_naive"]["antithetic"],
                "asian_control_variate": asian["variance_ratio_vs_naive"]["control_variate"],
                "asian_cv_antithetic": asian["variance_ratio_vs_naive"]["cv_antithetic"],
                "barrier_cv_antithetic": barrier["variance_ratio_vs_naive"]["cv_antithetic"],
                "passes_5x": metrics["variance_reduction_benchmark_asian"]["passes_5x"],
                "fit_seconds": fit_seconds,
            }
        )
        used[item["rel"]] = "Q2A z-scores and variance reduction"
    rows.sort(key=lambda row: float(row["asian_control_variate"]), reverse=True)
    for rank, row in enumerate(rows, start=1):
        row["rank"] = rank
    return rows, study, used


def q2b_rows(payloads: list[dict]) -> tuple[list[dict], dict[str, str]]:
    rows = []
    used = {}
    for item in payloads:
        if item["approach"] != "approach4":
            continue
        for cell in item["payload"]["metrics"]["table"]:
            rows.append(
                {
                    "source": item["rel"],
                    "method": cell["method"],
                    "rebalance": cell["rebalance_days"],
                    "policy_kappa": cell["policy_kappa_bp"],
                    "eval_kappa": cell["eval_kappa_bp"],
                    "pnl": cell["pnl"],
                    "cvar": cell["cvar_mean"],
                    "net_cvar": cell["net_cvar_mean"],
                    "net_cvar_std": cell["net_cvar_std"],
                    "variance": cell["variance_mean"],
                    "mean_pnl": cell["mean_pnl_mean"],
                    "mean_pnl_std": cell["mean_pnl_std"],
                    "turnover": cell["turnover_mean"],
                    "fit_seconds": item["payload"]["fit_seconds"],
                }
            )
        used[item["rel"]] = "Q2B CVaR, variance and expected P&L"
    rows.sort(key=lambda row: (0 if row["pnl"] == "brief" else 1, float(row["net_cvar"]), row["method"]))
    for rank, row in enumerate(rows, start=1):
        row["rank"] = rank
    return rows, used


def summary_block(block: dict) -> tuple[float, float, float, float, float, float, int | None]:
    if "Brier_mean" in block:
        return (
            block["Brier_mean"],
            block["Brier_std"],
            block["AUC_mean"],
            block["AUC_std"],
            block["accuracy_mean"],
            block["accuracy_std"],
            block.get("n"),
        )
    return (
        block["Brier"],
        0.0,
        block["AUC"],
        0.0,
        block["accuracy"],
        0.0,
        block.get("n"),
    )


def q3_rows(payloads: list[dict]) -> tuple[list[dict], dict[str, str]]:
    rows = []
    used = {}
    for item in payloads:
        metrics = item["payload"]["metrics"]
        if item["approach"] == "approach5":
            if "probit" in metrics and "test" in metrics["probit"]:
                for arm, block in metrics["probit"]["test"].items():
                    brier, brier_std, auc, auc_std, accuracy, accuracy_std, n = summary_block(block)
                    rows.append(
                        {
                            "source": item["rel"],
                            "arm": arm,
                            "vintage": "original",
                            "brier": brier,
                            "brier_std": brier_std,
                            "auc": auc,
                            "auc_std": auc_std,
                            "accuracy": accuracy,
                            "accuracy_std": accuracy_std,
                            "n": n,
                        }
                    )
            post_hoc = metrics.get("post_hoc", {})
            for block in post_hoc.get("test_table", []):
                brier, brier_std, auc, auc_std, accuracy, accuracy_std, n = summary_block(block)
                rows.append(
                    {
                        "source": item["rel"],
                        "arm": block["model"],
                        "vintage": "post_hoc",
                        "brier": brier,
                        "brier_std": brier_std,
                        "auc": auc,
                        "auc_std": auc_std,
                        "accuracy": accuracy,
                        "accuracy_std": accuracy_std,
                        "n": n,
                    }
                )
            used[item["rel"]] = "Q3 original and post_hoc probit arms"
        elif item["approach"] == "approach6":
            for arm, block in metrics.get("comparison", {}).items():
                brier, brier_std, auc, auc_std, accuracy, accuracy_std, n = summary_block(block)
                rows.append(
                    {
                        "source": item["rel"],
                        "arm": arm,
                        "vintage": "original",
                        "brier": brier,
                        "brier_std": brier_std,
                        "auc": auc,
                        "auc_std": auc_std,
                        "accuracy": accuracy,
                        "accuracy_std": accuracy_std,
                        "n": n,
                    }
                )
            retrain = metrics.get("post_hoc", {}).get("retrain", {})
            for arm, block in retrain.get("comparison", {}).items():
                brier, brier_std, auc, auc_std, accuracy, accuracy_std, n = summary_block(block)
                rows.append(
                    {
                        "source": item["rel"],
                        "arm": arm,
                        "vintage": "post_hoc",
                        "brier": brier,
                        "brier_std": brier_std,
                        "auc": auc,
                        "auc_std": auc_std,
                        "accuracy": accuracy,
                        "accuracy_std": accuracy_std,
                        "n": n,
                    }
                )
            used[item["rel"]] = "Q3 original and post_hoc LSTM/probit arms"
    rows.sort(key=lambda row: float(row["brier"]))
    for rank, row in enumerate(rows, start=1):
        row["rank"] = rank
    return rows, used


def coverage_rows(payloads: list[dict], used: dict[str, str]) -> list[list]:
    rows = []
    for item in payloads:
        rows.append(
            [
                item["rel"].removeprefix("results/").removesuffix("/metrics.json"),
                item["approach"],
                item["dataset"],
                fmt(item["payload"]["fit_seconds"], 2),
                used.get(item["rel"], "UNUSED"),
            ]
        )
    unused = [row for row in rows if row[-1] == "UNUSED"]
    if unused:
        raise ValueError(f"metrics.json files excluded silently: {unused}")
    return rows


def rich_table(title: str, columns: list[str], rows: list[list]) -> Table:
    table = Table(title=title, show_lines=False)
    for column in columns:
        table.add_column(column, overflow="fold")
    for row in rows:
        table.add_row(*[str(value) for value in row])
    return table


def make_plotly_table(section_rows: list[list[str]], header_color: str = "#1f4e79") -> go.Table:
    n_cols = len(section_rows[0])
    columns = [[row[i] for row in section_rows[1:]] for i in range(n_cols)]
    return go.Table(
        header=dict(
            values=section_rows[0],
            fill_color=header_color,
            font=dict(color="white", size=12),
            align="left",
        ),
        cells=dict(
            values=columns,
            fill_color=["#f7f9fc", "#eef2f7"],
            align="left",
            font=dict(size=11),
            height=24,
        ),
        columnwidth=[1.2] + [1.0] * (n_cols - 1),
    )


def build_html(
    coverage: list[list[str]],
    q1: list[list[str]],
    q2a: list[list[str]],
    q2a_study: list[list[str]],
    q2b: list[list[str]],
    q3: list[list[str]],
) -> go.Figure:
    sections = [
        ("Source coverage: every results/approach*/*/metrics.json", coverage),
        ("Q1: SVI vs neural repricing and violations (primary Q1B = io_scaled; io superseded)", q1),
        ("Q2A: z-scores and variance reduction (ranked by Asian control-variate ratio)", q2a),
        ("Q2A supplementary study: convergence and bias-variance", q2a_study),
        ("Q2B: CVaR, variance and expected P&L (ranked within P&L definition by net CVaR)", q2b),
        ("Q3: Brier, AUC and accuracy, original and post-hoc arms (ranked by Brier)", q3),
    ]
    counts = [max(1, len(section[1]) - 1) for section in sections]
    total = sum(counts)
    heights = [max(0.08, count / total) for count in counts]
    figure = make_subplots(
        rows=len(sections),
        cols=1,
        specs=[[{"type": "table"}] for _ in sections],
        subplot_titles=[section[0] for section in sections],
        vertical_spacing=0.035,
        row_heights=heights,
    )
    for index, section in enumerate(sections, start=1):
        figure.add_trace(make_plotly_table(section[1]), row=index, col=1)
    figure.update_layout(
        title="AP 2026 cross-approach comparison (all values read from metrics.json)",
        height=max(1800, 320 + 34 * sum(counts)),
        margin=dict(l=20, r=20, t=80, b=20),
        template="plotly_white",
    )
    figure.update_annotations(font_size=13)
    return figure


def main() -> int:
    payloads = load_all()
    used: dict[str, str] = {}
    q1, used_q1 = q1_rows(payloads)
    used.update(used_q1)
    q2a, q2a_study, used_q2a = q2a_rows(payloads)
    used.update(used_q2a)
    q2b, used_q2b = q2b_rows(payloads)
    used.update(used_q2b)
    q3, used_q3 = q3_rows(payloads)
    used.update(used_q3)
    coverage = coverage_rows(payloads, used)

ap2026-q2/report.md:682:5. **LSTM refit frequency.** Q3B refits the LSTM every six months and reuses the last refit between refits; Q3A refits the probit monthly. Source: `results/approach6/macro/metrics.json`.
ap2026-q2/report.md:683:6. **Cluster bridge.** Q3A clusters partition indicators, while the LSTM's month-level `h_t` clusters partition months, so a direct ARI is undefined. The bridge maps each indicator to a correlation vector with the 16 hidden dimensions and clusters those vectors with `k=9`; the resulting ARI may be partly mechanical because `h_t` is computed from those indicators. 219:The hedge is a European ATM call on IF with `S0=100`, `K=100`, `T=0.25`, `m=63`, `sigma=0.1911` (the Q2A five-year IF calibration) and `r=0.01417` (SHIBOR zero at `T`). The policy is a small MLP with two hidden layers of 32 units mapping `(S_t/S0, t/T)` to a delta in `[0,1]` through a sigmoid; it does not see the previous position. The objective is empirical CVaR at 0.95 of `-V_T`, the mean of the worst 5% of losses per batch. Training uses `2^17` paths, batches of `2^12`, 100 epochs, Adam at learning rate 0.005, and one policy per cost `kappa in {0,10,50}` bp. The same network initialization is used for every kappa. Validation uses three independent seeds with `2^17` paths each; training uses one seed (42).

199:## 9. Q3 Option B: LSTM and leakage
203:Q3B uses 12-month windows of the standardized aligned panel, excluding `gdp_yoy`, as input to an LSTM with at most two layers and a linear logit head. Training pairs are `(window ending s, d_{s+1})` with `s+1 <= origin t`. The loss is `BCEWithLogits` with `pos_weight = n_neg/n_pos`, and probabilities are corrected by `p_cal = sigmoid(logit - log(pos_weight))`. The walk-forward scheme is expanding, with the LSTM refit every six months while the Q3A probit refits monthly. Hyperparameters are selected on the 36-month tuning block only by mean Brier over three seeds.
205:The original run used 18-month validation blocks. The retrained model, which is the primary Q3B result, uses the chosen setting hidden 8, one layer, dropout 0.2 and weight decay `1e-2`, an expanding split with the last 36 training-pair months held out for validation, minimum 30 epochs, patience 30 and maximum 300 epochs, with three seeds. Leakage arms are the disciplined aligned panel, a zero-lag panel (`L_i=0`), a zero-lag panel with full-sample standardization, and a zero-lag probit. Leakage premiums use a circular 12-month block bootstrap with 5,000 replicates; positive means the leaked arm looks better (lower Brier or higher AUC).

## 3. Data

### 3.1 Sources, coverage and snapshots

Table 1: Committed clean artifacts in this repository. Source: `data/metadata.json`.

| artifact | source | rows | retrieved |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data/clean/options_io.csv` | CFFEX IO daily quotes; CSI 300 close from akshare.stock_zh_index_daily | 30068 | 2026-11-04 |
| `data/clean/shibor.csv` | China Shibor | 2398 | 2026-11-04 |
| `data/clean/sina_comparison.csv` | CFFEX close vs Sina option daily close | 30 | 2026-11-04 |

The raw CFFEX snapshot is committed through a `.gitignore` exception: 128 daily files, of which 126 parse. `20240917_1.csv` and `20260925_1.csv` are non-CSV 200 pages with missing columns. `data/legacy/io_settle_svi_params.csv` and `data/legacy/io_close_svi_params.csv` are committed snapshots used only for the eta-bound comparison; they have 693 fits each.

The Sina cross-check compared 30 rows in `data/clean/sina_comparison.csv`: 29 matched the CFFEX close with zero difference, and 1 failed (IO2603-P-4650). The comparison is a close-price spot check, not a full second price source.

The IF forward check uses raw CFFEX IF rows, not a main-contract series. Each of the 126 parsed files lists four IF contracts for the date. The check merges IO forwards to IF contracts by date and expiry year-month. Far IO expiries have no same-month IF contract listed, so the unmatched count is structural: 498 of 750 IO forwards match, 252 do not. This was verified in `load_cffex_futures`, which filters every IF contract from the raw file and merges on `expiry_month`, and in the raw files, which contain four IF contracts per date.

### 3.2 Q1 filtering, parity and implied volatility

Q1 uses the CFFEX `settle` field as the primary price and repeats the pipeline on `close`. There is no bid-ask snapshot, so liquidity is proxied by volume. Filters are volume >= 10, price >= 1, `|k| <= 0.20` and days-to-expiry >= 7. The volume floor stands in for a missing spread, the price floor removes near-zero quotes, the strike band keeps the fit local enough for a raw SVI slice, and the days floor avoids degenerate short tenors. On settle, sequential removals are 8,008 by volume, 1,303 by price, 1,380 by strike band and 606 by days, leaving 18,771 liquid quotes. There are 750 date-expiry groups, 728 with liquid quotes, 693 fits and 57 skipped groups (34 with fewer than six strikes, 23 with no liquid OTM quote). The OTM quote set has 11,146 quotes. Rate convention is `r(tau) = ln(1 + L/100 * tau * 365/360) / tau` from SHIBOR, linear in tenor and flat outside pillars. The forward is a volume-weighted mean of `F_K = K + (C-P)/DF` within `|ln(F_K / median(F_K))| <= 0.05`; `q = r - ln(F/S0)/T`.

## 11. Differences from the brief

1. **Butterfly formula.** The printed `g(k)` omits `w''/2`; the code uses the correct Gatheral form for decisions and reports both. On settle, raw strict violations are 8 with `w''/2` and 382 without; repaired strict violations are 1 and 390. On close, raw strict counts are 23 and 418; repaired strict counts are 3 and 423. Source: `results/approach1/io/metrics.json`, `results/approach1/io_close/metrics.json`.
2. **No bid-ask data.** Daily CFFEX data have no bid-ask spread, so volume >= 10 stands in for liquidity/spread. On settle this filter removes 8,008 quotes; the full sequential filter removes 11,297. Source: `results/approach1/io/metrics.json`.
3. **SVI eta bounds.** The current bounds are `[0.01,1.0]`, narrower than the legacy `[1e-6,2.0]`. This changes bound hits but not median RMSE materially. Source: `results/approach1/io/metrics.json`.
4. **Q1B sample date.** Q1B uses 2024-03-14, while the metadata sample date is 2024-03-15. The selection rule chooses the nearest mid-month date with at least 80% of the month's maximum quote count. Source: `results/approach2/io_scaled/metrics.json`.
5. **Individual submission.** This is an individual submission rather than a group submission.
6. **AI-drafted report.** The report was drafted by AI rather than written by a group, with instructor approval as stated by the author in Section 14.
7. **Only IO options.** Only CFFEX IO options are used for the surface; SSE ETF options are not fitted. Source: `data/metadata.json` and `results/approach1/io/metrics.json`.
8. **Parity forward.** `q` is replaced by the put-call parity forward: `q = r - ln(F/S0)/T` with `F` estimated from parity, rather than a dividend model. Source: `results/approach1/io/metrics.json`.
9. **FastboxData not used.** FastboxData was not used as a data source.

## 12. Limitations

- SVI and neural fits are audited only on the reported grids. The neural surface has 30 butterfly and 4 calendar violations on the dense grid outside its training collocation, so it must not be called globally arbitrage-free. SVI is not proved arbitrage-free off the audit grid either.
- Both models are weak in the wings and at short tenors: Q1A settle worst per-fit max repricing is 0.3251 and close is 0.2624; Q1B wing p95 is 0.7809 and max 1.519, versus SVI 0.5592.
- SVI fits frequently sit on the eta bounds (31 lower and 67 upper on settle; 72 lower and 46 upper on close), and the cause is not established.
- The Q1B per-tenor table comes from `NOTES_OPEN_ISSUES.md`, not from a committed `metrics.json`.

## 12. Limitations

- Macro data are current revised vintages, not real-time vintages. Most publication lags are conservative assumptions, not observed release dates. GDP is derived from cumulative real levels (79 derived quarters; validation maximum absolute difference 0.83 points).
- The retrained LSTM never exceeds 0.5 on the test block (maximum 0.3172) and does not beat persistence (Brier 0.2561 vs 0.2286; AUC 0.6422 vs 0.7390). Its accuracy is the all-negative rate.
- The PCA rank is chosen on 12 quarterly nowcast observations; the test block is short for regime classification, and the AUC intervals are wide (for example, the original probit minus persistence interval is `[-0.2375, 0.03518]`).
- The Q3 nowcast month-3 ex-COVID error is higher than month-1; the paired interval includes zero, and no cause is asserted.
- The Q3 clustering is unstable across windows (adjacent ARI median 0.1648) and is descriptive only.

Hao Lu

## Provenance and split disclosure

The work was done in one repository (parent tag `submission`, commit `4521da3`) and split afterwards into one repository per question following the instructor's guidance. Commit hashes changed and the old-to-new commit map is included in `SPLIT_HISTORY.md`. Dates in rewritten commits are the original ones; the split commits are dated when they were made. ## 1. Summary

The repository implements Q1 of the Advanced Programming 2026 brief, options A and B. Q1 fits an arbitrage-free implied-volatility surface to CFFEX IO options, with SVI slices (Q1A) and a neural surface (Q1B).

Q1A fits all 693 liquid date-expiry slices on the settle price and reaches zero butterfly and zero calendar violations at the 1e-8 tolerance on its audit grid, but 1 butterfly and 12 calendar checks remain strictly negative after repair. The median per-fit median repricing error is 0.77% on settle and 1.27% on close; the median per-fit maximum is 2.58% and 4.33%. Q1B is close to SVI in median repricing on the same 470 OTM quotes (0.87% vs 0.82%) but much worse in the tail (p95 12.34% vs 5.45%; maximum 98.30% vs 17.37%), and it violates arbitrage on a denser grid outside its training collocation.

What was not achieved: Q1B is not globally arbitrage-free and is not competitive with SVI in the wings. The data are daily, without bid-ask quotes.

## 1. Summary

The repository implements Q2 of the Advanced Programming 2026 brief, options A and B. Q2 prices path-dependent payoffs under GBM by Monte Carlo (Q2A) and learns a CVaR-optimal hedge (Q2B).

Q2A passes the Black-Scholes and closed-form checks; the Asian control-variate variance ratio is 308x to 1974x across four futures, above the 5x benchmark. Q2B's deep policy has lower gross and net CVaR than daily Black-Scholes hedging on the brief P&L at zero and at 50 bp cost.

What was not achieved: Q2B covers only IF and uses one training seed. The data are daily, without bid-ask quotes.

## 1. Summary

The repository implements Q3 of the Advanced Programming 2026 brief, options A and B. Q3 forecasts the PMI contraction regime with a classical probit/PCA model (Q3A) and an LSTM with leakage ablations (Q3B).

Q3A beats the expanding prior on Brier score but not persistence (AUC 0.6928 vs 0.7390), and its nowcast beats a random-walk-with-drift benchmark in all periods, including ex-COVID. Q3B does not beat persistence either; the retrained LSTM never predicts a probability above 0.5 on the test block and its test AUC is 0.6422 versus 0.7390 for persistence.

What was not achieved: Q3A and Q3B do not reach the indicative AUC target of 0.75 or beat persistence. The data are daily, without real-time macro vintages.

## 1. Summary

Q3A beats the expanding prior on Brier score but not persistence (AUC 0.6928 vs 0.7390), and its nowcast beats a random-walk-with-drift benchmark in all periods, including ex-COVID. What was not achieved: Q3A and Q3B do not reach the indicative AUC target of 0.75 or beat persistence. The data are daily, without real-time macro vintages.

# AGENTS.md

## Goal
Q2 of the Advanced Programming 2026 brief, options A and B: price path-dependent payoffs by Monte Carlo under GBM, and learn a hedge minimizing CVaR_0.95 of -V_T. Option A is the Monte Carlo engine; Option B is deep hedging.

## Environment
Python 3.13, managed with uv, dependencies pinned.
uv sync --python 3.13 && source .venv/bin/activate
./reproduce.sh --quick   # tests + compare only
./reproduce.sh           # offline data check, tests, Q2 approaches, compare
python code/check_reproduction.py

## Approach map
- approach1_q2a_mc.py: Q2A Monte Carlo pricing (formerly approach3)
- approach2_q2b_deephedge.py: Q2B deep hedging (formerly approach4)

## Data
data/clean/futures_IF.csv, futures_RB.csv, futures_CU.csv, futures_SC.csv and shibor.csv are committed snapshots. data/metadata.json is filtered to Q2 artifacts; data/fetch.py --offline verifies every checksum. Raw futures downloads are gitignored and are not part of this repository.

## Conventions
Seed: --seed 42 by default, CLI-overridable; every stochastic step is seeded.
Each code/approach*.py: argparse CLI, load -> verify -> split -> fit -> evaluate -> write.
Output: results/approachN/<dataset>/metrics.json = {params, metrics, fit_seconds, history}.
Terminal output via rich; figures via plotly HTML with include_plotlyjs=True.
Q2B reads the Q2A IF metrics for the sigma reference check; run Q2A first.

## Reproduction
`./reproduce.sh` is the full offline path; `./reproduce.sh --quick` runs tests and compare only.
`python code/check_reproduction.py` compares `.cache/clean_clone_full/results` against the committed `results`, ignores timing fields, and uses relative tolerance 1e-6.

## Provenance
This repository was split from the combined AP 2026 repository at parent tag `submission`, commit `4521da3`. See `SPLIT_HISTORY.md` for the old-to-new commit map, renamed paths and the split disclosure.

## Agent rules
Write nothing outside the repo root; tool caches stay in the repo and are gitignored.
Propose first and wait for approval before any destructive operation.
Commit after each milestone (data:, feat:, exp:, refactor:, docs:).
Never commit credentials. Never invent results: every reported number comes from a metrics.json.

</system-reminder>
